articleTitle: Leaky Wave Antenna on a Half-Mode Integrated Digitated Capacitor-based Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguide with Tilted Vertical Slots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presents a new tilted vertical slot array antenna on a half-mode integrated-digitated capacitor based corrugated substrate integrated waveguide (HM-IDC-CSIW). The half-mode waveguide is demonstrated to operate as a standard corrugated SIW. The antenna is then shown to operate at a frequency band of 30 – 40 GHz. Its performance is analyzed with change in tilt angle of the slot. The antenna is shown to have a beam-scanning range of 60° with an approximately constant gain of 14 dBi and efficiency > 80%. Such planar antennas being via-free are flexible, and hence are suitable for several conformal applications such as body area networks, telecommunications, and on-body sensing.

articleTitle: Radar-Based Digital Twins for Classification of UAVs and Avian Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, the efficacy of range-Doppler imaging is explored for the detection and classification of Unmanned Air Vehicles (UAVs), with attention to the radar system’s operating frequency and bandwidth. The investigation employs full-wave Electromagnetic (EM) CAD software to scrutinize the influence of varied radars, spanning different frequency bands, on the precision of range-Doppler images of a rotating blade. Notably, mmWave radars, distinguished by their expansive bandwidth, demonstrate superior range-Doppler accuracy compared to other examined radar systems. Building on this, a subsequent inquiry is undertaken to evaluate the performance of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms in drone classification amid the presence of avian organisms. The mmWave radar is modeled using EM CAD tools to generate diverse datasets encompassing a quadcopter UAV and avian subjects. Employing two distinct ML algorithms, the study reveals that an increased avian presence diminishes the radar’s ability to effectively detect and classify drones. The CNN model achieves 99% classification accuracy when a single bird coexists with the drone, declining to 90% in scenarios featuring a drone amidst a swarm of ten birds. We believe that our presented workflow presents a paradigm shift in how defense scientists can validate possible counter measures against illicit uses of compact drones.

articleTitle: Metallic Crack Detection Using Chipless RFID Single-bit Sensor Tag
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article yields a low-cost compact metallic crack detector RFID tag for wireless and sensing applications. The proposed chipless RFID (CRFID) tag has capability to detect cracks on metallic surfaces using pure-chip-free battery-free tag with no integrated/imbedded patch antennas. The vision is to deploy a low-cost, highly durable passive chip-free RFID tag. The tag has been analyzed for varying crack widths from 0.1mm to 3mm with metallic sheets of 30mm x 30mm and 60mm x 60mm. The tag resonates at 5.6GHz ultrahigh frequency (UHF) with a compact radius. Metallic Aluminum is deployed as a sample to be tested. Being passive in nature, the sensor tag mitigates additional battery source. The tag is a suitable choice for wireless and sensing applications in Internet of Things (IoT) and wireless sensor networks (WSN).

articleTitle: High-Gain SIW Antenna with Ridge Gap Waveguide Feed for W-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A high-gain substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) for W-band applications is designed and analyzed in this paper. The proposed antenna utilizes a well-established approach by combining SIW technology with a microstrip-based ridge gap waveguide (GWG) feed for better gain and efficiency. The integration of a novel slot on the radiating aperture, along with the ridge-based GWG feed, minimizes losses and yields efficient transmission. The proposed antenna has a boresight gain of more than 9.5 dB and an impedance bandwidth of 85-95 GHz. The combination of SIW and ridge-based GWG results in a compact, multi-layered structure that offers wider bandwidth, minimized losses, and enhanced gain. The radiation performance of the proposed antenna is authenticated through simulations using CST EM simulation software, showing over 90% radiation efficiency. For actual operating scenarios, a wideband transition structure between rectangular waveguide (RWG) and GWG is also designed. The proposed antenna design holds potential for applications requiring high-gain, wideband, and efficient radiation in W-band or millimeter wave (mmWave) communication systems.

articleTitle: Coded Metasurfaces for Two Dimensional Steering and Splitting of Incident Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of 2- bit and 1-bit digitally coded reflective metasurfaces (DCRM) for two-dimensional (2D) beam-steering and beam-splitting applications. Using MATLAB, we first calculate the phase coding information for a metasurface of size $10\lambda_{0}\times 10\lambda_{0}$ (where $\lambda_{0}$ is the free space wavelength at 5.9 GHz) to get a desired direction of reflected beam for both 1D and 2D beam steering using MATLAB, considering normally incident plane wave. Subsequently, we develop the complete metasurface structure using a full-wave solver (CST MWS) and observe the corresponding far-field scattering patterns. It is observed that the 2-bit DCRM achieves zero steering error with a half power beam width (HPBW) of $5^{o}$. Furthermore, We demonstrate the beam-splitting functionality for generating multiple beams in desired directions using a 1-bit DCRM. Moreover, we report the aperture sizes for DCRMs that achieve highly focused beam-steering with HPBW of $2^{o}$ & $3^{o}$, a directivity of 35.4 dBi & 30. 5dBi, and the SLL of −10.77 dB & −12.71 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Computational Analysis of Two-Arm Resistively Loaded Spiral Antenna for SST-1 Tokamak
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents, a resonant helical dual-arm spiral antenna, operating at 284MHz which is introduced within the context of the Steady State Superconducting Tokamak (SST-1).Through systematic analysis, the spiral antenna offers significant improvements in impedance matching. The antenna prototype radiates in both directions throughout the band with broadside gain ranging from 2.02 to 3.7dBi and a minimum reflection coefficient of -16.62 dB at 284MHz. Insights gained from these computational studies contribute to a better understanding of the antenna-plasma interaction and its impact on Tokamak performance. This work paves the way for future experimental investigations, confirming the effectiveness of the spiral antenna design and fostering advancements in fusion research.

articleTitle: Time-Modulated Metasurface for Spoofing Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a time-modulated metasurface for on-air mixing for spoofing Doppler radars. The metasurface’s impedance varies as a function of time which results in on-air mixing of the frequency of the incident wave and the modulation frequency of the metasurface generating multiple harmonics. This phenomenon can be used to trick Doppler radars as the reflected wave from the metasurface gets modulated. The design methodology and the measurement results for the metasurface, with a detailed study of the various parameters affecting the frequency mixing and test results with a radar, have been reported.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Variability Assessment Using Single Channel CW Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Heart Rate Variability (HRV) represents the variation in the interbeat interval of a heart signal and is also a reflection of the adaptability of the cardiovascular system to unexpected physiological and psychological changes. Radar-based non-contact HRV measurement can play a significant role in monitoring the health of an individual in a non-contact and unobtrusive manner. Prior research on HRV measurement mostly focused on using quadrature channel Continuous Wave (CW) radar, Frequency Modulated CW (FMCW) radar, and IR Ultra Wide Band (UWB) radar. A single-channel CW radar has a simpler architecture and fewer signal processing steps than the quadrature radar. This paper investigates the feasibility of utilizing a single-channel CW radar in ultra-short-term HRV analysis. Preliminary results showed a strong correlation of the HRV time and frequency domain metrics from the radar signal with that of an ECG signal and thus proved to be reliable in the accurate assessment of HRV.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for 6G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The exponential growth in wireless communication demands has driven the search for innovative solutions for next-generation wireless networks beyond 5G. Terahertz (THz) communications have emerged as a prime contender for facilitating ultra-high speed data transmission for the sixth-generation (6G) wireless era. To address the challenges associated with the THz signal propagation, serious path loss, and blockage vulnerability, this manuscript presents the concept of graphene-based reconfigurable intelligent surface (GRIS) as a transformative technology for enhancing THz communication in 6G systems. The surface conductivity of the GRIS unit cell element is adjusted by controlling the chemical potential (eV) of the graphene. The RIS unit cell consists of a square patch of graphene material mounted on a quartz substrate having a dielectric constant of 3.75 and loss tangent of 0.0004. The reflection coefficient amplitude (dB) and phase (degree) characteristics of the unit cell are analysed by controlling the chemical potential (0eV-2eV) in the frequency range of 1.4 THz-1.8 THz. The proposed model is insensitive to the angle of incidence and polarization. Hence unit cell is designed for both TE & TM polarizations along with different angles of incidence and has achieved almost stable reflection amplitude in the operating band.

articleTitle: High Power RF Systems of LEHIPA - Technology Development
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In RF accelerator, the high power RF system is one of the key important system that generates electric fields for beam acceleration. To ensure beam availability and accelerator safety, a reliable RF system with a highly sophisticated protection scheme is required. RF systems are complex, incorporating high-voltage and high-power subsystems in addition to RF and high current sub systems. A good amount of accelerator downtime typically comes from RF systems. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) has developed low energy high intensity proton accelerator (LEHIPA) as a front end of ADS. LEHIPA uses three 352 MHz, 1 MW klystron based high power radio frequency (RF) systems to power its three accelerating cavities. This paper, discusses the details of klystron RF system that incorporates some innovative concepts.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Coding Reconfigurable Metasurface Reflector for Millimeter Wave Communications in E-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter wave (mmWave) 1bit coding metasurface is presented. The unit cell of the metasurface consists of a modified dipole loaded with a Macom MA4AGFCP910 PIN diode, which works quite satisfactorily at E-band mmWave. The unit cell provides a $180^{\circ} \pm 30^{\circ}$ reflection phase difference between its ON and OFF states for a broad frequency range from $74-84 \mathrm{GHz}$ (12.65 %). Despite being a PCB-based design at E-band, the unit cell provides maximum reflection loss of only 2.7dB. Using such unit cell, an array of $30 \times 15$ elements is constructed with column-by-column arrangement of biasing for the PIN diodes to achieve 1-D beam steering. Furthermore, the RF is isolated from the DC on the bias lines using properly designed radial stubs. The theoretically calculated and full-wave simulated results of radiation patterns show good agreement with each other. The effect of beam squint and scan loss from the proposed broadband 1-bit coding metasurface is critically investigated. The design can find application in different mmWave communications in E-band.

articleTitle: Simplified Design Methodology for RF Dielectric Homogeneous and Graded Index Lenses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a simplified methodology to design new homogeneous and graded index (GRIN) RF dielectric lenses. The mathematical model is derived from the theory of ray optics to design 2D planar and convex lens design. The performance of these lenses is then verified in simulations with a 15 to 40 GHz WR51 waveguide probe, demonstrating a gain enhancement of approximately 15 dB and a reduced half-power beamwidth by a factor of approximately 7.5 throughout the frequency band.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband A-Sandwich Radome wall with Multilayer FSS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, an Ultra-wideband Radome wall with a multi-layered Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) structure for aircraft applications is proposed. A-sandwich structure is constructed with as the core layer and Syntactic foam applied as a skin layer for the radome. The proposed design has two core layers of along with multiple FSS layers providing a bandwidth of 14.25 GHz, starting from 7.75 GHz to 22 GHz, and a centre frequency of 14.87 GHz with sharp roll-off characteristics. The top and bottom layers of FSS have a cylindrical patch at the centre, whereas the middle layer has octagonal rings along the perimeter, reducing the inter-element spacing, which helps in angular stability and creates a coupling effect. The FSS structures provide stability for wide-angle incidence up to 30 degrees with low profile dimensions. Further, the dimensions of a design are in harmony for both TE and TM polarisation modes, showing stable results in the X and Ku bands.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual Band Dual Linear Polarized Shared Aperture Antenna for Satellite C Band Tx and Rx
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact dual-band dual-polarized shared aperture antenna is presented in this paper. In the overall structure, both upper and lower frequency bands provide dual polarizations i.e. Linear horizontal (LH) and Linear vertical (LV). The lower frequency band consists of a loop antenna realized using two vias connected horizontally and vertically. It provides high aperture efficiency and larger gain with stacking. Upper C band antenna consists of a DRA which provides higher impedance bandwidth as well as gain. The LH and LV feeding pins of DRA are connected to the transmission line through via, which are on the back side of the ground plane. This new feeding technique overcomes the cross-talk between the signals of two frequency bands. For both bands, LH and LV can be achieved on the same frequency bands. For lower band impedance bandwidth is 48MHz (3.06MHz −3.54MHz) and the gain is 10.02dB. and for upper band impedance bandwidth is 40MHz(5.78GHz-6.18GHz) and gain is 10.78dB. Isolation between both bands is better than 20 dB.

articleTitle: A CPW-fed band notch super wideband antenna with Scale up/down Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed slot super wideband (SWB) antenna with band notch characteristic is proposed. It comprises a wide rectangular slot excited by the tapered feedline. To obtain the SWB characteristic, a circular stub is added at the center of the slot. It effectively broadens the impedance bandwidth by improving the matching throughout the band. By optimizing the size and position of circular stub, the proposed antenna tenders an impedance bandwidth more than 175% with 15:1 frequency ratio (1-15 GHz). In addition, the antenna gain is improved from -2.2dBi to 6.3 dBi at 5 GHz and become almost stable in the entire frequency range. Besides, some guidelines have been prepared to scale up or down the proposed antenna structure for the desired frequency bands. To validate these design guidelines one test antenna is realized for 3 to 30 GHz frequency band. It is demonstrated that both antennas obtain more than 175% impedance bandwidth for VSWR<2. Finally, two L-shaped stubs are introduced just underneath the feed line to create band rejection between 3.1 to 4.2 GHz. It is observed that stubs efficiently reject the specific frequency band without affecting the frequency response of the proposed SWB antenna.

articleTitle: Design and development of a Ku-Band MMIC transmit receive front end chip
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a unique miniaturized single chip design solution for RF Front End of Ku-band AESA radar. The Front-End Chip (FEC) has been designed for the frequency range of 15.5 GHz to 17.5 GHz and fabricated with using 150 nm Gallium Nitride on SiC process of UMS, France. All the three functionalities i.e. Power amplifier, Low noise amplifier and Single Pole Double Throw Switch (SPDT) have been integrated in a small size of $4.5 \mathrm{~mm} \times 3.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. The fabricated TR chip has an output power of more than 37 dBm with high gain (27 dB) and efficiency (20%-28%) in the transmit chain. The FEC also has high gain (25dB) and low noise figure (less than 3.6 dB) of the receive chain. This design has been fabricated and the results have been validated by RF characterization.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Design of Low Chirp 32W Pulsed IMPATT Oscillator at W Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Pulsed IMPATT oscillator at W Band is realized having peak output power of greater than 30W. The cavity of the pulsed IMPATT oscillator is designed and simulated based on the different diode parameters provided by the diode manufacturer. MOSFET based pulsed driver bias circuit is also designed for testing the cavity. The driver circuit is capable of driving a pulsed current of 30A with a duty cycle less than one percent. An output peak power of 32W is achieved at 91.93 GHz frequency using the optimally designed cavity and pulse driver circuit. The oscillator is tested with a duty cycle of 0.3% and pulse repetition frequency of 30 KHz. Variation of output power and frequency is studied with variation of bias pin length and back short position of the designed cavity. The diameter of the bias pin is optimized to get the desired output frequency. The chirp bandwidth of the designed oscillator is optimized by varying the slope of the biasing current pulse.

articleTitle: A precision LTCC based CPWG-SL-CPWG DC-Ku band transition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) is the technology of choice for realization of high frequency Multi-Chip-Modules (MCMs). Transitions are an integral part of these MCMs providing an effective means of connecting two different types of transmission lines. This paper discusses the design and fabrication of a DC-Ku band Co-planar Waveguide with Ground (CPWG) to Stripline (SL) transition in LTCC technology. The deleterious effects of standard fabrication tolerances on transition performance are presented. Changes in screen-printing process parameters are subsequently proposed to improve achievable tolerances and thereby satisfy target specifications.

articleTitle: Dual Frequency Dual Polarized Antenna Fed by Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line for 5G Millimeter Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-frequency antenna design in Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line (SICL) technology, which exhibits dual-polarization capabilities for 5G mmWave application. A folded patch is designed using metallic post connected to both top and middle layer in the top substrate of SICL. The surface current and radiation patterns are analyzed to provide confirmation of both linear and circular polarization in the proposed antenna. To have broadside radiation, the bottom ground layer of the SICL is extended. The classical printed half-wavelength dipole antenna is designed at 28 GHz by feeding one dipole arm from the top layer and the other arm by the middle layer of the SICL. The novel antenna formed by the proposed co-located dipole and folded patch in this study exhibits a dual-frequency operation at 26.1 GHz and 29.85 GHz respectively. The designed antenna demonstrates linearly polarized unidirectional broadside beam with a gain of 6.5 dBi at first operating frequency 26.1 GHz and 3.2 dBic broadside LHCP gain at second operating frequency 28.95 GHz. This study showcases the efficacy of SICL in design of the proposed antenna and its feeding network, enabling simultaneous dual-frequency dual-polarized operation, rendering it well-suited for mmWave applications.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Dielectric Meta-Lens Antenna for Millimeter-Wave 5G Base-Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a compact 3D-printed dielectric meta-lens (DML) antenna intended for ultra-wideband operation in the millimeter-wave frequency range. Initially, cylindrical shaped dielectric unit cells having periodicity of $0.28 \lambda_{0}$ (where, $\lambda_{0}$ is the free-space wavelength at the design frequency i.e. 28 GHz) is designed. Next, the DML structure is crafted by arranging the unit cells in an array of $20 \times 20$ according to the phase distribution required on the lens aperture resulting in an aperture size of $5.6 \lambda_{0} \times 5.6 \lambda_{0}$. The complete DML antenna setup includes a dielectric horn antenna (DHA) positioned at a separation distance of 52 mm from the proposed DML, oriented along the -z-direction held in place with the help of a 3D-printed support structure. Once the DML antenna is fabricated it is assessed for its performance in an anechoic chamber. The experimental results indicate that the antenna attains a maximum measured gain of 23.9 dBi at 28 GHz, signifying a substantial gain enhancement of 9 dB. The measured 3-dB gain bandwidth of 34.4 % is achieved for the proposed DML antenna. Furthermore, the antenna demonstrates an impressive maximum aperture efficiency of 92 %.

articleTitle: Circular Ring Microwave Applicator for Superficial Hyperthermia Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the design of a circular ring applicator operating at a frequency of 434 MHz for superficial hyperthermia treatment of cancer. Simulation study is carried out on a homogeneous model to optimize the parameters of antenna design. The proposed antenna has a bandwidth of 26 MHz at −10 dB, power coupling > 90%, and a penetration depth of 13.67 mm. The specific absorption rate (SAR) of the proposed antenna on homogenous tissue at 5mm depth is 417 W/kg, which is higher compared to other applicators reported in the literature. The performance of the designed antenna is evaluated using a heterogeneous model that is developed from the patient image data. The assessment on the patient derived model indicates that the proposed applicator can be used for hyperthermia treatment of cancer.

articleTitle: Kalman Filter for Precise Altitude Estimation in FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Autonomous navigation is utilized in interplanetary landing missions to guide spacecraft towards specific destinations. For successful and soft landings, accurate altitude information is crucial. Radar altimeters are extensively employed in these missions to measure and determine precise altitudes. The Ka-band FMCW radar altimeter developed at SAC, ISRO will be used during upcoming landing mission [1]. This system is designed with a wide beam width, allowing it to measure the vertical distance to the ground (along nadir) accurately, even when the mounting platform experiences significant roll and pitch variations. However, the wide beam width results in the beam intercepting a large ground area. This means that any changes in the intercepted area can introduce variations in the characteristics of the return signal, posing challenges for precise altitude estimation. To mitigate the problem, a Kalman filter is designed and implemented. The system was then subjected to rigorous testing aboard a helicopter over different terrains. This paper discusses the filter design and the test results.

articleTitle: Design of InGaAs pHEMT process based Low Noise & Medium power C band MMIC Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of InGaAs pHEMT process based miniaturized 3 X 3 mm$^{2}$ 16 pin QFN package monolithic microwave integrated circuit with minimal noise and medium power amplifier for C band application. The simulated and experimental results are shown in this paper. This is a two stage self-biased common source single supply amplifier with 18 dB gain, 1.3 dB typical noise figure and 15 dBm of minimum OP1 dB. This design has integrated DC blocking capacitors at the input and output as part of matching circuit. 3 V single supply with a minimal power consumption of 177 mW. It is a plastic over mold QFN package.

articleTitle: Development of Hi-Rel Ka-Band Multipack Downconverter assembly for High Throughput Satellite
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports the development of Hi-Rel Ka-Band multipack down converter assembly for High throughput satellite (HTS). Multipack assembly consist of Main and Redundant Reference oscillator, Dual redundant Local Oscillator (LO) & four nos. of dual Down Converters. Dual Downconverter unit is realized using latest MMIC technology for excellent broadband electrical performance while exhibiting smallest dimension & mass. Modular design of downconverter with the use of external LO allows it to be reconfigured for different frequency plans. LO section is realized using successive multiplier chain approach & Single mechanical housed both main & redundant LO.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection with Flower Shaped Monopole Antennas utilizing Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The present study involves the construction of a flower-shaped patch with a ring structure in the ground plane using for Microwave Head Imaging (MHI). The structure that is constructed exhibits an operational frequency range spanning from 1.62 to 11.87 GHz, with a matching performance that exceeds 10 dB. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 5.48 dBi while operating at a frequency of 7.4 GHz. The evaluation of the impact of the antenna on the human head involves the examination of the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of the planned antenna. The process involves the creastion of a head model consisting of seven distinct layers. The assessment of Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is conducted by activating various antennas in a multistatic configuration. All the performance characteristics of the proposed structure were carefully examined from the simulator.

articleTitle: GaN HEMT-based Wideband Power Amplifier Integrated Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A GaN HEMT-based wideband Power Amplifier Integrated Antenna (PAIA) is presented in this work. The wideband power amplifier (PA) is designed from 0.9 to 1.3 GHz at an input power of 20 dBm giving 36.5 to 38 dBm of output power and power-added efficiency (PAE) is 52 to 62 %. It is then integrated with a slotted antenna which provides 36.2 to 39.5 dBm of output power and a PAE of 50 to 63 %. To improve the performance of the PAIA, the PA is further modified which provides 38.5 to 40.5 dBm output power and PAE of 52 to 65 %. The gain is more than 17 to 20 dB over the entire operating band. Modified integrated design provides better performance and makes it suitable for modern wireless communication system

articleTitle: Exploiting Time Domain Monostatic Backscatter Measurements for Gain Determination
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A simplified method for estimating antenna gain from monostatic backscattering measurements is proposed in this paper. It is a straightforward and effective time domain approach that exploits the radar range equation and scattering parameters in the presence of a target with a known radar cross-section. This technique is unique in that no other antenna is required besides the one being tested. Furthermore, by exploiting time gating, it is shown that measurements may be performed in the near-field, allowing for a compact setup. The technique was successfully applied to determine the gain of an impulse radiating antenna. Comparison of the measured results to simulated data showed good agreement, with a standard deviation of 0.72 dB in the frequency range from 700 MHz to 3.08 GHz.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Design of Frequency Selective Absorber for S, C and X bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a study for realizing a miniaturized frequency selective absorber (FSA) capable of wide performance in S, C, and X bands is presented. The proposed absorber consists of a resistive layer on which a hexagonal shaped ring resonator and lumped resistors mounted rectangular strips are printed. A wide range of absorption is achieved in the proposed study with 90% bandwidth ranging from 2.9 to 11.2 GHz, along with the miniaturized unit dimension of $0.074 \lambda \mathrm{L}$ (where $\lambda_{L}$ is associated with the lowest absorption frequency). The proposed structure is a 2-layer design comprising of 4 lumped elements per unit cell and a thickness of $0.079 \lambda_{L}$. The absorption process is thoroughly investigated through comprehensive parametric analysis.

articleTitle: Realisation Aspects of SWaP Optimised RF Front End Using Multi-Function Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The basic building blocks of Microwave Superheterodyne Receiver for Electronic Warfare (EW) are frequency conversion mixers, filters and amplifiers. Mixers are integrated in between tunable filter and highly selective filter for achieving the required sensitivity, image rejection, spurious suppression and selectivity. Small-size and high-performance devices are necessary to improve the functionality of system in light weight platforms. Switch Filter Bank (SFB) based tunable filters are used in multi octave microwave receivers for EW application. Most of the size of the receiver is occupied by the SFBs. This paper discusses about the SFB, which has been realised in a compact size using SWaP (Size Weight and Power) optimised Multi- Function Modules (MFM) using reduced ground discontinuity and improved flatness in the frequency response.

articleTitle: Multimode OAM Beams Generation using Concentric UCA for Future Large-Capacity Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The unique phase distribution characteristics in the radio beams carrying Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) can be utilized to build large-capacity future wireless communication systems. In this paper, the concentric Uniform Circular Array (UCA) comprising three circular arrays of identical rectangular patches for generating multimode OAM beams is presented, which can certainly be utilized to improve the data rate and spectrum efficiency in future wireless communication systems. The array is designed to operate at 5 GHz Wi-Fi applications for short-distance communication. It can transmit 0, ±1, ±2, and ±3 OAM modes simultaneously in free space with a realized gain of 9.3 dB, 10dB, 11.6dB, and 12 dB, respectively. Because of the inherited orthogonality property in the various OAM modes, these OAM modes can be used in spatial multiplexing with good isolation between the adjacent modes.

articleTitle: An UltraWideband Full Flexible 4 Elements DGS Based MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a compact wearable quad element MIMO antenna is presented operating at 4.5 GHz for 5G n77, n78, and n79 bands with the use of polyester substrate with a size of 80 $\times$ 82 $\times$ 0.4 mm3. Here T-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) technique has been utilized to improve the impedance bandwidth along with the reduction of the mutual coupling between the radiating elements. The antenna is evaluated in terms of reflection coefficient, gain, efficiency, and radiation pattern. The proposed MIMO antenna attained a maximum simulated gain of 4.3 dBi, and an efficiency of 96 % in the resonating band.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Direction of Arrival Using RFSoC Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a method for efficient hardware implementation of direction of arrival (DoA) estimation using Zynq UltraScale+ Radio Frequency System on Chip (RFSoC) ZCU216 Evaluation board. The RFSoC contains 4 ADC tiles, each with different phase lock loops (PLL) and clock signals, leading to random phase shifts between the receivers. Multi Tile Synchronization and Calibration of ADCs are incorporated before receiving RF signals from the antenna array to estimate the accurate DoA. The Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm is used to estimate the DoA, which has high resolution but has more computational complexity. To account for this, this paper presents a method to reduce the number of iterations for calculating the peak of the spectrum function using the MUSIC algorithm. To validate this, an image is transmitted as an LTE signal and received using a $1 \times 4$ linear antenna array. The DoA measurement is performed in the anechoic chamber, and measurements show that the direction of received signals can be predicted accurately using this DoA estimation method.

articleTitle: A Pentaband Hexagonal Split Ring Resonator with Defected Ground Structured 2-port MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a pentaband hexagonal split ring resonator (SRR) in configuration with defected ground structured of 2 port MIMO antenna. Five resonating modes are achieved at 6.16GHz, 10.52GHz, 12.70GHz, 17.55GHz and 21.40GHz which includes Ka band frequencies (3-30GHz). The proposed antenna is designed in TM 11 mode and the feeding technique used is microstrip line. At fifth resonating frequency i.e. 21.40GHz, 10db impedance bandwidth is (21.11-21.92) GHz which shows promising peak gain of 8.58 dB. Also the diversity performance parameters for MIMO antenna such as diversity gain (DG) is measured >9.999996 and Envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is measured <0.0011 with isolation of −25dB. The overall antenna dimension is $40^{\times}36\mathrm{mm}2$ throughout these measurements

articleTitle: A Meandered T-Slot Incorporated Patch Antenna for Microwave Thorax Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A meandered T-shaped patch antenna is designed for microwave thorax monitoring & is operational at 4GHz with a small size of 12mm x 18mm, which is appropriate for wearable devices. The dielectric loss tangent of 0.0013 and permittivity of 3 are features of the Rogers RO3003 substrate on which the antenna is designed. To obtain the required resonance frequency, meandering branches are used. One antenna serves as the transmitter while the other serves as the receiver. The most obvious signs of many conditions falling under the category of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), such as heart failure and lung carcinoma, are pulmonary oedema and pleural effusion, which are accumulations of fluid-mostly with a high-water content-in or around the lungs. One among the most effective methods of initial identification of CVDs is to monitor fluid levels inside the lungs. So, the prospective antenna is designed with a small size, as it can be used as a first-decision -making tool to pinpoint the precise cause of the oedema. The suggested antenna has a gain of 2.6 dBi & a maximum return loss of 15.9dB at 4GHz.

articleTitle: RCS Analysis of Chaff Dipoles in Microwave Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Chaffs serve as defensive countermeasures deployed on military aircraft to increase their likelihood of evading detection or attack by hostile air defense systems. Chaff consists of small fibers that reflect radar signals, which dispensed in large quantities from aircraft, form a cloud that temporarily hides the aircraft from radar detection. In this paper, monostatic RCS performance studies were carried out for metallic dipoles from S to Ku band $(2-18 \mathrm{GHz})$ Frequency. Simulations have been carried out by full-wave software ANSYS HFSS.

articleTitle: Design of a THz Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna for Space Based Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a Fabry-Perot Cavity (FPC) antenna for Tera-Hertz (THz) applications. The proposed antenna is a three layer metallic structure consisting of a matching layer, a cavity layer, and a Partially Reflecting Surface (PRS) layer. The antenna is linearly polarized, has a common BW of 18 GHz, and provides a peak gain of 18.2 dBi at 308 GHz. It can be assembled above WR 2.8 VNAX waveguide adapter easily. This antenna can find applications in high data rate space communications such as surface communication among various scientific instruments on planetary surfaces, crew module of manned space missions, and also in terrestrial 6G wireless communication.

articleTitle: Design of pHEMT based MMIC frequency multiplier with On-Chip ESD Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An active pHEMT based frequency doubler is designed using 0. 13umGaAs MMIC process with integrated On-Chip ESD protection circuitry. All GaAs integrated circuits are sensitive to ESD damage. Failures are typically seen at voltage range between 140V and 300V (HBM-Human Body Model). Hence it was required to introduce design modifications and additional circuitry to improve immunity against ESD damage. The designed frequency doubler operates at X Band (9.5GHz-l0.5GHz) to provide an output at K Band (19GHz21GHz) with output power of l0dB. The diode network used in design provides a practical protection for gate terminals of FET, easily exceeding 1000V(HBM). The design is optimized such that the additional circuitry doesn’t compromise performance or size of the design.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band 195.3 dB Peak FoM LCVCO using Bulk-CMOS high-Q Inductor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A peak FoM Ku-band LCVCO designed in a high resistivity 130nm bulk-CMOS process is presented. It is found that the center-tapped inductor with two top-level thick metals on a high resistivity substrate significantly improves the oscillator phase noise. The prototype uses PMOS cross-coupled pair with voltage biasing through the inductor to minimize noise from the bias resistor. The phase noise mechanism of the center-tapped inductor is analyzed, and an optimum inductor and varactor are selected to lessen phase noise and improve the tuning range respectively. This is demonstrated by the post-layout simulation results. VCO provides a wide tuning range from 15.6 to 16.6GHz and excellent phase noise of −120.56 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset when operating at 16.6GHz. The VCO core uses 5.1mA of current from a 1.8V supply and attains a figure of merit of 195.3dB. The peak FoM is achieved without using any tail filters. The designed LCVCO has a compact core size of $0.12mm^{2}$ only.

articleTitle: Design of Generalized Symmetric Doherty Power Amplifier with Device Parasitics Compensation for 5G Wireless Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The symmetric Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) with extended output power back-off (OPBO) for 5G applications is investigated in this article. The problems experienced in the actual design phase when the design involves a high frequency and power, including device non-idealities, are examined. A parasitic compensation technique addresses the DPA issues, such as RF current leakage from the main to the auxiliary (when the aux $P A$ is not open ideally). In addition, considering the device parasitic along with the load combiner design directly matches the optimum loads $\left(R_{\text {opt} }\right.$) at saturation and $2 R_{\text {opt} }$ at back-off, omitting the design requirement of the output matching network. For the verification, A $47-\mathrm{dBm}$ peak power, DPA with $8 \mathrm{~dB}$ OPBO, operating from $3.3 \mathrm{GHz}-3.7 \mathrm{GHz}$ is designed using CG2H40025F GaN devices. Good understanding is observed between the simulated and measured results. The DPA design shows $65-75 \%$ Drain Efficiency (DE) at saturation ($\gt47$ dBm) and $45-47 \% \mathrm{DE}$ at 8 -dB back-off output power. From the author’s knowledge, this device will be a potential candidate for small base station applications.

articleTitle: Transparent Binomially Tapered Series-Fed Patch Array With Circular Polarization for Space Surveillance and Tracking MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, design of a two transmitter four receiver (2TX-4Rx) MIMO Radar consists with optically transparent binomially tapered series fed patch (BT-SFP) antenna placed above the solar cell is proposed. First, circular polarization (CP) is imposed on the BT-SFP to make its operation space-compatible. Furthermore, the effect of the solar cell on the CP behaviour is critically examined. The proposed antenna provide gain of 9.74 dBic with wide CP beamwidth of 95° and low side lobes. The obtained −10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW) is 532 MHz and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) is 57 MHz, which makes the proposed Radar deployable on a small cubesat for on-board space-surveillance and tracking (SST) applications.

articleTitle: Design Proposal for Wide Scan Energy Efficient Concentric Ring Phased Array Antennas Using Penrose Tessellations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a design concept for irregularly subarrayed concentric rings antenna arrays (CRA) for phased array applications using Penrose tessellations. It offers a wide scan volume along with energy conservation due to reduction in the number of feeding transmit-receive modules (TRMs). The concept offers a similar sidelobe envelope as fully fed CRA with each element being fed by a TRM with a comparable directivity and angular resolution.

articleTitle: Wide Swath full Polarimetric SAR: Limitations & Techniques to Overcome
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Polarimetric SAR datasets are used by researchers in various target interpretation and classification studies. The scattering mechanism of any given target can be completely characterized by Full/Quad Polarimetric SAR datasets hence making it a specific requirement for various applications. For polarimetric analysis on a large scale, researchers require wide-swath polarimetric datasets. EOS-04 (Earth Observation Satellite-04) is the first spaceborne satellite capable of providing full polarimetric datasets with a swath of up to 168km in ScanSAR mode. However, full polarimetric acquisitions in EOS-04 are with certain limitations like azimuth resolution and incidence angle. Various ways to overcome these limitations are discussed in this paper which can be the guiding factors for future full polarimetric SARs.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Annular Ring Shorted Logarithmic Spiral Antenna offers Decade Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel antenna in which the logarithmic spiral antenna (LSA) is shorted with an annular ring has been proposed. The electrical performance in terms of transmission and radiation characteristics of the proposed antenna is analyzed. A prototype is fabricated and characterized to establish concurrence between the qualitative analysis and experimental results. The proposed LSA has an impedance bandwidth of 0.4-4GHz for VSWR better than 2.5 and gain bandwidth of 0.6-4GHz for gain better than 3 dBi. An excellent correlation is observed between the simulation and measured results.

articleTitle: Wideband high gain metasurface-based circularly polarized patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A metasurface-based circularly polarised (CP) microstrip patch antenna has been proposed in this paper. A square microstrip patch combined with plus- and diagonal-shaped slots have been used as the host antenna designed on a FR-4 substrate. The metasurface comprising a $4 \times 4$ square array has been designed on another FR-4 substrate with identical dimensions acting as a superstrate layer and separated by a layer of Teflon from the original patch. The proposed antenna offers a 10-dB impedance bandwidth over the frequency range of 5.37 GHz and 7.44 GHz. The axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of the proposed antenna lies between 6.02 GHz and 6.35 GHz. The maximum realized gain of 6.3 dBic in the 5.37 GHz to 6.35 has been achieved using the antenna and the antenna has been found to be right handed CP (RHCP) in nature. The proposed CP antenna can be deployed for applications like satellite communication, weather radar system etc.

articleTitle: A Five-Element MIMO Antenna Based on Wideband Triple-Resonance SIW Antenna for Vehicular Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presents a wideband triple-resonance substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) rectangular ring slot (RRS) antenna. Three different modes, i.e., half-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> cavity mode, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">020</inf> patch modes, are excited and merged in the cavity to achieve the wideband triple-resonance performance. The radiation principle of the antenna with its field distributions is also explained. Further, a parametric study is performed to understand the effect of the dimensional parameters of the proposed antenna. Finally, a five-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna has been proposed by arranging the presented single-element antenna in a cubical configuration having five faces. The antenna element achieves 25.95% bandwidth, 7 dBi peak gain, and the total and radiation efficiencies above 85.4% and 92.2%, respectively. The MIMO antenna achieves 26.76% bandwidth, with port-to-port isolation being higher than 25 dB and the envelope correlation coefficient < 0.002 within the operating bandwidth. Also, the peak gain of the MIMO elements is about 7 dBi.

articleTitle: Novel Metamaterial Inspired SSP-WGM Resonator Based Highly Sensitive EM Biosensor for Noninvasive Measurement of Blood Glucose Using Aqueous Glucose Solution and Saliva
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) based metamaterial-inspired electromagnetic (EM) biosensor for non-invasive diabetes analysis. The sensor design incorporates a spoof surface whispering gallery mode (SS-WGM) resonator, which effectively localizes the electric field within a specific region due to its slow-wave propagation. To achieve optimal sensitivity, a PDMS microfluidic channel is utilized to hold the sample (SUT) precisely on the region of maximum EM field concentration. Two different non-invasive samples, aqua solution mimicking blood, and human saliva, are used for evaluation. The comprehensive analysis reveals that this proposed microwave sensor holds great potential in advancing the development of modern lab-on-chip systems based on microwave technology.

Author Keywords: Spoof Surface Plasmonic Whispering Gallery Mode (SSP-WGM)

articleTitle: Design of FSS Based RF Energy Harvesting System With Near Unity Absorption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, an FSS based energy harvesting system with near unity absorption and operating at 2.2 GHz is proposed. The unit cell of the structure is based on the T-shaped resonator connected with square ring. The unit cell is analyzed numerically using the CST Microwave Studio. The designed FSS captures 99.98% of the incident power. The resistive load of the unit cell is 100 $\Omega$. The size of the unit cell is 25.4 mm $\times$ 25.4 mm, and it is fabricated on a low cost FR4 substrate. The corresponding rectifier is designed using the Villard voltage doubler topology. Open and short stubs are used for the designing of matching circuit. The designed rectifier achieves the maximum efficiency of 62% at 8 dBm input power. The 7$\times$7 unit cell structure is fabricated and integrated with the designed rectifier for the estimate of the received RF and DC power. The measured Rad-to-RF and RF-to-DC efficiency is 31.66% and 34.79% respectively.

articleTitle: SWaP-CR Optimized L-Band High Power Dual Channel TRM With Extended Pulse Width
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In active electronic scanning array (AESA) radars, Transmit/Receive module (TRM) is the most critical component, which dictates the performance and reliability of AESA. The figure-of-merits of TRM are peak transmit (Tx) output power, pulse width (PW), duty cycle (Duty) and receive (Rx) noise figure (NF) which dictate radar system performance; whereas size, weight, power, cost and reliability (SWaP-CR) as well as efficiency of TRM governs cooling load, dc power requirements and volume of active array antenna unit (AAAU) of AESA radars. This paper presents gallium nitride on silicon (GaN-on-Si) power transistor based dual channel TRM (DTRM), which operates upto 2ms PW and max. 20% Duty with min. 50% efficiency ($\eta$) and delivers 400W peak power per channel with power droop<1dB over 200MHz bandwidth in L-band, having max. dimension of $215\times 105\times 62$ (in mm), simultaneously achieving SWaP-CR. Since design is targeted for application which needs large quantity of DTRMs, it is robust enough to incorporate all the tolerances associated with component, manufacturing, process and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low profile Metasurface based Folded Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this present work, a wideband folded transmitarray (FTA) antenna has been proposed by using a low-profile metasurface (MS) array. The FTA is composed of a transmitarray (TA) based on four distinct meta-atoms (MAs) yielding mutual phase difference of 90° and a host reflect array (RA) to operate over the range 10 GHz to 15 GHz. The TAs have been realized incorporating 45° rotated cross dipoles with square ring corner cut designed on the F4B substrate while the other two layers of the substrate are metallized with orthogonal alignment. Similarly, the RAs has been designed by using a dipole with 45° rotation. An open-ended waveguide (OW) is used as a feeder for the FTA antenna which is placed in the center of the RA. The proposed FTA exhibits peak realized gain of 19.23 dBi with an aperture efficiency of 38.5% together with a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 40% referred to its center frequency of 12.5 GHz. The design is potentially used in radar, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), satellite communication, and radio astronomy.

articleTitle: Design of Couplers incorporating fabrication limitations for Helix TWT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Input and Output couplers have been designed for Ka band 130 W helix Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) with return loss better than -20 dB throughout the frequency band of 17.7 GHz to 19.7 GHz. The fabrication limitations surrounding the junction of first helix turn and the RF window and the impact of such limitations on return loss have been presented. Re-design of SMA connector in input section and the door knob structure in output section of TWT for obtaining optimum return loss has been done by modifying the simulation model to include these limitations. The observed simulated and measured results are in good agreement. The design simulations have been carried out in CST.

articleTitle: Design of an Annular Slot Loaded Circularly Polarized Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, we present a unique and innovative design for a reconfigurable patch antenna with circular polarization. The antenna configuration we propose features a square patch with two square slots placed vertically and four annular slots positioned at each corner. By regulating the operating conditions of the four diodes integrated into the antenna, a seamless shift from right-hand circular polarization to left-hand circular polarization, and vice versa, can be effectively attained. Through extensive simulations conducted using the CST Simulator platform, it has been observed that the reconfigurable antenna offers a substantial operational bandwidth in both states of polarization. The antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth (S$_{11} \lt -$10dB) of 8.68% (13.16 GHz to 14.35 GHz) and a 2.33% bandwidth (13.55 GHz to 13.87 GHz) for axial ratio, with a 3 dB threshold. Furthermore, the designed antenna achieves a maximum gain of 6.7dBi along the bore sight direction. Its compact form, high gain over a wide frequency spectrum, and the ability to reconfigure make it highly suitable for Ku band utilization.

articleTitle: A dual-band notched UWB antenna with a slot and a parasitic resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An ultra-wideband monopole antenna with dual-band notches is presented in this paper. A square slot is introduced on the upper edge of ground plane to improve the impedance bandwidth performance. The -10 dB impedance bandwidth is realized for UWB antenna ranges from 2.2 GHz to 15 GHz. The dual-band notches are realized with a U-shaped slot etched in monopole antenna for Wi-MAX band and a U-shaped parasitic resonator integrated on back side of the substrate for WLAN band. The notch bands achieved in two frequency bands from 3.1 GHz to 3.9 GHz and 4.6 GHz to 6.2 GHz. The proposed antenna is successfully simulated and provides good impedance bandwidth and stable gain over the UWB band.

articleTitle: Classification of Targets Using Time-Frequency Analysis of GPR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a potential method in demining techniques due to its capacity to identify plastic and metal-cased antipersonnel landmines. However, detecting landmines with GPR is difficult because other subsurface reflectors, such as stones, or metallic debris, can interfere with the detection process. This paper analyzes and evaluates a target discrimination approach on both synthetic and measurement data. It is based on significant features collected from the time-frequency domain of 1-D GPR signals using the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and the Wigner Ville distribution (WVD). These extracted features are then fed into the Neural Network (NN) classifier for effective classification. The proposed algorithm is evaluated using radar data gathered in controlled laboratory settings utilizing stepped frequency continuous wave (SFCW) GPR. The outcomes and performance metrics of this experimentation showcase the efficacy and potential of the developed approach in landmine detection and discrimination.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Enhanced Compact ENG Metamaterial Antenna for WLAN and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and bandwidth-enhanced metamaterial antenna is presented. The proposed antenna is designed by embedding a two-unit cell epsilon-negative transmission line (ENG-TL) on an FR4 epoxy substrate with thickness of1.6 mm. A coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed is used as the hosting transmission line to facilitate a via-less design. The bandwidth is improved by merging the zeroth-order resonance (ZOR) and first positive-order resonance (FPOR) of the ENG-TL with feed patch’s resonance with proper frequency spacing. The antenna miniaturization is achieved through the ZOR excited in the ENG-TL. The CPW feed allows very less fields to be confined within the dielectric substrate and facilitates more fields to be radiated out in air which improves the radiation efficiency. The simulated results show -10dB fractional bandwidth of 81.40% (5.15-12.22 GHz), peak radiation efficiency of 86.80% and a peak realized gain of 2.23 dB. The proposed antenna has a compact footprint of 0.23$\lambda_{0}$x0.25kx0.02k at 5.15 GHz. It can be used for WLAN (5.15-5.85 GHz) and X-band (8-12 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: IN-SILICO non-invasive glucose monitoring using patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study compares single and double patch antennas operating at 2.4504 GHz and 2.4508 GHz. The single patch antenna shows good impedance matching (-48.28 dB) and higher gain (7.004 dBi). The double patch antenna has S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>= - 39.35 dB but slightly reduced gain (4.198 dBi). Both antennas exhibit alterations in near-field electric and magnetic fields in double patch configuration. The double patch’s efficiency is 0.46 (46%), lower than the single patch’s 0.906 (90.6%). Consideration of these findings aids in selecting the suitable antenna for specific application needs. Furthermore, we present a sensitivity analysis of antenna performance in the presence of a lateral forearm model representing human tissue with varying dielectric properties of blood. Two scenarios were considered: the hand model placed at 5 mm from the antennas and in direct contact with the antennas. Parametric sweep simulations were performed for the dielectric constant (ε) of blood with six values: 58.264, 62.264, 66.264, 70.264, 74.264, and 78.264. S-parameter results, specifically S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>, were analyzed to understand the impact of blood dielectric constant on antenna behavior.

articleTitle: Indigenous Development of 15kW RF Power Amplifier for 1.5T MRI Scanner
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: RF Power Amplifier is an important sub-system of any MRI scanner. It essentially excites the protons to a high energy state. For imaging purpose hydrogen nucleus, a single proton plays a vital role in imaging due to its abundance in water and fat. The signal captured during the transitions from excited state to low energy state is processed in the spectrometer for image formation. The high power RF amplifier for Indian MRI has been designed and developed at 63.87 MHz. This paper primarily focuses on the indigenous development of solid state 15 kW RF pulse amplifier. The RF power amplifier along with necessary monitoring and interlock circuits has been integrated successfully in the system and images were obtained from integrated Indian MRI.

articleTitle: 6 Watt Power Amplifier Design and Analysis For S and C Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses the process of designing a broad-bandwidth (BBW) 6-watt power amplifier (PA) using Keysight’s Advanced Design System (ADS). This PA design makes use of a non-linear version of a gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) manufactured by Wolfspeed, the CGH40006P. PA can function within a frequency range of 3.0 to 4.6 GHz, with a central frequency of 4.0 GHz. A new method called ideal matching is used to find the input and output load impedance, along with a load-pull analysis. This helps the designed PA achieve a power added and drain efficiency of better than 50% over the frequency range of 3 to 4.6 GHz, with an output power of more than 37.78 dBm and a large signal gain (LSG) of 6 dB. The input and output matching networks have all been realised using Roger’s 4350B substrate. This PA input and output matching network has been designed with the novel approach of keeping Q value less than unity in the Smith chart utility tool available in ADS, so that the designed PA achieves a fractional bandwidth of 40%. The main use of this PA is for the radars, which can operate in the S and C band frequency ranges.

articleTitle: W-Band Broadband Single Balanced Waveguide Mixer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of a broadband mixer at W-band using Schottky-barrier chip diodes in single balanced configuration. The mixer has been designed with rectangular waveguide and suspended stripline transmission line media on 0.127 mm Rogers RT duroid substrate. EDA tools like HFSS and ADS are used to optimize the performance of the mixer circuit. The mixer operates over radio frequency (RF) bandwidth (92 to 102 GHz) with local oscillator (LO) frequency at 91 GHz and it works in downconversion mode. Simulated conversion loss is less than 10 dB over 10.3 percent RF bandwidth for 10 dBm of LO power and measured conversion loss is less than 13 dB for 11 dBm LO power. Measured LO to RF isolation is greater than 35 dB.

articleTitle: Applying Neural Network for Extending Cavity Perturbation: Extraction of Complex Permittivity in Non-Linear Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: To ensure precise modeling and simulation of microwave circuits and devices using CAD tools, it is essential to have a thorough knowledge of the dielectric properties of microwave substrates. However, in nonlinear regions, inaccurate characterization can occur as electromagnetic perturbation assumptions get invalid. The paper presents a novel neural network (NN) model, for accurately characterizing the dielectric materials’ properties under nonlinear region: the relative permittivity and loss tangent using a cylindrical cavity resonator operating in TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf> mode. The proposed technique provides a complete characterization of the dielectric sample in both conventional (linear) and extended (non-linear) regions of the cavity perturbation. The NN model underwent training utilizing Levenberg Marquardt algorithm with a comprehensive dataset of approximately 4 million samples containing resonant frequency, quality factor, 3-dB bandwidth, insertion loss, reflection loss. This dataset was derived from the cylindrical cavity model, which incorporated diverse dielectric samples exhibiting varying relative permittivity and loss factor, all for a given sample thickness. Subsequently, the model underwent validation to assess its accuracy across a broad range of dielectric constants, loss tangent, and pragmatic thickness of the sample. The proposed model achieved an accuracy exceeding 99 %, underscoring its effectiveness in predicting the dielectric properties of different materials.

articleTitle: Shared aperture dipole antenna design with common ground for pattern diversity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A two-port printed dipole antennas with shared ground and shared aperture to achieve uniform gain enhancement is presented. The metamaterial structure used is a Double Negative (DNG) complementary modified H-shaped resonator. The two antennas are orthogonal and as electrically close for an isolation of less than 10 dB. The measurements show that the resonator-loaded antenna presents a gain of about 5.2-6.7 dBi in the whole operational band (5-5.4 GHz), which is about 1.8-2.6 dB more than the unloaded one.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Digital Attenuator MMIC Over 1 to 10 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper on digital attenuator presents the design and development of a wideband MMIC over frequency range of 1-10 GHz, fabricated using 0.25 um GaAs p-HEMT process. The topology adapted is modified $\pi$- and T-type attenuator structures to enhance frequency of operation and to improve the performance, regarding insertion loss and the variation of insertion phase. The total attenuation of DA is of 15.5 dB and attenuation step of 0.5 dB. This attenuator realized on the footprint of 3.5 mm $\times 2$ mm, and the measured worst case rms amplitude errors are 0.4 dB and phase errors are 3.5° over a wide band of 1-10 GHz, evaluated over 5 chips and shows excellent performance validation against specifications.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly polarized MIMO dielectric resonator antenna for complete X-Band Coverage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research paper presents a MIMO Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) designed for X-band communication. The antenna operates in the 8-12 GHz frequency range and exhibits circular polarization with a wideband characteristic. High isolation, below -20dB, is achieved across the entire band through the introduction of a ground plane defect. The DRA consists of two stacked discs, where the upper disc is perforated and rotated to generate orthogonal modes. An air gap between the discs improves impedance bandwidth. The antenna is fed using orthogonal microstrip lines with conformal strips. Performance evaluation reveals a 25 % bandwidth with complete overlap of the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth. The proposed MIMO configuration offers a realized gain of 7.7 dBi to 8.6 dBi in the entire X-band. The efficiency is measured and observed above 90 % for the entire band. The proposed MIMO DRA offers advantages such as high isolation, wide bandwidth, and circular polarization, making it suitable for X-band communication applications.

articleTitle: High Dynamic Range Monopulse IF Receiver for an Airborne Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Monopulse technique is most commonly used to measure the angle of arrival of a target echo in a tracking radar. Such tracking radar is generally equipped with a microwave receiver to faithfully perform this measurement. For improved selectivity, this receiver is generally implemented in a double down-conversion scheme. This paper discusses the design and development of a high-dynamic range 4 channel IF receiver. This receiver is the second stage after the first down-conversion which is a 4 channel microwave receiver. These dual receivers are collectively used in an airborne radar system specific for a tracking application. Three out of four channels are for angle tracking purpose and the leftover channel is an auxiliary channel. The design’s specifications are dictated by system requirements including the volume and weight constraints. Basic configuration of the receiver with its simulation results and measured performance are presented. The impact of gain and phase imbalances of receiver on the d/s curve of the radar is also presented.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Conformal MIMO Antenna with Ladder Shaped Isolating Structure for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 3D printed conformal Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna is proposed for 5G sub-6GHz and Wi-Fi 6E applications. The antenna is printed on a Ninjaflex substrate and consists of two identical radiators. An innovative 3D ladder-shaped structure is used as an isolating element between the radiators to reduce mutual coupling. The identical radiators have a fan-shaped structure engraved with a circular ring to operate in a dual band at a resonance of 3.35 and 6.6GHz. The overall footprint of the 3D printed MIMO antenna is only $45 \times 25$ mm2 and conforms to a −10dB impedance bandwidth of 40.54% (2.95-4.45 GHz) in the lower 5G sub-6GHz frequency band and 18.32% (5.95-7.15 GHz) in the upper Wi-Fi 6E frequency band. The 3D printed MIMO antenna demonstrates excellent radiation characteristics with a gain of more than 2dBi and efficiency of more than 95% in both the dual bands. The antenna’s flexibility was also tested by bending it along the X and Y-axis at a radius of 30mm with successful results.

articleTitle: Development of LTCC based Inductors with Barium Hexaferrite Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper fabrication and characterization of ferrite-based inductors using LTCC technology is presented. Barium Hexaferrite (BaFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>) in the form of a paste is applied in between LTCC layers and cofired to form a ferrite-embedded inductor (2 turns) in design 1. In design 2, LTCC-compatible ferrite paste is developed in the laboratory and screen printed on the top layer to fabricate the inductor. These inductors are characterized in the frequency range of 1 GHz to 4 GHz. Design 1 shows a peak inductance of 11.51nH at 2.233 GHz and Quality factor(Q) 31. Design 2 shows a peak inductance of 8.795nH at 2.979 GHz and Q of 15.68 at this frequency.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Generation for Simultaneous Scanning Using Timed Arrays With Reduced Pointing Error
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents an approach to develop a simultaneous electronic scanning system utilizing the Time Modulated Antenna Array (TMAA) and a regression model. The TMA generates harmonics through inherent nonlinearity, enabling the radar to gather information from multiple directions concurrently. Leveraging a regression model, the beamforming system effectively predicts target positions within an azimuthal angle range of −50 degrees to 50 degrees. Experimental validation confirms the viability of the regression model, showcasing its accuracy in target detection and tracking.

articleTitle: Design of a Quasi-Elliptic Filter in Groove Gap Waveguide Technology Using Overmoded Cavity for Low-loss High-power Applications at Q-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of quasi-elliptic filters using groove gap waveguide technology at Q-band. The designed filter is an all-capacitive iris filter and the cross coupling is realized with the help of the phase reversed magnetic field in an overmoded waveguide cavity resonator using TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf> higher order mode. The concept is validated through a fourth order cascaded quadruplet filter designed with fractional bandwidth 1.97% at 38 GHz. The electrical performance of the filter is compared against a conventional rectangular waveguide based design for the same specifications. The high-power analysis of the filter is also carried out to demonstrate its practical applicability in high-power filter design.

articleTitle: Optimization of Modulating Waveforms for maximum Signal-to-Noise Ratio In a FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents an analysis of the received intermediate frequency (IF) spectrum for various modulating waveforms in a frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar system. Each waveform generates its own distinct IF spectrum, even when other parameters are held constant. The spectrum is additionally influenced by the sampling rate and the sampling window applied for the FFT operations. Four widely used waveforms-sinusoidal, sawtooth, triangular, and square waves, are considered for range measurement. The theoretical analysis shows that the sawtooth waveform produces the highest peak-to-peak voltage at the fundamental beat frequency. Therefore, it enhances the accuracy of range measurements. The theoretical predictions are validated through experiments conducted on an in-house built FMCW radar circuit.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Low-Loss Closely Spaced Dual-Band Filter for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact low-loss dual-band bandpass filter. It combines the effect of a combline configuration along with a shorted hairpin resonator configuration loaded with a series resonant circuit. The overall configuration manifests a closely spaced dual-band response with a distinct transmission zero in between without any additional circuitry. The circuit is analytically modeled, simulated, and experimentally validated. The measured insertion losses are 1 dB and 0.73 dB in closely spaced bands with center frequencies 1.3 GHz and 1.96 GHz, respectively. This planar filter finds wide application in miniaturized monolithic integration in wireless communication systems owing to its compact size.

articleTitle: Dual band Metasurface Polarizer for LP to CP Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a dual band metasurface which converts an incident linearly polarized wave into circularly polarized wave. Proposed metasurface polarizer consists of a 6x6 tabular arrangement of unit cells. Unit cell consists of two non-identical arc shape printed on top and bottom side of the substrate. It offers left hand circular polarization (LHCP) at lower band and right hand circular polarization (RHCP) at upper band. A slot loaded dual band linearly polarized antenna is also designed to demonstrate the operation of polarizer. Polarizer is kept very close to antenna ($\lambda$/20 at lower frequency) to keep the antenna size compact and it is made sure that return loss and gain performance is not disturbed. Proposed antenna with dual band metasurface based polarizer radiates LHCP at 2.7GHz and RHCP at 4.3GHz. It has 3dB axial ratio bandwidth of 20MHz and 270MHz at 2.7GHz and 4.3GHz, respectively. Although the metasurface is wideband in nature but linearly polarized dual band antenna is narrowband which limits the bandwidth. Full wave analysis of metasurface unit cell and the antenna with metasurface is conducted to validate it and reported here.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing enabling Radio Frequency Identification and Wireless Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Additive manufacturing processes, encompassing both two-dimensional and three-dimensional techniques, present unparalleled levels of flexibility for creating cutting-edge radio frequency identification and sensing systems. The analysis of electromagnetic characteristics in bulk or engineered materials holds a vital significance in the creation of novel devices and the enhancement of existing ones. The potential applications range from integrating tags into objects and wearable sensors to utilizing metasurfaces for improved probing of signals inside the human body and incorporating sensors into robotic hands to achieve precise object grasping.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Cross-Slot Antenna using Artificial Magnetic Conductor and Partially Reflecting Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a cross-slot antenna achieving pattern reconfigurability with linear polarization is presented. The proposed antenna has three distinct layers. The upper layer is a active Partially Reflecting Surface (PRS), middle layer contains a cross-slot antenna, and the bottom layer has Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) layer. The active PRS layer comprises a $4 \times 4$ unit cells and AMC layer consists of a $9 \times 9$ unit cells. Each unit cell on the PRS layer consists of a square loop and is loaded with two PIN diodes. Pattern reconfiguration is achieved by controlling operating states of PIN diodes on the PRS layer. The utilization of an AMC surface serves to enable directional radiation from the cross-slot antenna. The antenna is operated in three different operating modes. The simulated return loss characteristics and radiation patterns in all the operating states are presented. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna achieves wide impedance bandwidth from 3.34 to 3.70GHz in all the operating states. The overall radiation pattern of the antenna can be steered from -42° to +36°.

articleTitle: C Band 50W GaN Power Amplifier MMIC with High Harmonic Rejection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
