abstract: This paper presents design methodology of a C band 50W GaN Power Amplifier (PA) MMIC, fabricated in GaN MMIC process. The C-Band 50W GaN PA has been designed for use in Pulsed Applications. It is a 2-stage design, with input and output matched to 50Ohms and operates at $28 \mathrm{~V}$ supply voltage. Design goals are output saturated power of $50 \mathrm{~W} \mathrm{~min}$ at the fundamental with high harmonic rejection and PAE of $40 \%$ across required bandwidth. These design goals were met by combination of Load-pull and Harmonic tuning techniques. An LC resonator network specifically implemented at the output to improve harmonic rejection and obtain efficiency. Measured results demonstrate $50 \mathrm{~W}$ min saturated Output Power, $35 \%$ PAE, $15 \mathrm{~dB}$ Power Gain and a high harmonic rejection of 45dBc. Performance has been measured upto $30 \%$ Duty Cycle for a pulse width of $1 \mathrm{~ms}$.

articleTitle: Challenges in Design & Realization of Fabry-Perot Cavity Based High Gain Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper brings out the challenges in development of Fabry-Perot Cavity based high gain antennas. Criticality of dimensional tolerance and importance of accurate assembly of such antennas is brought out through design, realization and characterization of a Ku-band (10.95-11.20GHz) single horn fed single PRS based Fabry-Perot Cavity antenna (FPCA). Sensitivity of radiation pattern due to tilt angle of PRS w.r.t. ground plane is brought out. A novel cascaded impedance matching network to achieve better than 17dB return-loss over the band is also presented.

articleTitle: HEM and TM Excitation Modes For a Three-Port Wideband MIMO Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna at a mm-Wave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article is brief about multiple-input multiple output (MIMO) cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA). Two resonant modes, hybrid electromagnetic and transverse electromagnetic HEM 11 and TM 01 mode excitement, have been applied in MIMO CDRA for 5G mm wave communication. HEM and TM mode generates strong electric and magnetic dipoles achieved by using a slot aperture coupling technique through T-shaped microstrip feed lines. A prototype was successfully verified and experimentally demonstrated by the commercially available low-loss dielectric substrates Rogers RT 6010 and RO 4350. The proposed CDRA antenna was designed using CST simulation software and tested by a vector network analyzer. Further, less than −15dB isolation has also been attained at all three ports, resulting in no mutual coupling between the antenna elements.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Annular Ring Slot Antenna for Ka band Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The article addresses the design and performance evaluation of a Circularly Polarised Annular Ring Slot Antenna (CP ARSA) built for Ka band satellite applications. Distributed capacitances are inserted along the inner slots to induce degenerate modes at the resonant frequency. The antenna has a 20 % and 4.5% wide impedance bandwidth of 5.61 GHz (25.63 - 31.24 GHz) and an axial ratio bandwidth of 1.26 GHz (27.39 - 28.65 GHz). The antenna radiation pattern is RHCP with a gain of 5.36 dBic.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Low Profile Full-Metal CTS array for SATCOM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents the design and numerical investigation of a fully metallic low-profile antenna operating in the Ka-Band. The antenna is composed of two stacked circular parallel plate waveguides (PPWs), for beamforming and radiation, respectively. The system’s beamformer, positioned at the bottom of the structure, consists of a planar lens working in reflection, while the radiating part consists of a Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS) and is positioned on top. This latter PPW has corrugation on the bottom wall to support a slow wave, and slots etched on the upper wall to obtain radiation. The relative rotational movement between these two sections generates a phase gradient across the radiating aperture, resulting in a scan of the beam in the upper hemisphere. This approach ensures nearly frequency- and scan-independent active impedance and radiation efficiency, yielding broad band and consistent performance across all pointing directions. Furthermore, tapering efficiency is enhanced by appropriately adjusting the radiating slot width.

articleTitle: Analysis of 1-Bit Unit cell for Reflect Array Antenna in X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of a 1-bit unit cell for reflectarray antennas in X-band applications. Reflectarray antennas offer advantages such as lower profiles and lighter weights compared to traditional antennas. The unit cell is made up of four arrow-shaped structures with a single head, enabling the manipulation of electromagnetic waves and beam steering capabilities. The unit cell operates in two modes, bit-0 and bit-l. Simulation results demonstrate that the unit cell achieves a phase difference of 180 degrees for the co-polarization reflection coefficient across a wide range of frequency. Additionally, the paper discusses the potential use of tunable elements and graphene for switching operations to reduce fabrication costs. This research contributes to the development of compact and efficient reflectarray antennas for X-band applications.

articleTitle: Linearly Polarized D-band Leaky Wave Antenna Based on Series Slotted Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a slotted waveguide leaky wave antenna is presented for sub-THz applications. The 1-D series slot array consists of alternating slot reactance pairs that provide broadside radiation and large impedance bandwidth. The given antenna provides a minimum gain of 20 dBi in the 0.12 THz to 0.13 THz frequency range. The maximum efficiency achieved by the leaky wave antenna is 96 %, and its half power beamwidth is 2.4°. The alternating slot pair shows almost zero cross-polarization in the proposed antenna design, which represents the linear polarization purity. The presented full metallic, high gain, and wide bandwidth antenna is a suitable candidate for various D-band applications.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave multilayered design of rectangular metal waveguide-based slotted antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work uses multiple layers of mechanically machined metal contours to assemble a K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band (26.5GHz to 40 GHz) WR28 standard rectangular metal waveguide-based slotted antenna. The mechanical compression-based electronic packaging degrades the simulated electromagnetic results by tolerable margins. A total of 16 slots along the length of the waveguide is designed to obtain a maximum measured gain of 14 dBi along the broadside direction. To combat the inherent feature of low impedance matching bandwidth of such antennas, a shunt stub-based matching technique is implemented. The measured input reflection coefficient is better than -10 dB over 5 % bandwidth at a center frequency around 31.4 GHz with an estimated efficiency of 85 %. Apart from conduction loss, other losses are due to leakage from potential air gaps and surface roughness between the assembled layers of brass.

articleTitle: Pencil Beam Scanning Antenna for SCATSAT-1 Scatterometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The twin pencil beam scanning antenna system is used by ISRO’s SCATSAT-1 satellite, which carries the ocean scatterometer payload described in this paper. It addresses requirements, setup, design features, and RF performance. The desired radiation pattern is achieved by using a prime focal reflector along with a primary feed that employs the dominant mode (TE 11) and higher order modes of a circular waveguide. The high-power dual-channel microwave rotary joint for continuous power transmission from the stationary part to the rotating antenna system is also included in the study. The reflector antenna along with twin feeds deliver the anticipated electrical performance.

articleTitle: Development of RF Based Energy Harvesting Module for Passive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a radio frequency (RF)-based energy harvesting module for passive sensing, enabling wearable devices for measuring human physiological parameters. A compact meandered antenna was designed in Ansys, HFSS software to harvest RF energy at an operating frequency of 915 MHz UHF region. An LC based impedance matching network was designed to match the impedance of an antenna with a single stage rectification circuit in ADS software. The harvesting module, which is the combination of antenna and rectification circuit was fabricated and tested with in-house developed low-cost photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor. The lab-scale results are observed to be promising in developing a compact full-scale passive wireless sensor for monitoring physiological parameters.

articleTitle: Design of Circular Cross-Section Smooth Profile Spline Horn Antenna for Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel design of smooth profile spline horn antenna having circular cross section for Ku-band application is presented in this paper. Conventionally, low cross-polarization and high Gaussian coupling efficiency is achieved by corrugated conical horn. However, due to multiple corrugation the production cost of such horn increases significantly. Smooth profile horn offers symmetric beam, low crosspol and low sidelobe are preferred choice as their manufacturing is simpler than that of corrugated conical horns. The proposed horn is designed for a wide frequency range 10-15 GHz Ku-band operation with rectangular waveguide WR-75 as its input. The measured result shows reflection coefficient value below -17dB over a wide band frequency 10-15 GHz for Kuband application. The measurement of fabricated horn demonstrate strong correlation between simulations and measurements in terms of input matching. The simulated results suggests that this horn has very high Gaussian Coupling efficiency comparable to classical corrugated horns and the constant beam waist of $2.7\pm 0.2$ cm over full waveguide band.

articleTitle: Circular Polarized Patch Antenna for X-Band and Ku-Band Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low-profile (45 mm × 45 mm) microstrip microstrip patch antenna design has been presented here. This design gives triple band characteristics with circular polarization. It consists of a hexagonal patch with four slots, two forming a plus (+) and the other two forming a cross (X) slots. The patch is of copper and printed on an FR-4 substrate. The antenna resonates at 8. 688 GHz and 10.96 GHz (X-band), at 18.768 GHz (Ku band), which can be operated for satellite communication. These three bands are obtained with bandwidths of 0.3 GHz, 0.565 GHz and 3.644 GHz respectively. The design attains a peak gain of 4.64 dB.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface Switching between Absorption, Transmission, and Reflection, along with Frequency Tunability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A reconfigurable frequency selective surface (RFSS) with multiple electromagnetic (EM) operations using p-i-n diodes and varactors has been presented in this paper. The proposed design comprises metallic patterns on two sides of an FR4 substrate, with varactors mounted on the top layer and p-i-n diodes on both layers to achieve tuning and switching operations. This structure offers multiple characteristics, such as absorption, transmission, and reflection, under different switching modes along with frequency-tunable functionality. These characteristics have been achieved by controlling the p-i-n diode biasing conditions, which perform various switching modes, and adjusting the varactor diode’s reverse bias voltage to provide the frequency tunability for each mode. The simulated results demonstrate that in the OFF (top side p-i-n diodes)-OFF (bottom side p-i-n diodes) case, the MRFSS exhibits a bandpass response with an insertion loss of 1.8-2.9 dB from 1.68-2.56 GHz. The OFF-ON state shows a narrow-band absorber with an absorptivity ranging from 84.3 % - 96.5% in the frequency range of 1.84-2.85 GHz. The ON-OFF and ON-ON states enable partial and full reflection modes, with reflection amplitudes greater than -2.5 dB and -1.5 dB from 2.48-4.43 GHz and 2.55-4.62 GHz, respectively. This proposed RFSS structure with multiple characteristics and frequency tunability holds great potential for various applications.

articleTitle: Broadband High Gain Planar Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A microstrip antenna with one bottom and top seven(1BT7) configuration is designed which covers some portion of C band and 90% portion of X band. The cavity walls are incorporated to improve bandwidth and gain of antenna.

articleTitle: Wafer Level Packaging for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents results of some of the experiments to establish wafer level packaging of GaAs MMICs intended to be used in millimeter wave frequencies. A method to extend the RF connection to backside of the MMIC has been implemented without any modification to the MMIC process flow. Measurements on a CPW line with two such via transitions (aka signal via) show effectiveness of very low loss implementation as replacements to conventional bond wire based implementation.

articleTitle: Higher Order Harmonic Generation Using Capacitive Nonlinearity of the Step Recovery Diode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design, fabrication and experimental results of a C-Band higher order harmonic generator from input signal in UHF Band by using Step Recovery Diode is presented in this paper. The microwave circuit is realized on Rogers material of 10mil thickness and placed inside a metal block with proper channeling. The proposed harmonic generator using step recovery diode can be used as in Transmitter or Receiver subsystem of any Electronic Warfare system devoted to generate signals at specific frequencies.

articleTitle: Investigation into a low Profile, Planar, Multi Band Dense Dielectric Patch Inspired Hybrid Planar Antenna with Stable Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the present work, a new dense dielectric patch antenna inspired hybrid antenna structure has been proposed to achieve multiband characteristics with stable co-polarised broadside radiation patterns in the principal planes. In the design, very thin dielectric resonator with thickness 1 mm, permittivity 78 has been used as dense dielectric patch which makes the overall antenna structure low profile and compact. Also the radiation patterns are much symmetric. In case of multiband antennas, it is a real challenge to get stable radiation patterns and often, with introduction of multiple resonances, there are significant tilts in radiation patterns. It may hamper use of multiband antennas in practical applications. This lacunae has been alleviated in the present work. In all the bands, the proposed antenna exhibits broadside stable pattern with around 8.5 dBi, 8.31 dBi, 6 dBi peak gain. The simulation has been done in Ansys Electronic Desktop Suite 18.

articleTitle: Automation of Printed MIMO Antenna Design Using MATLAB for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 4-port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) design using printed Yagi-Uda antennas is proposed for 5G applications. The proposed design consists of 4 printed Yagi-Uda antennas at four corners of an FR4 substrate. A script has been written in MATLAB for designing the antenna in CST Microwave Studio. When the code is run in MATLAB, it automatically opens up CST using an API and draws the antenna in CST as per the dimensions given in the code. Two poles of different lengths have been used to form the dipole element (driven element) of each antenna. An isolator patch has also been designed and used midway on the substrate to yield better isolation. The overall dimension (125mm $\times 200$ mm $\times 1.6$ mm) of the proposed structure is almost similar to the dimension of a Tab. Hence it can be used inside gadgets like Tab or Laptop. This design is capable of operating in two 5G bands – n3 (1.71-1.78 GHz) and n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz). The simulated and measured results are in good agreement and they show decent isolation (cross-port S-parameters <−20 dB). Simulated gain-values obtained in both the bands are also decent $(\sim 1$ dBi at n3 and $\sim 4$ dBi at n78).

articleTitle: Multistate Planar OAM Antenna for Reduced Inter-Modal Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) is a new dimension of modulation for significant enhancement of the data communication rates within the given spectrum. OAM carried by an EM wave is associated with its characteristic phase variation in space, leading to orthogonality of each wave. Since this technology is now at an early developmental stage, there are several challenges in practically achieving the desired outcomes. This paper presents an OAM Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz) antenna capable of producing up to five (three simultaneous) orthogonal OAM states using a simple planner design. Additionally, a new approach to reduce inter-modal interference in line-of-sight OAM links has also been proposed and has been presented showing up to 9dB of isolation without any physical modification. Three different feed network designs are also included to, and one is discussed in detail for compliance with the demodulation requirements.

Author Keywords: Circular Microstrip antennas Orbital Angular Momentum

articleTitle: 3D Printed Broadside Coupled H-guide Based Directional Coupler at Sub-THz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we designed and analysed the broadside coupled H guide based directional coupler for the Sub-THz frequency range. The designed broadside directional coupler is fabricated using the Form Lab SLA (stereolithography) based 3D printer. In this technique, Grey resin material is used which acts as a polymer material. To excite the LSM mode firstly we designed the broadband transition from rectangular waveguide to H-guide which is fed by the rectangular waveguide WR-2.8. The even and odd mode properties of the broadside coupled H-guide have been studied. The proposed broadside coupler has a 24dB coupling at a frequency of 330GHz. To enhance the mechanical stability we introduced the bridge between the broadside coupled guides. In addition to the bridge and altering the gap between the waveguide, the coupling is varied with respect to the frequency.

articleTitle: X-Band Receiver Design for Missile Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a receiver design in X-Band frequency used in Missile system. It receives a BPSK modulated signal and down converts it to required intermediate frequency and is fed to a correlator for further processing. This receiver has dynamic range of 70 dB with receiver sensitivity of −110dBm. The RF frequency around 9.5 to 10.5 GHz is down converted to IF frequency of 20 MHz and automatic gain control (AGC) is implemented to maintain output signal level at +5dBm. The noise figure of the receiver is designed is ≤3dB. Furthermore, it outputs Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) and PLL Lock status for monitoring the status of the receiver.

articleTitle: Cavity Backed Cross Dipole Antenna With Wide Axial Ratio Beamwidth and High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and realization of broadband and wide-beam right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) cross dipole antenna. The crossed dipole is backed by a conical shaped cavity to achieve improved axial ratio beam-width over a wide frequency band with enhanced gain. The design incorporates a conventional feeding technique using a coaxial probe. A sleeve is designed which is soldered with the cable to ensure strength for the cable. The fabricated prototype of the proposed antenna has an overall size of $0.87 \lambda \mathrm{X} 0.87 \lambda \mathrm{X} 0.38\lambda$ ($\lambda$ is the free-space wavelength at the lowest CP operating frequency). The obtained impedance bandwidth (RL >15dB) is 18% (2-2.4GHz) and axial ratio bandwidth (AR <3dB) is 9%. The axial ratio (AR <3dB) beam-width achieved overall phi planes is 120° for 5.5% bandwidth. Efficiency achieved is above 90% for complete bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons based Leaky-wave Antenna for Continuous Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research presents a general idea to develop a continuous beam scanning antenna utilizing the spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs)-based transmission line. The transmission line using the corrugated metallic grooves helps in strong confinement of field within the line, which further improves the coupling between the line and the radiators. Theoretically and numerically simulated results shows good agreement in terms of dispersion and scanning range. It is found that the antenna is highly capable of dual beam continuous scanning in the sub-6 GHz frequency band. The dual beam continuous scan from -90° (at 3.07 GHz) to +16° (at 4.9 GHz) in the visible space. The antenna achieved an overall gain of 9.8 dB and fractional bandwidth of 117% at centre frequency of 3.15 GHz. Owing to the single layer, groundless, and improved performance characteristics, the proposed antenna seems to be potential candidate for sub-6 GHz applications.

articleTitle: A Multiband Ultrathin Multifunctional Polarization Rotator Metasurface and its Application in RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization rotating metasurface using reflective topology for simultaneous linear to orthogonal linear (LP-OLP) polarization rotation and linear to circular (LP-CP) polarization rotation over the multiple frequency bands is presented in this paper. The top of the unit-cell structure contains a modified ladder-shaped pattern on the thin dielectric substrate, while a continuous metallic layer is placed at the bottom of the metasurface to eliminate the transmission. The proposed multiband polarization rotator metasurface shows linear to circular polarization rotation over the frequency region of 5. 73-5.96GHz, 6. 65-9.82GHz, 11.23-11.78GHz. Simultaneously, it depicts linear to orthogonal linear (LP-OLP) polarization rotation over the frequency bands of 6. 09-6.44GHz, 10.19-10.96GHz. A wide angular stability is also obtained for several practical applications like remote sensing, microwave imaging, etc. This multiband ultrathin multifunctional polarization rotating metasurface is mainly suitable for C-band (4.0-8.0GHz) and X-band (8.0 -12.0GHz) applications. Moreover, a checkerboard surface is designed using the proposed polarization rotator, which reduces the monostatic and bistatic RCS.

articleTitle: Defected Ground Circular Shaped Non- Invasive Microwave Sensor for Deep Brain Temperature Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a circular shape microwave sensor for passive measurement of deep brain temperature noninvasively. The structure of proposed sensor consists of electromagnetic band gap (EBG) based ground plane with double sided rings of C shaped having opposite openings in the circular patch. The microwave sensor is designed on FR-4 substrate with dimension $40 \times 30 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm} 3$. The measured reflection coefficient in vacuum is $-48 \mathrm{~dB}$ at resonance frequency 3.8 GHz. The observed impedance bandwidth is $2.75 \mathrm{GHz}(2.75-$ 5.5GHz) with total gain of $3.1 \mathrm{~dB}$. The simulated results with human head phantom show maximum SAR value $381.87 \mathrm{w} / \mathrm{kg}$, maximum volume loss density $4.088 \times 108 \mathrm{w} / \mathrm{m} 3$ and minimum detectable electric field $(\mathrm{v} / \mathrm{m})$ of $5 \mathrm{~dB}$ in brain tissue for lw of input power at the depth of $15 \mathrm{~mm}$ inside head. The proposed sensor is capable of measuring deep brain temperature in the range of $350-400 \mathrm{C}$ in active mode.

articleTitle: High Gain Wideband 16×16 Reflectarray Antenna for 5G and mm-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposed a compact high gain wideband $16\times 16$ reflectarray (RA) antenna for 5G and mm-wave applications. The proposed RA has an octagonal shape polarization rotating unit cell to obtain a quantized 360 ° phase. This phase is quantized in two states by rotating the polarization which is obtained by etching a slot at ±45° on an octagonal patch. The required phase on this RA is compensated by positioned 0 and $\pi$-state of the unit cell. It is illuminated with a 13dBi pyramidal horn antenna. The maximum aperture efficiency and average realized gain are 22.46 % and 22.1 dBi respectively in the operating band of 30-40 GHz.

articleTitle: Transparent Band-to-Band Frequency Reconfigurable Microwave Absorber using Vanadium Dioxide based Switchable Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is a phase change material that manifests a reversible insulator to metal transition at $\sim 68^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> proclaims more than three orders of resistance switching, low on state resistance and fast transition (ns), which has encouraged its substantial application in RF switching, and reconfigurable microwave devices. This simulation work reports a transparent band-to-band frequency reconfigurable absorber using VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> based switchable ground plane between the top layer and bottom optically transparent ITO metallic ground plane. In insulating state of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, incident waves are transmitted through the switchable ground plane and proposed absorber resonates in the C-band from 5.71 GHz to 8.84 GHz with the reflection coefficient of $\sim -28$ dB at 6.84 GHz. Whereas, in the metallic state of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, switchable ground plane acts as a reflector. As a result, the absorber operates in the X and Ku bands from 10.28 GHz to 21.7 GHz with $\sim -26$ dB reflection coefficient at 15.23 GHz. The metallic ITO layer at the bottom serves as a ground plane as well as a heater to thermally trigger the phase transition of the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film.

articleTitle: High Efficiency and High Linearity GaN Power Amplifier with Harmonic Tuning and Fundamental Matching Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper outlines the design of a power amplifier (PA) that exhibits excellent efficiency and linearity. The design incorporates a novel harmonic tuning network (HTN) and a fundamental matching network (FMN). The HTN is implemented using two tuning lines for proper impedance mapping followed by separate harmonic traps for the second and third harmonics. Furthermore, the fundamental and harmonic impedances are properly mapped to the optimal values to achieve the desired efficiency and linearity. The design strategy is substantiated by developing a printed circuit board (PCB)-based PA utilizing a CREE CG2H40010F GaN device. The designed PA achieves a maximum power-added efficiency (PAE) of 77.8% and has a saturated output power of 39.7 dBm. Additionally, an improvement of approximately 3 dB is achieved in the third-order intercept (OIP3).

articleTitle: Printed Arrays for Radar for Drone Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design, simulation, realization of array antennas for surveillance and detection of drones using an X-band FMCW radar. Separate antennas for transmit and receive are provided. The fabricated prototypes demonstrate the feasibility of the designs, with good agreement between simulated and measured results. Radiation patterns at resonant frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> at X-band are presented, and parameters such as gain, beamwidths, and cross-polarization levels are reported. The paper emphasizes the importance of isolation between the transmit and receive antennas for optimal radar performance. Simulations indicate that a spacing of 300 mm offers the required isolation of 80 dB.

articleTitle: Review of Concealed Object Detections using RF Imaging over UWB Regime for Security Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the realm of contemporary communication, navigation, and remote sensing, the microwave spectrum stands as a pivotal natural asset. Spanning an extensive heritage of over a century, the method of utilizing electromagnetic principles for imaging has intrigued the intellectual pursuits of researchers and engineers alike. As the frontiers of science and technology advanced, solutions for imaging within the lower echelons of the microwave spectrum gradually came to light. The advent of airborne Synthetic Aperture Radars (SAR) marked pioneering steps in this trajectory. Endowed with unparalleled capabilities in terrestrial observation and reconnaissance, these SAR technologies started a new interest among researchers to expand SAR imaging further, encompassing different frequencies and a diverse array of applications. In a striking testament to progress, the last two decades have witnessed a cascade of breakthroughs and transformative innovations, revitalizing microwave technologies for the sole purpose of personnel security screening. Employing microwave signals, endowed with the unique capability to safely permeate clothing, concealed threats such as explosives and firearms can be unveiled without causing any concerns to personal health or inducing unwanted aftereffects. This document presents a brief journey in the advancements in Microwave Imaging (MI) technology for security imaging applications using Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Model-Based Design Approach for Class EFJ Power Amplifier with Analog Predistortion Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study shows a data-driven model-based design method for a 2.4 GHz Class EFJ power amplifier (PA) with an analog pre-distortion (APD) circuit. The primary focus is on enhancing the amplifier’s linearity without compromising gain. The APD circuit is incorporated to improve linearity characteristics, resulting in notable enhancements in linearity, a high adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR), and a power added efficiency (PAE) of 36%, albeit with a decrease in power gain. The measured output power of the amplifier is 35 dB. A Conventional (feedforward) Artificial Neural Network (CANN) model is employed to analyze linearity patterns further and make future predictions. The C-ANN model is trained using a comprehensive dataset containing input features and corresponding linearity measurements. Utilizing the trained C-ANN model makes it possible to anticipate the linearity of forthcoming PAs based on their input characteristics.

articleTitle: Design and Mathematical Modelling of Statistically Distributed Rotated Dual Split Elliptical CSRR Loaded SIW Antenna for Narrow Beam Highly Reduced SLL Based Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, statistically distributed Rotated Dual Split Elliptical Complementary Split Ring Resonator (RDS-ECSRR) loaded substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna with highly reduced side lobe level (SLL) and narrow half power beam-width (HPBW) is proposed. Both offset and rotation of RDS-ECSRR are distributed in statistical distributions to control the SLL and HPBW. The offset has been distributed using Uniform and Normal distribution whereas rotation of RDS-ECSRR is distributed using regular arithmetic progression (AP).A maximum of $\approx$ 13.2 dB realized gain with nearly 22.3 dB reduction in SLL and $\leq 11.1^{\circ}$ HPBW has been achieved using proposed Normal distributed RDS-ECSRR loaded SIW antenna. A closed form empirical relationship with at least 95% co-efficient bound has been modeled to predict the non-linear nature of SLL and HPBW reduction based on offset and rotation optimization. 2D and 3D radiation pattern for each statistical distribution has been illustrated to showcase the reduction in HPBW and SLL in each sub-section of this article.

articleTitle: A Simplified RF Technique to Estimate the Conductivity of Metal Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, an innovative and simplified RF (radio frequency) approach is presented to determine the conductivity of the test specimen at RF regime. A modified split pi (MSPi) shaped design topology coupled to a microstrip line is utilized as the conductivity sensor topology. The designed structure requires the placement of test specimen to convert the overall shape of the sensing element into an asymmetric rectangular split ring resonator (ARSSR). It produces a substantial notch level at the corresponding resonant frequency. The notch level of the ARSSR changes with the change in the RF conductive loss associated with the conductive test specimen. The sizes of different arms including test specimen parameters are optimized accordingly to attain a wide linear range with good conductivity resolution. The performance of the sensor is numerically verified corresponding to the conductivity range of standard metal sample (1e7 S/m), metallic composites and conductive inks (1e4 S/m). Simulation studies show that the sensor can determine the conductivity of samples with the conductivity range from 1e7 S/m to 1e4 S/m. The MSPi structure prototype is fabricated and tested with copper and aluminum samples. The measured results are in line with the idea proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer System using Near Zero Refractive Index Metasurface for ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a new star-shaped spiral meta-atom design having near zero refractive index (RI) and its periodic metasurfaces that enhances the power transfer efficiency (PTE) of a wireless power transfer (WPT) system operating in the industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band (2.40-2.48 GHz). The proposed meta-atom has double transmission windows in the 1-6 GHz range covering the ISM band in its first transmission window. Due to the near zero RI property, this metasurface can convert any incident waves (spherical/cylindrical) to planar waves upon transmission through it. Two circular microstrip antennas (CMSAs) having resonances at 2.42 GHz and 2.43 GHz in the ISM band are designed to set-up a WPT system. A $3 \times 3$ and a $4 \times 4$ metasurface have been designed using the proposed meta-atom that enhances PTE from 19.14% (−7.18 dB) to 24.66% (−6.08 dB). A step-by-step design procedure starting from the meta-atom up to the WPT system, along with the complete parametric study of the WPT system and a detailed physical analysis of the working of the meta-atom based on electromagnetic (EM) simulations, has been presented.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Design of Wideband Waveguide Packaging of Multi-MMIC Receiver at W band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper computer aided design (CAD) of packaging a multi-MMIC (monolithic microwave integrated circuit) receiver at W band is presented. A broadband microstrip to waveguide transition is designed. Cavities are formed to accommodate MMICs, single layer capacitors (SLCs) and bias circuits. A thorough simulation along with the bond-wires and cavities is carried out using 3D EM solver for packaging of multi-MMICs in waveguide. The designed waveguide package is used to build the receiver at W band consisting of one low noise amplifier (LNA) MMIC followed by a Mixer MMIC with conversion gain of 6.7 dB and noise figure (NF) of 7.6 dB over a bandwidth of 75-100 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Non-Quadrature Branch Line Coupler with Unequal Power Division using Asymmetric T-Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, it is shown that non-quadrature branch-line couplers can be designed using asymmetric two-port networks of T-Structure instead of transmission lines as in the conventional branch-line coupler. The design equations of the proposed coupler have been obtained using the Y-matrix method. The primary advantage is that it provides design flexibility for equal and unequal power division with quadrature and non-quadrature phase differences across ports. A practical design of the proposed coupler has been implemented on FR4 Substrate.

articleTitle: Design of Cryogenic Circulator in 65-nm CMOS Technology Using All-Pass Filter Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Quantum computers can reduce the computation time of many simple tasks that a classical computer cannot perform quickly. As the number of qubits in a quantum computer increases, handling qubit readout at room temperature becomes difficult. To manage the qubit readout efficiently for a quantum computer with thousands of qubits, qubit readout circuitry operating at cryogenic temperature is desired. Circulator is an important component of the qubit readout circuit, which is conventionally a bulky element. Various architectures have been proposed for integrated CMOS circulators. All-pass filter architecture is studied and implemented in 65nm CMOS technology. Non-reciprocal characteristics are achieved over a large bandwidth. After Post-Layout simulation, an insertion loss of 3.28 dB is attained, whereas isolation of more than 16 dB is reported over a large bandwidth. IIP3 greater than 15 dBm is obtained in all directions of the circulator, keeping it away from nonlinear region of operation for quantum applications.

articleTitle: Instant In-situ Non-destructive Measurement of Brix/Concentration of Sugar Syrup using Microwaves for Sugar Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the indigenous development of non-destructive instant Brix or Concentration measurement system using Microwave and its testing results in a live sugar factory. The system mainly consists of a 5.8 GHz Microwave transceiver and an Insertion probe which is fitted on the vacuum boiler for measuring the sugar syrup Brix or Concentration parameter. The transceiver is programmable by user and can be configured for any range of Brix parameters. It has programmable transmission power and receiver gain and can be configured by user through GUI. The insertion probe is rugged and sustainable in harsh environment conditions in sugar mills. The system has been installed in a running sugar factory and conducted trials. The system has measured the Brix parameter with an accuracy of +/−0.3°

articleTitle: Timing Synchronization in an FPGA-based Real-time Quantum Key Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), the time tagging (with a synchronized timing reference) of photon transmission/reception events is of utmost importance for the purposes of coincidence identification to obtain the sifted key between the communicating terminals (A: Aryabhata and B: Bhaskara). In entangled photon based QKD system, both communicating terminals receive the photons whereas in case of weak coherent photon based QKD system, one terminal transmits the photons, which are received at receiver. For the coincidence identification in QKD system, it is necessary to synchronize the time bases used for time tagging of photons between the communicating terminals operating at independent clocks. This paper presents timing synchronization and FPGA implementation of Time of Flight (ToF) estimation in a NavIC synchronized real time Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) system. The proposed time synchronization and Time of Flight estimation method has been implemented and successfully used in ISRO’s and India’s first successful demonstration of 300m free space entangled photon based real time quantum key distribution system and weak coherent photon based real time QKD system as well. The achieved accuracy for time of flight estimation is 10ns and timing synchronization within 20ns.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Thermal Analysis of W- Band Sheet Beam Electron Gun
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Sheet beam electron gun is needed for high power, tunable, compact terahertz vacuum devices. In this paper, a planner sheet beam electron gun without Magnetic focusing has been presented. Optimizing using numerical method a sheet beam of cross section 0.7 mm $\times 0.18$ mm has achieved with 50mA current at a beam voltage of 20 KV. Thermal and structural analysis of electron gun has done to increase efficiency and reliability of beam performance. Thermal deformation of electrodes has been computed in order to evaluate the spacing between electrodes in operating/hot condition. Further the current and structure of the electron gun has been optimized considering the expanded dimensions. The beam transported 100% over 50 mm without applying any magnetic field.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface With Novel Comb-Shaped Unit Cell Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Future wireless communication systems like 5G and even 6G have attracted an immense research interest in Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) with their promising coverage. In this paper, a simulation-based study on metasurface-based design for RIS has been presented, using a Comb-shaped unit cell structure. The unit cell has been simulated for its reflection phase response vs frequency in the mmWave band (24-30 GHz). A commercially available varactor diode has been mounted on the unit cell in the simulation, to provide user-controlled capacitance, which in turn can control the phase delay on the surface. The unit cell has been characterized for its phase response versus capacitance at 27 GHz. From this, a set of capacitances have been chosen that will provide a predetermined phase gradient over the reflectarray constructed using the unit cell. This phase gradient will control the reflected beam tilt angle. From a Bistatic RCS simulation of the structure, for two different phase gradients, the beam tilt angles have been found, which are observed to be very close to the calculated values, thus validating the design.

articleTitle: Wavelet Windows for leakage reduction in remote sensing images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Wavelets are usually used for data analysis and other applications. The remote-sensing images are usually defocused/ blurred due to the target's motion or improper backscatter received. This defocusing cannot be eliminated unless a proper defocusing algorithm is used. One of the simple techniques to remove defocusing is by applying windowing. Due to the bell-shaped structure of the wavelets, they can also be used as windows. This paper shows the application of window functions derived from different wavelets for leakage reduction in remote sensing images. Finally, it is shown that the window function derived from the complex Morlet wavelet gives better results than already existing windows by using inverse synthetic aperture (ISAR) data.

articleTitle: Quantum Protocols: A study on free space and fiber based QKD links
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Quantum key distribution is a revolutionary way of quantum cryptography which guarantees absolute security by using the fundamental principle of quantum mechanics. Quantum network consist of two or more nodes of $QKD$ connected via optical fiber or free space. Free space channel can connect two nodes at distances more than 1000Km s apart, whereas fiber links will be used to connect the end users in nearby vicinity. Here we present a study on potential quantum key distribution protocol which can be used in the future quantum network, leading to quantum internet on large scale.

articleTitle: A Novel Multiband Patch Antenna Based on Quasi-Mandelbrot Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a quasi-Mandelbrot fractal geometry is proposed and applied to the design of patch antennas. An equation for calculating the operating frequency of the patch antennas based on the quasi-Mandelbrot geometry is figured out according to the fractal and topological geometry theories. Simulation and experiment results demonstrate that the proposed patch antenna has up to seven resonant frequencies with a good gain at each resonant frequency. The quasi-Mandelbrot fractal geometry opens a new approach for designing multiband patch antennas whose number of bands can be much more than that of multiband patch antennas based on traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Decoupling Technique for the E-plane Array Microstrip Antenna Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a co-linearly polarized microstrip antenna placed in an E-plane configuration with high isolation for WLAN applications (5.8 GHz). The proposed antenna has reduced the mutual coupling without the use of any complex circuit, by using an innovative combination of: −1) a metallic vias wall through the substrate to minimize the E-field coupling, 2) four rectangular slots in the ground plane near the non-radiating edge of antenna helps to mitigate the H-field coupling. The proposed design provides an isolation of 30 dB over the band 5.72-5.85 GHz and a peak isolation of 45 dB at 5.8 GHz, along with 5.8 dBi gain and cross-pol level is less than 20 dB in the broadside direction. The proposed planar antenna design process is described and verified using the CST-Microwave full wave simulator.

articleTitle: Möbius-Coupled SRR (Split Ring Resonator) Oscillator Extends High-Performance Signal Generations into K-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Contemporary trends in SRR-inspired coupled resonator tank circuits show a note-worthy front-runner in low-phase noise power-efficient high-frequency signal generations for the current (5G) and later generation communication systems. Responding to this requisite, this paper provides an of the application of Möbius-Coupled SSR for the realization of low-cost compact size signal sources with low phase noise (typically- 125 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset, operating frequency 30 GHz, power dissipation 4. 75V, 35.2mA) through K-band.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Profile stacked patch Antenna for ISM and X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a design of two antenna arrangement with two different feedings stacked one over another to resonate ISM and X-band applications. The traditional circular patch antenna with microstrip feeding is designed to radiate in ISM (2.45 GHz) band. The 2$\times$ 2 antenna array with single co-axial feeding is located on the top of the circular patch antenna for X-band (S to 12 GHz) spectrum. Each antenna array elements have two opposite circular shaped dumbbell slots to enhance the bandwidth and other radiating characteristics. Both the stacked antennas are shares common ground plane. The proposed antenna has a physical size of 40$\times$ 40$\times$ 2.2 mm3. The proposed antenna radiating characteristics such as VSWR, gain, efficiency and radiation pattern are described. The numerically simulated antenna has bandwidth of 0.1 and 4 GHz, average gains are 4.02 and 7.32 dBi, and both the bands radiation efficiency>S5% at ISM and X-band spectrum, respectively.

articleTitle: A mm-Scale Low-Frequency Magnetoelectric Antenna for Short-Range Communications in Biomedical Implants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes an experimental demonstration of a wireless communication system with a mm-scale low-frequency Magnetoelectric receiving antenna that operates at a resonance frequency of 49.9 kHz. The proposed antenna is intended for short-range communication up to 200 cm, with a received power of −47.4 dBm. The proposed device has a limit-of-detection (LoD) of 0.3 mOe, and the corresponding voltage spectral density is $1.9 \mu V / \sqrt{H z}$ at 49.9 kHz. The device has a magnetic field sensitivity of 0.55 V/Oe. The near-field data transfer has been successfully established by the transmission of a base-band signal ”10101010” employing the frequency shift keying (FSK) modulation technique. The received signal is successfully recorded at two different misaligned angles between the transmitting coil and the ME device, 0 and 90 degree in the azimuth plane. Due to the unique features of the lead-free heterostructure based ME antenna, such as low frequency, miniaturized size, ease of fabrication, and cost-effectiveness, it has potential application in implantable biomedical electronics.

articleTitle: A Conformal Wideband Metamaterial Absorber Integrated with Chip Resistor for Microwave Shielding in C- and X- band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The study proposes an ultrathin wideband with stable polarized metamaterial absorber that suitable for both flat and curved surfaces. The basic building block of this absorber consists of four top metallic ‘T’ shaped resonators, which are connected by quad lumped resistors to optimize the absorption band. This unit cell is placed on FR4 with a copper backing. The absorber demonstrates perfect absorption within the frequency range of 4.3 GHz to 12 GHz under normal incidence angle. The remarkable novelty of this design lies in achieving ‘near to unity’ absorption and a reflection coefficient lower than −20 dB in the respective frequency range of 4.3 GHz to 12 GHz. The proposed design exhibits polarization independence for oblique angles of incidence due to its symmetrical structure. Furthermore, the absorber boasts a compact size of only $0.20 \lambda_{0} \times 0.20 \lambda 0$ with a substrate thickness of $0.0011 \lambda_{o}$, where the wavelength $\left(\lambda_{o}\right)$ is measured at 5 GHz. The study explores, optimizes, and demonstrates various other main characteristics and parameters of the absorber. To support the hypothesis of achieving high absorption, the authors examine normalized impedance, surface current density, and field distribution as well.

articleTitle: A Signal Elevated CPW Line Using SU-8 Core for mm-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a thick Signal Elevated Coplanar Waveguide (SECPV) using SU-8 core to reduce substrate loss which is dominant in conventional CPIV lines at higher frequencies. A SECPW line has been fabricated over a glass substrate with copper as conductors. The measured line shows good RF performance with an insertion loss of 0.09 dB/mm and 0.32 dB/mm at 24 GHz and 50 GHz respectively, while the measured return loss is better than −18 dB throughout the spectrum with a measured time delay of 10.3 ps.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of Multi-Output, Ka-Band Frequency Synthesizer with High Output Power
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a Phased Locked Loop (PLL) based compact, dual output, high output power frequency synthesizer (FS) for generating local oscillator (LO) signals at 28.2GHz and 7.6GHz. Highly stable Temperature Compensated Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) is used for input reference signal (50MHz). The generated reference signal is further fed to frequency multiplier, band pass filter followed by a multi-chip drop-in module (DIM) to deliver high output power (1.31W) at desired frequency band. Multi-chip DIM comprises of MMIC frequency multiplier, band pass filter (BPF) and high power GaAs Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) amplifier, which are accommodated in a single module with proper heat dissipation scheme. All the components are finally housed in a single package and measured. Measured results unveil output power of +31.2dBm at 28.2GHz with phase noise of −107.37dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset and +14.3dBm at 7.6GHz with phase noise of −121.45dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset. The realized frequency synthesizer can be used for astronomical applications as a LO source.

articleTitle: Achieving Spaceworthiness for Large-Size LTCC Packaging of Microwave MCM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the various methodologies for realization of microwave subsystems through packaging of multiple bare MMICs. The use of LTCC substrate for packaging of hermetic multi-chip modules (MCM) has given significant benefits in terms of miniaturization and mass reduction. However, it poses several challenges for assembly and hermetic sealing of these large-size (>35 mm in both dimensions) LTCC modules. Various techniques for assembly and hermetic sealing were attempted and their outcomes are summarized.

articleTitle: Development of a Near-Field Sensor for Diagnosis of Liver Diseases Using 3D-EM Simulation of Mouse Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, we studied the response of an antipodal Vivaldi antenna in the presence of different types of mice liver models. The scope of the study was limited to two types of liver diseases, i.e., nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and fibrosis. The complex dielectric properties of each liver type were measured using the open-ended coaxial probe dielectric spectroscopy method. A Vivaldi antenna for near-field sensing was designed and then simulated in CST Studio to determine the antenna characteristics. The antenna performance from the simulation matched the reflection coefficients (S11) measurements collected with the fabricated antenna in an anechoic chamber. This verified antenna was used for further measurements of different liver models placed near the antenna. The antenna response, S11 measurements, varied from one tissue type to another, demonstrating the potential of using the Vivaldi antenna as a near-field sensor to differentiate liver disease models from the healthy liver model.

articleTitle: Design and development of Antenna System for Millimeter-wave Humidity Sounder Payload
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of antenna system for humidity sounder for ISRO Microsat2B satellite. 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> offset reflector antenna system was proposed for this mission. Critical elements of the antenna part was feed horn operating from 167-199GHz. Spline profiled smooth-wall horn is designed using mode matching based code along with GA based optimization algorithm. The complete antenna system was designed and developed. The simulated and measured beam efficiency of the antenna is better than 93% over the bands. The simulated and measured secondary radiation patterns are compared and they are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Suppression in Aperiodic Antenna for Large Phased Array using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the field of array antenna design, there is a growing demand for high-performance antenna systems with smaller grating lobes. Grating lobes, undesirable secondary lobes that show up in the radiation pattern of array antennas, can interfere with signals, lower their quality, and have a restricted ability to resolve space. Aperiodic arrays have been an appealing way of reducing grating lobes while preserving optimal radiation characteristics in recent years. The design, analysis, and performance assessment of aperiodic arrays for grating lobe reduction are covered in detail in this study.The concept and advantages of aperiodic arrays are introduced, emphasising how they can decrease grating lobes by interrupting the periodicity in the arrangement of the antenna elements. This paper uses genetic algorithm which is a powerful optimization technique that can be applied to find the optimum distance between subarrays in an aperiodic array, leading to a reduction in grating lobes.Through multiple generations, the genetic algorithm narrows down the search space, gradually converging towards the arrangement that yields the lowest grating lobes. The selection of element placements, inter-element spacing, and optimisation strategies are covered as design factors for aperiodic arrays.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Omni-directional Antenna using Modified Split-ring Slot as a Radiator for UHF Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile omni-directional antenna has been suggested for UHF communication. The proposed antenna consists of a radiating split ring slot array (SRS-A) for achieving an omnidirectional property at a resonant frequency of 385 MHz. To provide an excitation to these SRS-A, a 1:8 power divider has been designed for desired radiation characteristics. The overall size of the low profile antenna is 460 × 460 × 1 (mm)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The purpose of designing the proposed antenna is to achieve an omni-directional radiation property with high radiation efficiency and gain of 2.50 dB while maintaining a low profile. The proposed antenna is suitable for the UHF band wireless communication.

articleTitle: Ku-Band GaN High Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A high-power, broadband, high power added efficiency linear power-amplifier is designed using 0.25$\mu$ m GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor technology. The amplifier uses 3-stages with large periphery output devices to deliver an output power of 15W at Ku-band. The amplifier demonstrated up to 20 dB large signal gain over 18% bandwidth. The 4.6mm $\times$ 2mm MMIC chip demonstrated peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 30% and average PAE of 28% over the band.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized Conformal Square - Ring Slot Based Antenna for Reliable Vehicular Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study suggests a circularly polarized square ring slot-based microstrip patch antenna suitable for vehicular communication system. The antenna design involves a chamfered square-shaped patch placed within a square ring slot, connected by two small stubs. Circular polarization has been achieved by chamfering the opposite corners of a inner square patch. The impedance bandwidth is achieved to be 750 MHz (5.15-5.90 GHz), while the 3-dB Axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) is obtained from 5.15 GHz to 5.22 GHz respectively. Both the planar and conformal versions of the proposed antenna demonstrate wideband characteristics. In addition, using a virtual model of the car, the radiation characteristics of the antenna while placed on a vehicle were investigated. The results reveal that the proposed antenna is compact, performs well, and is well suited when integrated with vehicle targeting WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Spurious Free Wide Stopband Waveguide Filter for Q-band Payload
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance, low-loss Q-band waveguide filter with a wide spurious free stopband. A 6-pole Chebyshev filter is designed with a stepped impedance waveguide resonator at 38GHz, which provides more than 50 dB rejection at 1.5 times center frequency. The filter far stopband performance is superior compared to the equivalent waveguide resonator filter with a minimal increase of insertion loss. The filter performance is stable over the temperature range from −20 deg. C to 80 deg. C with a frequency drift of 16.26 ppm.

articleTitle: Navigating the Road to Connectivity: Use Cases and Design Considerations for V2X Networks Using Millimeter-Wave 5G Beam-Steering Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) rely heavily on a suite of perception sensors such as cameras and LIDAR for accurate and robust on-road decision making. However, these sensors have a limitation of line-of-sight (LOS), which can significantly restrict their effectiveness. To overcome this limitation, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks are being developed to wirelessly receive non-line-of-sight (nLOS) data from surrounding sources such as road-side units (RSUs). By leveraging nLOS data, V2X networks can significantly enhance the situational awareness of CAVs, improving traffic efficiency and road safety. In this paper, we present selected use-cases of V2X networks such as vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, vehicle platooning and cooperative perception using a beam-steering antenna that offers a wide bandwidth and fast beam-steering.

articleTitle: Development of active polarization tracking and compensation system for satellite-to-ground QKD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In polarization-encoded satellite-to-ground quantum communication, the on-board transmitter and a receiver at the optical ground station encode and decode linearly polarized quantum bits for execution of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol. Dynamic polarization tracking and compensation is a key technique in realizing such a space based QKD system. In this work, we report the design and development of motorized waveplate based active polarization compensation system. Integrated testing and validation with Decoy-state enabled BB84 QKD testbed over ~5m free space channel and quantum link polarization extinction ratio (PER) ≥ 100:1 has been carried out successfully. Satellite motion was emulated as a continuous 1°/s polarization basis rotation at the Quantum Tx output. When active polarization compensation system was enabled, sazimuth (Az.) deviation was measured with ±1.5° accuracy. During this experiment, overall signal QBER was consistently maintained at <3.5% with secure key generation rate of ~1350kbps, proving the suitability of this scheme for realistic satellite-to-ground QKD scenarios.

articleTitle: Open-Source Visualization Tools for Antenna Engineers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Data visualization is an important part of data analysis and is used in all fields, antenna engineering being one of them. Antenna engineers mostly use closed-source tools to run simulations for electromagnetic applications. However, these tools have their limitations in data visualization and only process their own created data internally for visualization. To facilitate engineers, there are several open-source alternatives but these tools are not being used much by antenna engineers due to lack of exposure. In this manuscript. we compare various open-source two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) visualization tools for antenna engineers in terms of plot aesthetics, strengths and weaknesses of these tools, and speed. This work will help to bring more engineers to open-source tools so that they can benefit from them.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of backscattering from dielectric sphere for design of THz tags
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The electromagnetic backscattering from an isolated spherical dielectric resonator is investigated for its potential application as a chipless and retrodirective tag. The motivation to use a dielectric resonator is its zero conduction loss, thereby being ideally suited to a low-power terahertz operation. The theoretical analysis is done using Mie theory, addressing the natural electromagnetic modes of an isolated spherical scatterer, and interference of the fundamental dipole modes pertaining to directive backward scattering. The working principle, optimized design and practical limitations of the envisaged tag design are discussed taking into consideration engineering trade-off and low-cost system design.

articleTitle: Study of Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Effectiveness of Conductive Polymer Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new type of pollution known as electromagnetic interference (EMI) is one of the major problems in today’s wireless world due to developments and advances in science and technology. This EMI not only interferes with the normal operation of electronic equipment, but also adversely affects human health. Conductive Polymer Composite (CPC) shields have taken an important place for shielding purposes due to their advantages such as light weight, low cost, flexibility, chemical resistance and corrosion resistance. The Shielding Effectiveness (SE) of composites against EM radiation strongly depends on the manufacturing technique used, conductivity, thickness, and dielectric properties of the composite. To this end, various composites were studied using insulating polymer matrices combined with different types of conductive fillers such as graphite (Gr), carbon nanotubes (CNT) and nanometal particles and various types of biochar from biomass such as sugarcane bagasse, bamboo and wood chips. Shields can be manufactured using compression molding techniques for rigid shields and solvent casting for flexible sheets. Impedance analyzers are used to measure the dielectric properties and vector network analyzers are used to measure the S-parameters of different shields manufactured in different high frequency ranges. The far-field EMI shielding using the obtained dielectric properties and S-parameters can be calculated.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch with a Vertical Loading for Improved Radiation Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study introduces a novel design approach to reduce the cross-polarized (XP) radiation from a microstrip patch over the orthogonal plane. A vertical loading is positioned at the center of the patch to attenuate the fields originating due to TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode. In contrast to earlier reported works, this loading is printed on a PTFE substrate to minimize the loading height. This breaks the fundamental notion of $\lambda$/4 loading height for XP suppression. A C-band rectangular patch is used for the study. The proposed method reduces the loading height by 77 %. It also suppresses the XP radiation over the orthogonal plane by 15 dB, maintaining the input impedance and co-polar radiation patterns undisturbed.

articleTitle: A mmWave Phased Array for Joint Radar and Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: To fulfill the capacity requirement of next-generation communication, the mmWave band is the center of attention and a mmWave phased array can provide the necessary flexibility in the hardware. Taking analogies from the monopulse radar concepts, we propose to use a mix of sum and difference patterns in a small planar phased array to collect the direction of arrival quickly. The proposed receiver architecture employs the fast beam-switching feature of the beamforming IC to enhance the unambiguous angular range of the array and thereby making it a promising candidate for joint radar and communication.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filter Based On Inductive Post Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a Band Pass Filter (BPF) using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technique in the Ka-band frequency range. The device model is designed with an inductive post in a single layer of substrate, which is compact and easy to fabricate. Filter have a center frequency around 31.5 GHz, B.W. = 2 GHz, fractional B.W. = 6.29%, Insertion loss at center frequency is around 0.6 dB & Return loss is better than 22 dB, Stop Band rejection is better than 15 dB at both side of Pass Band. A fabricated model is presented for validation of the simulated filter design. The measured result is in good agreement with the simulated result. The proposed Filter can be used in 5G applications with good performance.

articleTitle: In-House Experimental Demonstration of a Four-Port Antenna System and Wilkinson Power Combiner for Rectenna Applications in n78 Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a subsystem for the rectenna configuration in the n78 band (between 3.2 and 3.67 GHz). This subsystem includes an orthogonally arranged 4-port antenna array and a 4-way Wilkinson power combiner. The individual antenna element is a binomially tapered seriesfed 3-element patch sub-array with sidelobe level (SLL) less than -20dB. The 4-port antenna configuration provides 360 degree beam coverage with a peak gain of 6.5 dBi at 3.55 GHz operating frequency for energy harvesting applications. The 4-way Wilkinson power combiner is specifically designed at the n78 frequency band. It provides isolation between input ports ranging from -15 to -20dB and has an insertion loss (IL) slightly greater than 6 dB. The proposed subsystem can combine the received power at the antenna ports and feed it to the rectifier input to generate a DC output voltage. A simple in-house experimental demonstration of the combined power output in the laboratory environment is provided with the 4-port receiving antenna (Rx) being irradiated by multiple ultrawideband (UWB) Vivaldi antennas having SdBi peak gain each.

articleTitle: Output Power and Efficiency Improvement of a Class C Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficient class C power amplifier (PA). The practical current-voltage waveforms at the drain/collector terminal of the package plane deviate significantly due to the parasitic effects of a discrete transistor at the RF frequencies. This work focuses on optimizing the current-voltage waveforms at the package plane to minimize the DC power consumption of the device. Additionally, a harmonic suppression network is introduced as a part of the output matching network. This arrangement substantially enhances both the power-added efficiency (PAE) and the output RF power. The harmonic rejection also experiences a significant improvement. The simulated predictions are validated through fabrication and measurement. The PAE improves by at least 10%, and the output power increases by at least 1.6 dBm compared to a class C PA.

articleTitle: Development of Microwave Magnetic Components using LTCC Technology with embedded Barium Hexaferrite Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate a magnetically tunable microstrip patch antenna and an SIW based Isolator developed by successfully embedding Barium Hexaferrite disc in the middle of LTCC (Ferro L8) layers. By forming a cavity inside the LTCC substrate and placing a sintered ferrite disc in the cavity, a ferrite embedded LTCC substrate was fabricated. Microstrip patch antenna which has a center frequency of 10.6 GHz shows tunability of 400 MHz (3.77%) by applying magnetic field of 0.5 Tesla to this substrate. SIW based Isolator having isolation of 35 dB at 31 GHz was also designed on this substrate.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz Asymmetric Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons based Broadband Beam Scanning Antenna for Wide Angle Coverage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this research an interesting spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) waveguide-based beam scanning antenna for wide angle coverage is proposed. The SSPPs waveguide is designed using the antisymmetric unit cell of periodic modulated metallic grooves. The non radiating mode of SSPPs is used to fed the elliptical patches placed close to the grooves for generating radiating fast mode. The asymmetry in the transverse direction of the waveguide is introduced for strong improvement in the continuous beam scanning range through broadside. The complete idea is theoretically and numerically validated, and it is found that single main beam steer from −46° (at 3.41 GHz) to +46° (at 5.63 GHz) through broadside which is quite difficult due to open stop band effect. The maximum scanning range and the impedance bandwidth of 92° and 66% is achieved in the leaky region respectively for sub-6 GHz band applications.

articleTitle: Classification of RF Fingerprint Signals from UAV Controller Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have gained widespread popularity in various industries with advent in technology due to their advantages and cost-effectiveness, but they also pose serious threats to security if misused. Detection and classification of radio frequency (RF) signals obtained through communication between a drone and its controller is one of the ways to look out for and prevent misapplication of UAVs. This paper presents a novel approach to classify RF signals from distinct drones using machine learning (ML) techniques. The study involves training and evaluating of multiple ML models on a limited batch of dataset consisting of 5 specimens of RF signals from various drone types. In addition, the paper also identifies the key features of signals that are needed to be extracted from RF signal data for appropriate modeling and classification. The key objective of this research was to achieve best accuracy while using limited dataset by identifying and including most valuable features of RF signal. Important signal features like Mean, Variance, Skewness, Kurtosis and Energy Spectral Entropy were extracted from the RF data. Despite the minimal data used, the kNN classification achieves the accuracy of 88.2% with inclusion of all 17 classes of drones and improved to 92.86% when trained on 14 classes. This shows promising potential for real-world application. The study demonstrates that even with a small training dataset, ML techniques can effectively classify RF signals from drones.

articleTitle: In-situ surface crack detection on metal using a passive wireless RFID-based NDT sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In-situ structural health monitoring is essential for the early detection of surface cracks at dedicated stress locations. This paper presents a circular-shaped RFID sensor design for wireless surface crack detection on metal. The sensor was designed in the HFSS software tool with a diameter of 50 mm in dimension. Simulation analysis was performed for varying crack depths and widths at sub-millimeter resolution. The sensor is sensitive enough to detect a minimum crack depth of 0.2 mm. The average resonant frequency gradient $(\Delta)$ is used to differentiate the varying crack depths and widths. For varying crack depths, the observed $\Delta$ values are 2.1 MHz and 6.1 MHz for sub-mm and mm resolution, whereas for varying crack widths, the values are 2 MHz and 7.6 MHz, respectively. Simulated crack samples are fabricated and examined using conventional Eddy USB to illustrate the pros and cons of passive wireless surface crack detection using an RFID-based NDT sensor.

articleTitle: Physics Embedded Neural Network (PENN) Architecture for Solving Maxwell’s Equations towards Accelerated Microwave Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate a neural network architecture that is useful in providing a solution of wave equation through the optimization of the neural network. The developed algorithm is based on integrating the physics equations directly into the neural network and therefore provides an effective, datafree method of solution of the underlying equations.
