The proposed neural network exhibits solution time similar to that of classical finite element method (FEM) solver. Additionally, by employing transfer learning, neural network achieves even faster solution for similar new equation. As compared to the direct neural network optimization, the transfer learning solution is up to 7.1 times faster for the cases considered.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Design of Frequency Reconfigurable Compact Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a machine learning (ML) based compact microstrip patch frequency reconfigurable antenna for multiple frequency band application. The antenna consists of four metalized patches symmetrically arranged and coupled via slots and metallic bars, respectively. Variations in the material, geometry, and bias parameters of the microstrip patch antenna, along with the R, L, and C values of the equivalent circuits of the varactor diode, add frequency reconfigurability. Frequency reconfigurability is predicted using the artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate model for multiple frequency bands of 0.5 GHz – 7.5 GHz with very high accuracy and time efficient manner as compared to full-wave electromagnetic simulations solvers such as high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) or CST microwave studio (MWS).

articleTitle: Optimization of Beam Shaver Section for Helix TWT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Beam Shaver Section (BSS) has been designed and simulated for a high-efficiency Ku band helix traveling-wave tube (TWT). Required cathode flux linkage and magnetic field value at beam throw point have been calculated analytically as well as using 3D EM simulations. A study is presented wherein effects of first and second magnet of BSS section on TWT output power and helix interception current are simulated. Effect of magnet treating tolerance on TWT output power with respect to second magnet is also simulated. All simulations were carried out in the commercially available CST MWS software. Simulation results have been experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Reducing Q Factor in a Near Half-Mode Miniaturized Patch Antenna Using Slotted Ground
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The significance of compact, miniaturized antennas in modern wireless communication lies in their efficient use of space, adaptability, and versatility. Coupled microstrips are known for miniaturising the electrical dimensions of a patch antenna by introducing capacitive loading. This in turn increases the propagation constant and enhances slow-wave characteristics, thereby reducing the electrical dimensions of the antenna. In this work, a dual coupled slot based miniaturised antenna operating at near half-mode resonance is proposed. The electrical dimensions of the structure were reduced to $0.15\times 0.15 \lambda_{0}^{2}$, but with a very low bandwidth (1.8%). To improve the bandwidth of the antenna without significantly sacrificing it electrical dimensions, slots were etched out from the ground plane of the antenna. This adds some reactance in the surface current path, which reduces the Q-factor and increases bandwidth. The increase in electrical dimensions of the antenna is found to be within tolerable limits. The proposed work is compared with prior existing literature and is found to have a larger figure of merit in terms of electrical dimensions, bandwidth and gain.

articleTitle: Concurrent Triple Band Complex to Real Impedance Transformer for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work introduces a novel technique to simultaneously match any three uncorrelated Frequency Dependent Complex Loads (FDCLs) to a real source. Its adaptability allows it to transform any load combination for any frequency ratio. Since all the transmission lines used in the design have a characteristic impedance of 50 Ohms, there isn’t any fabrication related restrictions of the structure. In the proposed scheme, a branched stub adds susceptance to the load admittance such that the modified loads for all the three frequencies can be moved to g=1 circle, hence matching the real part of the admittance using a single series transmission line. The left over susceptances are cancelled through another branched stub. Two triple band prototype matching networks have been presented. All the structures are fabricated on ROGERS RO4003 substrate with dielectric constant, er=3.38 and height, h=20 mils. The simulated and the measured results are in good accordance.

articleTitle: Rotated Dual-Split Circular CSRR Loaded Homogeneous Metasurface Backed HOM Suppressed Polarization Diversified MPA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we design a Rotated Dual-Split Circular CSRR (RDS-CCSRR) loaded Isotropic Homogeneous Metasurface (IIM) backed higher order mode (HOM) suppressed microstrip patch antenna (MPA). The proposed antenna exhibits dual band response at 3.54 GHz and 4.375 GHz with overall size of $0.19 \lambda_{0} \times 0.19 \lambda_{0}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ is the free space wavelength at 3.54 GHz. To suppress the higher order modes (HOMs), probe through hole (PTH) has been introduced near CSRR. An Inhomogeneous, Isotropic metasurface (IIM) has been backed with RDS-CCSRR loaded patch to modulate the surface wave characteristics which effects the polarization behavior of the overall antenna. The proposed IIM backed CSRR loaded MPA achieves $\mathrm{S}_{11}\lt-18.5$ dB in dual bands with improved realized gain and undistorted hemispherical radiation pattern. Behavior of Polarization control through metasurface backing and substrate height variation is observed into this article.

articleTitle: Monte-Carlo based Approach for Analysis of Systematic and Random Errors in Deployment of Radial Rib Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the Monte-Carlo based approach for modeling and analyzing systematic and random errors that can be employed during the deployment of the ribs of a Radial Rib type reflector antenna. Systematic and random errors are introduced in the rib deployment by defining the periodic and random function of the rotation w.r.t. the anchoring point of the ribs. Both functions have random variables following the uniform probability distribution. The RMS of the reflecting gore surface with such errors in the ribs and its corresponding gain loss is computed. Here, such modeling and analysis are used to implement Monte-Carlo based analysis by running a large number of cases of the errors and the corresponding probability density functions are developed to estimate the impact of the errors on the secondary gain performance. Both types of errors are analyzed for the $0.05^{0}$ and $0.1^{0}$ tolerance ranges in the rib deployment. It is concluded that systematic error has more impact and is more critical to the antenna performance than random error.

articleTitle: Heuristically Aided Design of Dual Band Shared Aperture Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis of a shared aperture antenna array operating over S and X bands. The antenna elements are PEC backed probe fed rectangular patch antennas with same thickness of the substrate for both the bands. The array are interspersed using array thinning technique utilizing invasive weed optimization technique and the inter-element spacing chosen is $\lambda / 2$ for both S and X bands. A $10 \times 10$ S-band array and a $30 \times 30 \mathrm{X}$-band array were thinned simultaneously to achieve peak side lobe levels less than −16 dB in both the bands while avoiding the overlapping of X-band patches over the S-band patches. The technique also inherently takes care of the physical patch dimensions as well. The proposed work is useful for phased array applications.

articleTitle: Novel Metasurface Design with ϵ-shaped Unit Cell for High Reflectivity and Wide Phase Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In recent years, metasurfaces have emerged as powerful tools for manipulating electromagnetic waves with unprecedented control and flexibility. In this study, a novel $\epsilon$-shaped metasurface design that exhibits high reflectivity and a wide phase range is proposed. The metasurface is composed of epsilon-shaped subwavelength structures arranged in a specific configuration to achieve the desired reflection properties. By carefully tuning the geometry and dimensions of the epsilon-shaped split ring resonator, it has been demonstrated that the metasurface can reflect incident waves with high efficiency. Moreover, the proposed $\epsilon$-shaped metasurface design enables a wide range of phase control capabilities. By incorporating a variable-sized split ring structure, one can actively manipulate the phase of the reflected waves across a large span. This feature opens up new opportunities for wavefront shaping, beam steering, and other advanced applications requiring precise phase control. To evaluate the performance of the metasurface, numerical simulations are carried out to analyze its reflectivity and phase response. The results show that the $\epsilon$-shaped metasurface achieves a high reflectivity exceeding 90% while maintaining a wide phase range of 340° at 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Transparent Compact Rectenna (TCR) Based Continuous Wireless Charging System (CWCS) for Smart Watches by Utilizing Available 5G Microwave Radiations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper represents a compact, transparent microwave energy harvesting (MEH) system at a 3.3 GHz frequency band to assist the rechargeable battery system of the smart watch. The operating frequency of the proposed system is targeted to the 5G and beyond communication’s frequency bands. It is feasible to integrate a CPW-fed transparent folded monopole circular patch antenna onto the dial of the smart watch. Transparent conductive materials ITO and PET as substrates are utilized to design the proposed antenna to enhance the transparent efficiency of the rectenna system. The radiated gain of the proposed antenna is achieved of 2.16 dB at 3.3 GHz, with an omnidirectional radiating field pattern. Further, a microwave energy harvesting system is designed that consists of an antenna, a matching circuit, and a voltage doubler rectifier circuit by utilizing the Schottky diode (HSMS2860). The maximum output voltage of the rectenna system is obtained at 0.926 volts, while the maximum output power of 0.5484 (mW) is achieved at 3.3 GHz. The maximum RF-dc conversion efficiency (PCE%) of the proposed microwave energy harvesting system is obtained at 55%.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Unequally Spaced Antenna Array with Reduced Design Complexity and Computational Cost
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method of synthesizing unequally spaced array (UESA) antenna is proposed. For UESA, the problem dimension (D) i.e., the number of unknown variables is increased with increasing the number of array elements. Usually, the stochastic evolutionary algorithm is employed to determine the unknown element positions of the array under consideration. For large array, the design complexity is increased, and the algorithm takes large computational time to find out unknown variables. In this paper, a novel UESA structure consisting of multiple sub-arrays with equally spaced elements is proposed. As the constituent elements within a sub-array are equally spaced, the number of unknown design variables to be determined for the proposed array structure is drastically reduced. To show the effectiveness of the proposed method, the numerical results by considering a 30-element array is presented and compared with the previously reported results.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces With Suppressed Quantization Lobe for Arbitrary Reflection Angles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology in wireless communication by dynamically altering electromagnetic wave propagation. These programmable surfaces, constructed using metamaterials, exhibit anomalous reflection through the manipulation of electric and magnetic properties. This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of RIS design, emphasizing the challenge of phase quantization. Initially, we elucidate RIS principles and the significance of precise phase control for wavefront manipulation. Mathematical models are developed, accounting for incident wave direction, desired beam patterns, and phase resolution first in ID and then in 2D scenarios. The study addresses a critical issue: the appearance of undesired quantization lobes due to phase quantization. To mitigate this, a novel strategy employing random phase delays is introduced, dispersing lobes across the beam pattern. In conclusion, this paper offers a thorough investigation of RIS, introducing an innovative approach to alleviate quantization lobe effects on communication performance.

articleTitle: Planar Slot Antenna Array Based On Spoof Surface Plasmon Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a slot antenna array fed by a spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission line is proposed. The transmission line used to feed the slot array has triangular corrugation on both sides. The proposed planar slot antenna array structure exhibits a frequency scanning characteristic. The antenna operates in the frequency range of 6-10 GHz having fractional bandwidth of 50% with a continuous scanning range of 85° with an average gain of 12 dBi. Presented antenna helps to reduce the overall width of the structure and can be a good candidate for reconfigurable antennas as the active circuit biasing will be on the bottom side and will not disturb the antenna pattern.

articleTitle: Design of Water-cooling Jacket for Multi-stage Depressed Collector of High-power Travelling Wave Tube Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The objective of the water-cooling jacket of Multi-stage depressed collector (MDC) is to continuous extract heat during the aging and testing of the high power helix Travelling Wave Tube (TWT) before packaging. The water-cooling jacket for MDC is design to remove the heat up to 250W in continuous wave (CW) mode operation of the TWT. The inlet water condition like water inlet pressure and temperature, flow rate ware optimized to meet the above design requirements. In this paper author has presented detailed design, thermal-structural analysis of water jacket and computational fluid dynamic (CFD) analysis of water cooling channel. The result of the analysis i.e. maximum temperature is validate with the acceptable temperature limits.

articleTitle: 1-18 GHz Low Insertion Loss, High P1dB and High Isolation SPDT Switch With Integrated on Chip Driver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of ultra-broadband 1-18 GHz low insertion loss, high P1dB, and high isolation single pole double throw (SPDT) switch with an integrated on-chip driver. In this work, the requirement of a conventional SPDT switch of high control voltage 0/-20V is replaced by -5V/-2.5V. Also, two series elements are cascaded to mitigate the effect of high C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> of large devices. The reported switch shows insertion loss better than 1dB, a P1dB compression point greater than 44.5 dBm, and isolation better than 50 dB in the entire band. The designed SPDT switch covers a chip area of 2 x 1 mm$^{2}$.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 25 kW(CW) Millimeter Wave Source with External Waveguide Mode Converters for Advance Material Heating/Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of millimeter wave source of 28 GHz frequency with 25 kW RF output power is discussed here. Also the design of waveguide mode converters (rippled wall, serpentine and corrugated) to convert the operating mode into Gaussian mode is discussed. The design of the millimeter wave source and transmission system is performed considering its potential applications in the precision heating and high-quality processing of the different materials of low loss factor. The commercial as well as indigenously developed design codes of beam-wave interaction and beam trajectory analysis are implemented in the design and analysis of the device.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band, Polarization Insensitive Rectifying Surface for RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual-band polarization-insensitive metasurface array-based RF energy harvester is presented in this paper. The unit cell of the metasurface consists of an X-shaped and four Dshaped slotted resonators. 4 Schottky diodes (BAT15-03WL) are embedded in the rectifying surface. A simultaneous impedance matching between free space and rectifying surface (metasurface + rectifier diodes) is achieved at 3.035 GHz and 6.885 GHz. The unit cells are connected with thin highly inductive microstrip lines to collect DC voltage. The proposed RF energy harvester offers more than 95% absorption efficiency for different angles of polarization and up to 80% absorption efficiency for wide angles of incidence at both the designated bands. The proposed harvester can harvest energy from the 3.035 GHz and 6.885 GHz frequency bands.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of BiCMOS SiGe PA for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes effect of different circuit parameters and matching network losses on SiGe power amplifier for mm-Wave application. To proof the efficacy of the study on effect of various parameters, a differential cascode power amplifier (PA) is implemented in GLOBALFOUNDRIES 130nm BiCMOS process at 28GHz. The design shows that the PA can achieve 24dBm output power with 38% peak efficiency at 28GHz. The PA also shows good performance at 3 dB and 6 dB back-off which makes it suitable for mm-Wave application.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed, Spanner-shaped Compact Antenna for Ultra-wideband and V2X Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Spanner-shaped antenna that covers the sub-6 GHz 5G range and operates between 3.59 GHz and 18.78 GHz is described in this article. It includes a circular patch with a Spanner-shaped modification, microstrip line feed, and coplanar ground planes. It features dimensions of $20 \times 26$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, fractional bandwidth of 135.8%, quasi-stable radiation patterns, peak realized gain of 6 dBi, efficiency near 90%, and an excellent Bandwidth-to-Dimension Ratio (BDR) 1827. This proposed antenna betters the previously described designs in terms of broader bandwidth, compact dimensions, high BDR, peak gain, and size compactness. This design is a good fit for modern ultra-wideband and V2X applications.

articleTitle: Precision Thin Film Metallization for Space-borne SAW Narrow Band Pass Filters using E-Beam Evaporation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) filters provide an efficient and compact means of narrow band channelization in Satellite Communication payloads. The efficiency of this narrow band filtering is critically dependent on temperature and fabrication induced frequency shifts in the filter centre frequency. The temperature induced drifts can be minimized by the choice of a suitable piezoelectric substrate. However, tolerances associated with the fabrication processes, especially the thin film metallization thickness, can have a deleterious effect on the repeatability and accuracy of the centre frequency. Here, we present results demonstrating a reliable and repeatable fabrication process for SAW narrow band pass filter (BPF) development. We have achieved precise thickness tolerance of 1% for NiCr/Al metallization, using e-beam evaporation. The thickness characterization is conducted using stylus profilometer and X-ray reflectivity (XRR) measurement, using high resolution x-ray diffraction (HRXRD) system. We have showcased that a change of just ±120 Å in the metal thickness, about the nominal value, leads to a deviation of approximately ∓ 146 kHz in the centre frequency of a UHF SAW filter. Process details to minimize the metallization thickness tolerance are discussed and the ensuing benefits in achieving the desired centre frequency is presented through fabrication and measurement.

articleTitle: Design and Surface Impedance Characterization of Orthogonally Discrete 2 bit Coded Impedance Modulated Surface For Holographic Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, an orthogonally discretized 2 bit coded both inductive and capacitive based meta unit-cell loaded impedance modulated metasurface is proposed for holographic beamforming applications. Using Tensor Surface Impedance Matrix (TSIM) analysis we characterize the equivalent surface impedance for each unit-cell variation to make an effective nonhomogeneous characterization. Periodic boundary condition under PML setup has been used to create the dispersion relation for each orthogonally discretized unit-cell. A K-Map based 2 bit coded $3.5 \lambda_{0} \times 3.5 \lambda_{0}$ (in mm) impedance modulated metasurface is proposed in this work. To incorporate the holographic behavior into the proposed impedance modulated surface, an extended monopole is fed at one of the corners on the surface. An observation is made that by simulating the surface within $f_{r} \in(10 \mathrm{GHz}-11.25 \mathrm{GHz})$, a high SLL reduction has occurred. Finally, a highly directive single beam is achieved at $\boldsymbol{\theta}=55^{\circ}$ and $\phi=45^{\circ}$ with a maximum realized gain of $12.85 \mathrm{~dB}$. Simulated $S_{11}, 2 \mathrm{D}$ and 3D gain patterns are illustrated in this article.

articleTitle: Wideband Fully Metallic Fabry Perot Cavity Antenna with a Curved Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband FPCA with fully metallic construction using a curved ground plane. A metallic construction is quite favourable for high power space applications. By curving the ground plane, a variable resonance cavity height is realized. That results in a wider 3dB Gain-Bandwidth of 19% as compared to 9.2% for a traditional flat ground plane. A very low sacrifice in maximum gain, a mere 0.48dB is traded against this increase in the bandwidth. Impacts on Gain-Bandwidth by different degrees of ground plane curvatures are also presented.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Reflective SP4T Switch Using MMIC Discrete Components’ Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes about various issues and challenges in the design and development of small signal ultra wide band multi-way switch. In this discrete topology, AlGaAs PIN diode based MMICs are used as the basic element. Seriesshunt topology is used for this 1-18 GHz SP4T switch as it achieves better performance in insertion loss, VSWR and isolation characteristics as well. The entire simulation is carried out in ADS software starting from schematic level simulation, passive layout simulation and ‘layout alike’ schematic with discrete components. Its driver circuit is designed using ORCAD software. The driver circuit uses the driver IC to control switching, driver and diode combination is considered. In this topology, driver IC, diode and resistor combinations are used with positive and negative supplies. The whole DC board is simulated in ORCAD. In parallel, driver is also simulated in ADS and both the simulated data has been found to be satisfactory. Final mechanical housing to package the switch done in solid works.

articleTitle: Fully Metallic Metamaterial Polarizer with 3D Printed Circular Polarised Pyramidal Horn Antenna for Millimetre Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a 3D-printed circular polarized pyramidal horn antenna based on a multi-layer, fully metallic, Frequency selective metasurface polarizer for millimeter-wave applications. The proposed polarizer consists of three alike metallic screens with periodically perforated cross and rectangular slots. the polarizer is placed at the top of the 3D-printed pyramidal horn antenna and simulated using a CST microwave solver. The designed antenna is found to operate from 29.9 GHz to 30.3 GHz with broadside realized gain of 19.3 dBi. The axial ratio bandwidth of 400 MHz and maximum realized gain reduction of 0.5 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Antenna Array on 3D Printed PLA Substrate with Fractal Ground
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discuss the effect of two dissimilar fractal geometry loaded on ground plane of an antenna array on a 3D printed PLA substrate. The miniaturised 3D printed 1 X2 antenna array is realized for ISM band with operating frequency at 2. 4GHz. Polylactic acid (PLA) a biodegradable material is used to prepare a 3D printed substrate, whose RF characterization study is carried out by ring resonator method. Two different fractal geometry have been employed on ground plane so as to shift the resonance frequency of an initial microstrip antenna array from 3.8 GHz to 2.4 GHz thereby reducing the size. Concentric ring fractal geometry and rectangle embedded circle fractal geometries are utilized in the design of antenna array. Simulation of the design is analyzed using Ansys-HFSS tool. 33.08% reduction in the dimension of antenna array is achieved. The matching of simulation and measurement results validates the presented design.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Loop Based Polarization Dependent/ Independent Reflectors for Microwave Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents performance analysis of Frequency selective reflecting surfaces (FSSs) based on rectangular, elliptical and rhombic loop unit elements respectively. Two orthogonally oriented configurations of polarization dependent (PD) arrays of rectangular loop, elliptical loop and rhombic loops are designed and their transmission characteristics under normal electromagnetic (EM) wave incidence are studied for comparison. These orthogonal PD arrays are first cascaded on both sides of the dielectric substrate as back-to-back (BTB) configurations and then merged and patterned on same side of the substrate. The transmission responses of both BTB and merged FSSs configurations are studied and compared. Later, all these FSSs are evaluated under oblique EM incidences. Although all FSSs maintain stable response even under oblique incidence in the microwave frequency bands, rectangular loop based FSSs provide excellent stability in their transmission responses. Merged FSSs outperform PD and BTB FSSs in the form of bandwidths (BWs) over which angular stable (AS) and polarization independent (PI) transmission responses are preserved. Merged rectangular loop (MRECT) FSS and Merged elliptical loop (MELIP) FSS remain AS and PI over 2.67 GHz and 1.65 GHz wide frequency bands respectively while Merged rhombic loop (MRL) FSS preserves AS and PI over 0.57 GHz wide frequency band.

articleTitle: Beam-forming of a Linear Antenna Array Using Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a 4-element linearly polarized antenna array incorporated with a reconfigurable frequency selective surface is proposed for the beam-forming applications. The antenna structure comprises $1 \times 4$ linearly polarized radiating elements, which is fed by a power dividing circuit and a coaxial fed connector. A reconfigurable FSS superstrate is mounted on the top of the antenna array to exploit the beam-forming capability of the proposed design. The reconfigurable FSS embodies $6 \times 6$ unit cells arrangement, each having dimension of $0.36 \lambda_{0} \times 0.36 \lambda_{0}$. The reconfigurable FSS superstrate layer is again splitted into two segments to obtain the desired beam-forming. The unit cell is made reconfigurable by employing PIN diodes in its vertical arms. The over all dimension of the antenna structure is $2.4 \lambda_{0} \times 2.4 \lambda_{0} \times 0.47 \lambda_{0}$. The proposed structure can generate three radiating beams, when the reconfigurable FSS is illuminated by the electromagnetic radiation generated by the antenna array. The reconfigurable FSS superstrate is biased accordingly to obtain all three radiation beams. The proposed design provide a maximum realized gain of 10.7dBi and beam tilt of ± 48° at the operating frequency of 5.5 GHz.

articleTitle: T-Slot Patch Antenna Design for 5G Applications in Sub-6 GHz Band with Radome Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact dual-polarized patch antenna designed specifically for Sub-6 GHz 5G base station arrays. The antenna’s compactness is achieved through a T-slot patch design, and it features a unique feeding structure with connecting vias. By incorporating a reflector with side walls, the antenna’s directivity and port isolation are enhanced. The study also includes an investigation into radome effects, revealing how material and placement height impact antenna performance. This antenna supports simultaneous transmission and reception in two polarizations, ensuring effective signal propagation. With a wide bandwidth of about 0.44 GHz and a high gain of around 7.6 dB, it provides reliable connectivity for Sub-6 GHz 5G networks.

articleTitle: Hexagonal Shaped Metamaterial MIMO Patch Antenna for WiFi Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A four-port Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna system operating in the Wireless communication band (2.4 GHz) in 0.8mm (0.013$\lambda$) separation is presented in this work. All the four antennas are designed as inset-fed microstrip square patch antenna with slight chamfering at the radiating edges to improve isolation. The elements of MIMO structure are placed in the substrate with 0.584$\lambda$ X 0.584$\lambda$. The MIMO design is simulated through CST providing a potential bandwidth of 80 MHz with a gain of 5.2 dBi and high isolation of 37 dB. For isolation between the patch elements 3-sets of hexagonal shaped Complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) structure is placed near radiating edge in each patch. CSRR meta material gives the additional isolation of 17 dB. Comparison of Fabricated and simulated results for S-parameters and radiation pattern also presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bit-transformation of a multi-bit QR Code Based RFID and Barcode based RFID with Improved Read Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Chipless RFID has flourished in a new age of technological development in the realm of IoT and sensor applications. The primary factor driving the growth of RFID technology is its relative affordability and printing flexibility. Additionally, this system has user-friendly bit storing and bit transformation capabilities. Chipless RFID can also function as a passive sensor due to its diverse RF properties. In this work, a QR code and bar code based resonator is proposed to enhance the read range capability. The QR code resonator patch is made up of a number of small copper rectangular and square boxes of different dimensions and arranged over a FR4 substrate, similarly the number of calculated bars of copper is also fabricated. The backscattered signal is considered to be the radar cross section (RCS), which is obtained with three peaks for both the QR code and barcode based resonator. The bit density and bit capacity can also be calculated in order to demonstrate the tag’s originality. This QR code tag resonates at 2.48 GHz, 3.04 GHz and 4.03 GHz and bar code based resonator resonates at 2.6 GHz,4.3 GHz, 5.2 GHz, 6.2 GHz for with the definite current distribution.

articleTitle: Magnet-less Circulator with Bulk Acoustic Wave Filter Delay Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Recent applications like quantum computing and in-band full duplex communication systems demand non-reciprocal components that are magnet-less, integrable, linear, and compact. This resulted in a lot of research interest in time variance based non-reciprocity. This paper reports the design and measurement of a four port non-reciprocal circulator using sequentially switched delay line (SSDL) elements. Bulk Acoustic Wave (BAW) filters are used as the time delay elements as they exhibit High-Quality factors, which resulted in a reduction in the modulation frequency compared to the previous LC demonstrations. The switching action of Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) switches is synchronized with the delay of the BAW filters to route the electromagnetic signal to the desired port, without using a magnet. The commercial off-the-shelf BAW filters and SPDT switches are integrated on a Printed Circuit Board (PCB) and measured the S - parameter responses. The proposed circulator shows broad low insertion loss (IL) of 6 dB, and high isolation (IX) around 31 dB at 2.59 GHz with a BW of 60 MHz.

articleTitle: Realization of substrate integrated waveguide filter for high frequency satcom applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 4-pole Ka-band chebychev band pass filter based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is designed and developed. Effect of surface roughness of the copper cladding on RT5880 is simulated. The sensitivity analysis for the important filter parameter is performed for its realization at Ka-band. 3D EM simulation of the filter and measurement results are presented and discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Element MIMO Antenna for Wearable WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The relentless advancement of wireless communication technology has spurred the development of Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs), ushering in a new era of personalized healthcare, fitness monitoring, and wearable technology. In the context of WBANs, the demand for efficient, reliable, and seamless communication between wearable devices has grown exponentially. However, these devices often face challenges related to wireless communication, such as limited range, interference, and signal degradation. To overcome these obstacles and enhance the communication capabilities of wearable devices, the integration of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna technology has garnered significant attention. In this present a dual element MIMO antenna design for wearable WBAN application at frequency of 2.45GHz. Different simulation analysis of presented antenna is done with four layer (bone, muscle, fat and skin) human tissue model for on and off body wearable WBAN application.

articleTitle: Study of variation in Insertion Loss and Isolation on Indigenous GaN HEMT Switch as a function of Device Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: RF switch is an integral part of front end of T/R module. RF characterization plays a critical role in the development of these switches. In the present paper RF characterization and performance analysis of indigenously developed GaN HEMT based RF switch has been discussed. In these switches, GaN HEMT device acts as ON and OFF switch depending upon the DC control voltage applied to the device. Extensive measurement has been carried out over indigenously developed GaN HEMT for different geometry of devices. Variation of performance parameters i.e. Insertion loss and Isolation as a function of device geometry has been analyzed. This extensive analysis of GaN HEMT devices with varying geometries, ascertains the relationship between device geometry and performance.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Dual Gridded Reflector with Trifurcated Feed Horn
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports the design of wideband (1.9:1) contoured beam Dual Gridded Reflector antenna at C-band. Single antenna system is working over normal & upper extended C-transmit & C-receive bands. Compact Trifurcated feed horn design and analysis with good cross polarization characteristics over the complete band described. Analyzed cross polarization of the feed is less than -34 dB over the full band. Dual Gridded reflector antenna analyzed results at C-Transmit & C-Receive bands presented. Full wave analysis of Grid based on Floquet Mode theory for plane wave incidence described. Analyzed Edge of Coverage Gain is better than 27.5 dBi at C-Tx band, 27 dBi at C-Rx band for both front and rear reflectors. Analyzed cross polarization isolation is less than -30 dB over the coverage region for both front & rear reflectors across the frequency band.

articleTitle: A Fast Optimization Scheme of Antenna Arrays using the Multi-Objective Pareto Front
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study offers a method for efficiently estimating the radiation characteristics of an antenna system by utilizing the scattering matrix of it. The system includes a set of radiating elements and some probes placed at regular intervals, which helps in reconstructing the S-matrix, ultimately helping in such an estimation. Subsequently, a test case is analyzed for optimizing the radiated fields using the multi-objective Pareto front for the best trade-off.

articleTitle: Analysis of Pseudospark-Driven Electron Beam Generation and Its Propagation Inside High-Power THz BWO
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a simulation study has been carried out to analyze the pseudospark (PS)-driven electron beam generation and propagation inside a plasma-assisted, high-power THz backward wave oscillator (BWO), using particle-incell (PIC) simulation software, OOPIC Pro. The PS-driven electron beam is generated inside a plasma cathode electron (PCE) gun and results in the production of a highly energetic electron beam possessing high current density. The beam propagation takes place inside the drift space of the W-band staggered double vane THz wave interaction structure, suitable for the generation of 0.1 THz radiation. Analysis of beam generation and propagation is necessary for the optimization of the parameters affecting the generation of high-power THz radiation. These parameters comprise the applied gap voltage (V) on the PCE gun, gas pressure (P) inside the PCE gun and interaction structure, and the beam current (I) of the emitted beam inside the interaction structure. In this paper, a study has been performed to analyze the effect of these parameters on PS-driven electron beam generation and propagation at applied gap voltage of 20 and 30 kV, gas pressure ranging from 1 to 20 Pa, and beam current ranging from 1 to 20 A.

articleTitle: Enhancing Satellite System Reliability through Bistable RF MEMS Switch: An Optimization Approach using XGBoost model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radio Frequency Micro Electro Mechanical System (RF MEMS) switches offer unparalleled reliability and swift response times with compact design, making them an ideal choice for ensuring faultless redundancy in critical satellite systems. This paper proposes a Crab leg Bistable RF MEMS switch to perform redundancy functions in satellite applications. To optimize the proposed switch, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model is presented, which is proven to be an efficient Machine Learning (ML) model. The proposed XGBoost model was developed based on both direct and indirect approaches to determine the RF and physical characteristics in both stable states of the switch. The XGBoost model overcomes the time-consuming EM optimization problem. In this work, the proposed model aims to significantly reduce the duration required for designing the switch. In comparison to the Electro-Magnetic (EM) simulator, which demands nearly 50 minutes for each iteration, the proposed model reduces the design time by 90%. The effectiveness of the developed ML model is validated by comparing predicted results with those obtained from the HFSS model, resulting in the achievement of favorable convergence.

articleTitle: Design of Multiband FSS-Radome for Shared Aperture Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel frequency selective surface structure (FSS) embedded Radome is proposed for multiband operation, which exhibits angular stability and polarization independence. The proposed FSS uses a combination of different patch-type elements in two cascaded layers, forming a thin design that is suitable for aerospace applications. It operates in the frequency bands, S, C, and X with low transmission loss (< −0.5 dB) and excellent isolation (<−20 dB) between each passband. The proposed FSS-radome exhibits angular stability up to 60° for both TE and TM polarizations. Further, a prototype has been fabricated and tested for proof-of-the-concept. The simulated results found to be in good agreement with the measured results. The proposed FSS-embedded Radome can be used to for shared aperture antennas employed for aerospace applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Semi-Circular Finger Shaped Antenna with Metamaterial Loaded Ground for Brain Tumor Detection and Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this communication, an innovative finger shaped antenna with unidirectional radiation pattern resonating at 2.8 GHz in free space and having an operational bandwidth of 0.6 GHz for Tumor detection and localization system is proposed. The reported design has minimal footprint area of $28\times 28\times 0.75$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and showcases the remarkable results. The prospective antenna is designed on a Rogers TMM 4 substrate with the relative permittivity of 4.5 and utilizes a partial ground plane measuring 6 mm in length to expand the bandwidth and achieve the desired operational frequency. The humanoid head phantom comprising of 6 layers (brain, CSF, dura, skull, fat and skin) and the tumor, which possesses various physical and electromagnetic characteristics is designed within the HFSS. The detection of tumor in brain is done by analyzing the difference in scattering parameters for healthy and diseased tissue. However, the localization and sizing of the tumor is done by extracting the phase and magnitude of the electric field rather than utilizing complex imaging algorithms saving critical resources. Furthermore, the antenna’s Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) for a regular head phantom and a phantom with a tumor is measured at 0.16779 W/Kg and 0.206 W/kg correspondingly, while these values are lesser than the average SAR of 2 W/kg.

articleTitle: High Gain Wideband Dual Circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna for GNSS Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the design and development of high gain wideband dual circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna for GNSS Reflectometry application is presented. The proposed antenna comprises electromagnetically coupled stacked patch (EMCP) configuration with hybrid quadrature coupler to generate dual circular polarization. The antenna has been developed and characterized. The measured gain of the antenna is better than 8.5 dBi for both the polarization. It has 29.8 percent and 30.4 percent measured 10 dB return loss and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth respectively. The antenna is used as a nadir looking antenna in GNSS receiver for Reflectometry applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Differential Spacecraft Charging Using Suprathermal GEO Plasma Particles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the method to analyze the differential spacecraft charging using q-non extensive Tsallis distribution to take into account the higher energy tails of suprathermal GEO space plasma particles. The work involves plasma modelling considering different types of primary and secondary plasma particles, deriving current valence equations on the spacecraft bodies. Different current densities are obtained using Tsallis non extensive q-distribution. The temporal built-up spacecraft potential is obtained by solving the differential equation derived from current balance equation and spacecraft potential and the capacitance of the spacecraft body. Capacitance computation has been carried out using Fast Multipole Method accelerated GMRES (Generalized Minimal Residual) method which is capable of solving matrix multiplication in linear time complexity of O(N). The result present analysis has been compared with Maxwellian distribution.

articleTitle: A New Surface-Shaping Technique Based on Parametric Irregular-Point Cluster for Contoured-Beam Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new surface shaping method for contoured beam reflector antenna has presented in this paper. The shaping technique has based on tabulated surface of parameterized irregular point cluster. User selectable fifth order polynomial or linear interpolation has used between any two points. Thus, this technique is different from conventional spline and zernike surface shaping method. Any point in tabulated surface has defined by variables. The variables have optimized as per specified radio frequency (RF) goal. Matlab Code has developed to generate parametrized tabulated surface and corresponding variables for optimization using Ticra Tool software. This surface shaping technique afford additional flexibility to achieve stringent RF Goal for contoured beam antenna. Two cases of reflector shaping have presented. In first case, surface shaping using linear interpolation for faceted mesh reflector antenna. In second case, surface shaping using smooth shaping using fifth order polynomial interpolation for solid composite reflector antenna. The results from 3D Periodic method of moments (pMoM) method for 2.5m Ku-Band shaped mesh reflector antenna is agreeing well with results from Physical Optics and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PO and PTD) method.

articleTitle: Microstrip Leaky Wave Antenna with Constant & High Gain and High-Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a microstrip leaky wave antenna (MLWA) aimed at achieving constant and high gain with high efficiency across the X band with only 8 unit cells in the structure. The investigation extends to the introduction of slots in the feeding line to evaluate their impact on antenna parameters. The findings demonstrate that the inclusion of slots leads to a slight increase in gain with a maximum Peak Realized Gain of 17.3 dBi and expands the −10 dB impedance bandwidth. Moreover, the presence of slots reduces the grading lobe level as well. Moreover, this antenna is continuously scanning from backwards to forward direction, allowing for a wider scanning range without encountering an open stop band from +40° to −16°. The proposed MLWA configuration exhibits improved performance characteristics, positioning it as a promising solution for diverse wireless communication and radar applications.

articleTitle: Dual-Circularly Polarized Microstrip Flat Panel Antenna Array for SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Compact Flat Panel 8× 8 antenna array for dual-circular polarization at S-band with highly portable characteristics is presented in this paper. A 4-layer microstrip antenna configuration is proposed to achieve dual-circular polarization. The design uses a circular patch antenna that resonates at the S-band, where the aperture coupling excites the antenna element. Dual-excitation technique employed to achieve dual-circular polarization and a parasitic patch used to improve the axial ratio bandwidth. A tile of 4× 4 array configuration designed with an integrated power divider. A 4-tile configuration proposed to achieve a gain of 21 dBic, while restricting the axial ratio less than 2 dB, the Side Lobe Level (SLL) at nearly 12.5 dBic for both Left Hand Circular Polarization (LHCP) and Right Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP). The dual-circular polarization configuration achieves high isolation of -60dB. The proposed antenna fabricated and validated through measurements. The measured results shows a good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: RadarSleepNet: Sleep Pose Classification via PointNet++ and 5D Radar Point Clouds
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Understanding sleep patterns and postures is critical for assessing overall well-being. However, traditional sleep analysis methods are often limited in their practicality due to invasive devices or complex configurations. In this study, we introduce RadarSleepNet, a non-intrusive 60 GHz Frequency-modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar-based system for sleep posture monitoring that accurately infers sleep postures without compromising privacy or comfort, even in low-light conditions. Our system combines a SincNet classifier and a PointNet++ sleep pose estimation model, achieving remarkable class accuracy for each sleep posture: 98.43% for supine, 98.01% for side (chest facing radar), 97.22% for prone, and 95.72% for side (back facing radar). This demonstrates its effectiveness in accurately classifying sleep postures. This innovation offers significant potential in healthcare, providing insights into disease management and improving individual health understanding.

articleTitle: Intrinsic Isolation in SIW-based MIMO Antenna for 5G mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact, low profile two port wideband Multiple input Multiple output (MIMO) antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) functioning is proposed for millimeterWave (mmWave) applications. The structure includes two elliptical shaped patch radiators responsible for wide bandwidth, positioned side by side. For better impedance matching, each antenna element is fed by a steeped impedance transmission line. This antenna is unique as it exploits MIMO technology with SIW benefits in order to improve isolation as well as quality of transmission. According to simulated results, the proposed MIMO antenna can cover the n259band of the mmWave. Maximum isolation between ports is 22 dB without any additional isolation structure, and the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) in the band of interest is less than 0.02. The proposed antenna may be used for small portable devices defined for mmWave communication in 5GNR networks.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Linearized Channel Amplifier (LCAMP) at S-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes Design, Development and Realization of Linearized Channel Amplifier (LCAMP) at Sband (Centre Frequency: 2067 MHz, Bandwidth: 85 MHz) for SATCOM applications. LCAMP consists of Linearizer and Channel Amplifier Sections integrated in a single RF Chain, unlike standalone linearizers. LCAMP provides tunable Gain and Phase expansion capability of up to 6 dB and 45° respectively, with a small signal gain of 55 dB. LCAMP operates in both Fixed Gain Mode (FGM) and Automatic Level Control (ALC) Mode with a wide input dynamic range of 20dB with peak to peak output power variation less than 0.4 dB. LCAMP is equipped with telecommandable digital attenuators to set Gain, Output Power and provide RF muting capability. FPGA based digital controller section is used to realize ALC functionality and constant gain over temperature. Gain variation of 0.4 dB is achieved over a temperature range of -10 to 60°C.

articleTitle: X-Band GaN Power Amplifier for Weather Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design methodology and simulation results of an X-band power amplifier (PA) developed for weather radar applications. The primary goal of the PA design was to achieve both a high output power (Pout) and a high power added efficiency (PAE) for the entire X-band using a commercially available 150-nm gate length GaN on SiC technology. This paper also presents the impact of harmonic tuning in designing high-efficiency PAs. A single-stage class-F mode PA was designed for X-band using waveform shaping multi-resonance harmonic matching circuit. The PA achieves 44-48% PAE, 35-36dBm output power, and 10-11dB gain across an 8-12 GHz frequency range with a layout area of 0.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A two-stage design, which incorporates harmonic tuning of the load and source impedance, achieves 45-55% PAE, 40-41 dBm output power, and 16-17dB gain across an 8-12 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: RF Characterization of Xilinx RFSoC XCZU28DR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Its needless to say that RFSoC provides shot in the arm for the field of cognitive signal processing and software defined radio which thrives on adaptability and optimally balancing the mutually contradicting requirements of processing capabilities, power consumption and multi-channel density. This RF-to-digital block is also useful for miniaturization with low data latency which otherwise would be a huge challenge in traditional multi-chip architectures. The RF Data Converter (RFDC) block, containing both DACs and ADCs, is the USP in this Xilinx introduced RFSoC which needs to be evaluated for its RF performance for it to be an effective replacement of the currently existing standalone DACs and ADCs as daughter boards. This paper deals with the RF characterization of the RFDC block of Xilinx RFSoC device XCZU28DR-2FFVG1517E by configuring it using a block design, simulating it on vivado simulator, deploying it on ZCU111 evaluation board and finally capturing the generated waveforms.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design of Planar Ablatable Radome Using Inhomogeneous Planar Layer Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radome in a high-velocity airborne platform experiences a steep ascent in temperature, affecting its electromagnetic performance. This paper uses the inhomogeneous planar layer model to design a novel radome wall and analyze its performance under dynamic temperature ranges. The model considers the dielectric wall a combination of several layers with different dielectric properties to account for the variation in temperature along thickness of the radome. Outer coating of ablative material is provided to protect the radome wall experiencing elevated temperature levels for high-speed airborne applications. To overcome the issue of total internal reflection at higher angles of incidence, an additional layer of the same ablative material is applied to the inside of the radome wall. Power transmission coefficient, insertion phase delay and power reflection coefficient are calculated using the equivalent transmission line method. The performance of the resulting radome wall is compared with that of the monolithic radome wall designed at a constant temperature.

articleTitle: SIW-based Hexagonal Slot MIMO Antenna Array for 28 GHz Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based MIMO antenna array operating at 28 GHz, intended for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) wireless applications. The design entails a hexagonal slot etched into the upper layer of the SIW cavity. Through meticulous optimization of different parameters (the slot’s dimensions and its placement within the SIW cavity), a broadside radiation pattern is resulted featuring an impedance bandwidth of 370 MHz (from 27.82 GHz to 28.19 GHz) centered around 28 GHz and a peak gain of 6.10 dBi. To further improve the antenna’s performance, a 1$\times$2 antenna array is devised, accompanied by an SIW feed network. This array geometry yields a maximum gain of 8.28 dBi and an impedance bandwidth spanning 0.87 GHz (from 27.59 GHz to 28.46 GHz). To further enhance channel capacity, a $1 \times 4$ MIMO array is formulated by extending the antenna array. Thus the proposed structure encompasses several notable attributes including large operating gain, and good channel capacity, along with commendable efficiency, and minimal cross-polarization, thereby rendering it well-suited for mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Algorithm Inspired Binary Sequence based Fault Detection in Uniformly Excited Linear Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This Present article proposes a hybrid technique of fault finding in uniformly excited linear antenna array with improved execution time. In this technique differential evolution algorithm has been used to approximate the faulty behavior of uniformly excited linear antenna array. After anticipating the approximate behavior, binary sequence based method has been developed facilitating identification of faulty elements in the linear antenna array. Effectiveness of the method has been demonstrated through fault instances in 26 elements uniformly excited linear antenna array of isotropic radiators.

articleTitle: Compact 5-18 GHz Vivaldi-Like Antenna for Airborne EW Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact Vivaldi-like antenna operating in the frequency range of 5-18 GHz to be used for Airborne EW phased array applications is presented in this paper. A planar 1D array of 8 identical elements and a power combining network to feed the array are also reported. Performance of the radiator in terms of reflection coefficient, radiation efficiency, gain, and radiation pattern are reported while the S- are reported parameters in case of power combining array. The proposed solution is compact and has a stable radiation pattern over the entire operating frequency range. It could be a better candidate for airborne EW and surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Symmetrical Beam Pattern Generation of Open-ended Waveguide with Enhanced Gain using an Elliptical Dielectric Sandwiched Groundplane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper uses a standard WR28 open-ended waveguide (OEWG) antenna to generate a symmetrical beam pattern with improved gain. An elliptical ground plane consisting of a dielectric substrate sandwiched between two conducting layers is placed at the open-end side of the OEWG to improve the gain, and later elliptical slots are etched to expose the dielectric substrate. The introduction of an elliptical ground plane has enhanced the gain of OEWG from 5.69 dBi to 8.86 dBi. Later, an elliptical slot was introduced to expose the hidden substrate, which helped to generate a symmetrical beam in the range of $-45^{\circ}\leq\theta\leq 45^{\circ}$. Finally, an edge modification along the E-plane helped generate a symmetrical beam pattern in the range of $-90^{\circ}\leq\theta\leq 90^{\circ}$. Ansys HFSS full-wave simulator is used to carry out the optimization and simulations.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Band Metamaterial Absorber Based on Resistive Sheet for L to Ku Band Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, the design of an ultra-wideband polarization-insensitive metamaterial absorber for L-band to Ku-band frequency application is investigated. The Unit cell of the metamaterial absorber consists of two ohmic sheet layers, in which one ohmic sheet of square shape is sandwiched between two thin substrates and another ohmic sheet of square shape is placed on the top of dielectric substrate. Due to its four-fold symmetry, the design yields polarization-insensitive characteristics in the desired band. More than 90% absorptivity from 1 GHz to 15 GHz has wide fractional bandwidth of 175% concerning the center frequency. The unit cell structure has a peak absorptivity of 98.6% at 2.24 GHz. The proposed structure has more than 90% absorption in both TE and TM modes at normal incidence. The structure also provides more than 80% wide absorption at incident angle up to $\theta =45^{\circ}$ for both TE and TM modes. Ultra-wideband response of the absorber with polarization-insensitive makes it commercially suitable for applications ranging from L Band to Ku Band.

articleTitle: Broadband Tunable and Angularly Stable Circular Polarization Conversion in THz-Gap using Graphene Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact $(\sim \lambda / 10.91)$ transmittive-type graphene metasurface with a thickness of $\sim \lambda / 6.59$ has been explored in this paper. Two thin identical shaped graphene patterns have been deposited on the two opposite sides of a polyimide substrate in such a way that the incident linearly polarized (LP) electromagnetic wave (EM) gets converted to its circularly polarized (CP) form while passing through it. The device has achieved a considerable 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 0.51 THz from 2.79 THz to 3.3 THz. The circular polarization state of the transmitted electromagnetic wave has been validated by calculating the Stoke’s parameters as well as from the study of electric field profile. The device offers broadband tunable characteristics under proper biasing conditions. It can also provide a stable 3-dB axial ratio (AR) performance under different oblique incidences of the EM wave till 60°.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive and Wide-Incident Angle Stability Wideband Absorber Based on Resistive film for S and C bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The absorptivity is more than 90% from 2.41 to 8.47 GHz with an absorption bandwidth is 6.06 GHz and fractional bandwidth is 111.39%. The unit size and thickness of the proposed structure are $0.120 \lambda_{L}$ and $0.078 \lambda_{L}$. The absorptivity of the proposed structure is constant above 90% at different polarization angles under normal incident angle due to the symmetric structure. So, it is polarization insensitive. The absorptivity of the proposed structure is above 80% upto angle 50° under an oblique angle. The proposed structure normalized input impedance for impedance matching theory was calculated using $S_{11}$ values. Explain the electric field and equivalent circuit model to better understanding the absorption mechanism. Compare the proposed structure with the previous absorber in terms of unit size, thickness and fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Measurement Issue Debugging for HDMI2.1 CRLS Topology: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) design and measurement scenario corresponding to one of the high-speed interfaces is considered in this work. The design and measurement corresponding to HDMI 2.1 interface with fixed rate link (FRL) mode is reported, where each lane operates at 10Gbps with total bandwidth of 4lanes @10Gbps each for 4K (60/120Hz) performance. A full design of experiment (DoE) is carried out with IBIS-AMI model for Tx and specification-based Rx, connector & cable models, to comply with the requisite eye mask level for 1e-10 BER. The targeted eye mask level is analytically determined using the HDMI Compliance Test Specification (CTS). The simulated eye height and width are then compared with specification target (HFR1-7 Data Eye Mask Test) values. The fabricated board is also tested for HFR17 during the post silicon electrical validation (EV). It is observed that few of the samples has marginal eye mask violation that was not observed in the simulation. A step-by-step investigation is carried out to find the root cause with minimum false conditioning. The major findings associated with the test case measurements are discussed here to emphasize the possible source of degradation in eye margin leads to HFR1-7 test violation.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Antenna Array Based Pancreatic Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a microwave technique to diagnose pancreatic cancer (PC) through a $2 \times 2$ sequentially rotated circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna array. A pancreatic phantom consisting of pancreas, liver, kidney, spleen, muscle, fat, skin, etc. is used with the antenna array. The operating band of the array lies within the frequency range of 1.5-2.2 GHz. The PC is studied by introduction of tumor in the phantom model of a healthy pancreas. It is observed that the tumor causes a shift in the resonance frequency of the antenna. The parameters of antenna array is studied for the four stages of PC depending upon the tumor size in each stage. The increase in the size of tumor causes an enhancement in reflection, an increase in E/H-field and a decrease in axial ratio of the antenna array. The Specific absorption rate (SAR) for the different stages of PC is below 2 W/Kg for 10g, which is well within the safety limits. The current work provides a simple PC diagnosis technique which is fast, safe, compact, economical, comfortable and non-invasive.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband CRP Antenna for Advanced Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this research article, the simulated design and fabrication prototype of a wideband Complementary Split-Ring-Resonator Rectangular Patch (CRP) antenna with partially Ground Plane (GP) is proposed. The size of the proposed design is $30\times 30mm^{2}$ and fabricated using FR$4_{-}$epoxy substrate. The patch includes SRR slots to increase the impedance bandwidth. Proposed antenna is suitable for Airport Surveillance (2.7 GHz - 2.9 GHz), WiMAX applications (3.3 to 3.7 GHz) and further S-band (2-4GHz) satellite and radar applications. It covers the wideband frequency ranging from 2.25 GHz to 4.25 GHz. It achieved the reflection coefficient ($S_{11}$) of -17.822 at 2.45 GHz and -28.75 dB at 4.2 GHz frequency. This design is predominantly concentrated on wideband and compact size. The radiation patterns, gain, bandwidth and VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio) for the simulated antenna and fabricated prototype are all in good agreement with the measured data.

articleTitle: Design of planar antenna array for the generation of near-distance energy hotspots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The theoretical beam efficiency in the far-field, as calculated by the Friis transmission equation, exhibits a considerable decrease within a few wavelengths from the radiating element. Consequently, applications like wireless power transfer and imaging are limited at large distances due to the low efficiency of the beam. To address this challenge, the use of radiating near-fields has been proposed. This work integrates the concept of a phased array antenna on an X-shaped array of patches to generate a desired focal region. The primary aim of this work is to engineer the energy hotspot at a distance well beyond the near-field region of the constituent patch antenna while also encompassing large dimensions in terms of range and cross-range, thereby relaxing the geometrical constraints typically associated with wireless power transfer operations. A frequency-scaled prototype of an 8-element patch array and an isolated element operating at 2.25 GHz has been fabricated and measured, verifying the proposed working principle.

articleTitle: A Novel Parallelogram Shaped Microstrip Fractal Antenna For Home Automation using Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The article proposes a novel parallelogram shaped fractal patch for miniaturization and its possibilities to be explored for microstrip patch antenna and its application in home automation. Without changing the external dimensions of the patch the fractal patch is fully used for miniaturization of the antenna. The perimeter of the parallelogram shaped fractal patch increases, keeping its surface area constant without capitalizing any extra space. The proposed parallelogram shaped fractal patch antenna gives 62.20 % miniaturization in terms of frequency or 67.50 % in terms of size reduction as compared to conventional microstrip patch antenna. The second antenna proposed is made from the first antenna by cutting the antenna into half from the symmetry axis and the frequency miniaturization is 59.04 % with 83.70 % reduction in size as compared to the conventional microstrip patch antenna. The different performance parameters of the antenna like S11/dB, Gain have been analyzed and reported in the article.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of High Isolation 3D CPW-fed MIMO Antenna for Ultra Wide Band applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a non-planer or 3D Co-planer waveg-uide (CPW) fed, four-port multi input multi output (MIMO) antenna for 2-20GHz ultra-wideband (UWB) applications is presented. Firstly, a single rectangular antenna element is designed. After that by arranging four such antenna elements in cubic order, a 3D MIMO antenna is designed. The proposed MIMO antenna design shows good isolation between its ports without using any decoupling structure. The diversity parameters of the designed antennas are evaluated by investigating Envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), Diversity gain (DG), Mean effective gain (MEG) and Total active reflection coefficient (TARC) values and all show satisfactory results for the entire (2-20GHz) band. This proposed 3D MIMO antenna design is suitable for WLAN, sub-6GHz, 5G mid band, radar and satellite applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Reflection & Leakage on Antenna Measurement in Compact Antenna Test Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the impact and mitigation of reflections and leakage on radiation characteristics of antenna characterized in compact antenna test range (CATR). Quietness in terms of amplitude and phase variation of the Quiet Zone (QZ) is very important to qualify an antenna test range. Reflection from chamber walls and leakage from feed & faulty components/ connectors greatly deteriorate the quality of Quiet Zone (QZ) and hence the measured radiation pattern and its associated parameters of AUT. To show the impact of two different situations reflection and RF leakage, we have measured the performance in four different conditions.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Circular Patch Antenna Through Reflective Excitation Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: With the advancement in wireless communication technology towards 5G and higher generations, researchers have invested much efforts towards attaining high bandwidth communication. Bandwidth of a circular patch antenna and its overall performance has been enhanced using a novel reflective technique proposed in this paper. By exciting the patch antenna reflectively through a metallic post connected to an ungrounded coplanar waveguide (CPW) line terminated with a pair of vias attached to the line by a metallic pad, another resonance is generated near the fundamental mode, significantly improving impedance bandwidth. The bandwidth of the proposed radiator is enhanced by 387.7% when compared with that of a probefed circular patch antenna (from 6.61% to 30.11%) using the proposed technique. A radiation efficiency >90% was attained for the antenna structure mentioned in this work. The progress of the proposed design from a conventional circular patch to that of a bandwidth enhanced patch is also discussed.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Waveguide Singlet With Wide Stopband
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 3-D printed waveguide singlet structure with a wide stopband is proposed for waveguide filters. The proposed structure is made up of two closely spaced, slanted tri-post configurations that are arranged longitudinally in the rectangular waveguide. Furthermore, these slanted tri-post configurations consist of three slanted, equal-height posts arranged transversely. The singlet structure exploits TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">201</inf> as a resonating mode and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> as a non-resonating bypass coupling. This arrangement produces one pole and a transmission zero (TZ). The position of TZ can be controlled by changing the height and by the slant angles of the posts. Metal 3-D printing is utilized to fabricate the structure due to its ability to build complex slanted profiles easily. The singlet has been built and measured, demonstrating its suitability for the design of highly selective waveguide filters.

articleTitle: Characterization of Reactive Energy Density in the Antenna Near-Field using EM Lagrangian Density
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the use of period-averaged EM Lagrangian density for the efficient frequency-domain characterization of reactive energy density around arbitrary antennas. First, we correlate this period-averaged EM Lagrangian density, a quantity less explored in the antennas and propagation community, with the popular complex Poynting’s theorem. Next, by using full-wave computational EM solver, we plot the 2D spatial maps of EM Lagrangian density in the near-field of a thin-wire V-dipole antenna for different flare angles. Such spatial maps can provide vital insights into the radiation mechanism and near-field structure of generic antennas, by unveiling the capacitive and inductive nature of the non-propagating reactive energy density.

articleTitle: Parameterization of Micro-Milling Process for Fabrication of 0.22 THz Interaction Structure With Improved Surface Roughness and Dimensional Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, an effort has been made to analyze the micro-milling parameters on the development of planar interaction structure suitable for 0.22 THz source with improved surface roughness and dimensional tolerances. The various critical micro-milling parameters like feed rate has been varied between 0.05 mm/min to 1 mm/min, while two types of milling process have been utilized, namely hatching and contour. The spindle speed has also been varied from 10000 rpm to 20000 rpm. The whole set of experiments have been performed using coolant as well as without coolant. The effects of abovementioned variable milling parameters on the development of 0.22 THz planar beam-wave interaction structure have been analyzed using scanning electron microscope (SEM) machine. The experiments have been performed on two different types of vacuum-grade materials namely, OFHC copper and molybdenum.

articleTitle: Compact Microstrip Patch Antenna with slotted patch and parasitic elements for X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact microstrip patch antenna with a slotted patch is presented for X Band Applications. The ground plane is partial in nature and contains three parasitic elements. The proposed antenna has dimensions of 12m$\mathrm{m}^{\star}$12m$\mathrm{m}^{\star}$1.5mm and is operational in the frequency range of 6.95-12.88 GHz (having a bandwidth of 5.93 GHz), therefore encompassing the X Band (S-12 GHz). The antenna is fabricated on an FR-4 (glass epoxy) substrate with a relative permittivity of 4.3 and a loss tangent of 0.025. At 12. 8GHz, the designed antenna has a maximum gain of2.59 dB in the working bandwidth. The design simulations were performed in CST Microwave Studio software, and the corresponding return losses and parameter study has been explained in this paper.

articleTitle: Methodology to Design a CCF−1 Ku Band GaN MMIC PA with Nonlinear Output Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An active second harmonic load improves the efficiency of a continuous class F inverse power amplifier (PA). Such an active load can be achieved with either an active harmonic injection or by utilizing the effect of a nonlinear output capacitance $(C_{out})$. This paper presents a methodology to achieve an active second harmonic load to the continuous class F inverse PA at the current source reference plane (CRP) with a passive matching network at the extrinsic reference plane (ERP).
