As a proof of concept, a continuous class F inverse PA operating at the Ku band is designed with $0.25\mu \mathrm{m}$ GaN HEMT technology from UMS. The designed PA operates from 16.5 to 17.4 GHz with a drain efficiency (DE) of 15 to 25%.

articleTitle: A Wearable IoT Based Assistive Device to Aid Communication With Hearing Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a wearable IoT based haptic assistive device to aid communication with hearing impaired (Divyang). The device helps to initiate communication between family members and Divyang using a switch module and vibration module. For the proof of concept, BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) based wireless devices are realized and tested. The key feature of the proposed assistive device is that it is simple to realize and use and inexpensive thus enabling better accessibility to the Divyang. Several practical considerations like miniaturization, low power consumption (battery operated device) have been taken into account in the prototype. The prototype has been succefully tested for its operation.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra Wideband MMIC Reflective Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design, fabrication and testing of a low-loss ultra-broadband SPDT switch using the AlGaAs / InGaAs pHEMT MMIC process are carried out on a test jig. Measurements across the entire band show more than 38 dB of isolation and 2.2 dB of insertion loss. Due to series-shunt architecture, all three ports of this SPDT switch are perfectly matched, with return losses of more than 12 dB up to 20 GHz and 10 dB over the entire operating range. Because the switch works with gate voltages of -3V or -5V and 0V, which guarantees negligible current less than 0.1mA and low current consumption during operation. This SPDT switch has an area of 2mm square. The main features offered are low loss, high isolation, compactness and fast switching speed.

articleTitle: Active Phased Array Antenna for Satellite Communication Onboard Data Link Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, design of an active phased array antenna is presented for airborne communication system receive only applications. The antenna is designed in C band using four micro-strip elements. Beamforming network is designed incorporating first stage LNA, phase-shifters and attenuators. Received signal from four elements is combined and down converted to L-band IF for reception through a satellite receiver. The antenna array is protected from extreme environment using Teflon Radome. Antenna array fabricated and its beam pattern and gain measured for different progressive phase shifts achieving beam tilt of ±45 degree.

articleTitle: Design of 1-bit High Gain Reflectarray Antenna using Dual Reradiating Element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the design and analysis of a hybrid configuration of reflectarray antenna for X-band applications is presented. The incident electromagnetic wave is reflected by the combination of a square patch within a square ring (element 1) and a circular patch (element 2). The total 360° phase is obtained by changing the size of the square patch and the radius of the circular patch. This 360° phase is quantized into two states 0 and $\pi$. The phase variation from 0 to 180° is obtained by element 1, and an additional 0° to -180° is obtained by element 2. Each element has a reflection magnitude close to 0 dB with a 360° reflection phase. The hybrid reflectarray provides a high gain, wide bandwidth, and reflected pencil beam in the operating band from 8 GHz to 11 GHz. The maximum realized gain of the reflectarray antenna is 24.5 dBi at 9. 59 GHz, and the 3 dB bandwidth of 1.6 GHz is obtained from 8.8 GHz to 10.4 GHz. The side lobe levels are below -15 dB.

articleTitle: Defected Ground Structure (DGS) Based Narrow Rectangular Patches: Detailed Investigations With Promising Improvement in Cross-Polar Radiations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: While investigating defected ground structure (DGS)-integrated rectangular patches, most of the researchers concentrate on square or wide patch with aspect ratio $\gt1.$ However, the narrow/thin (aspect ratio $\lt1)$ patches are often useful for their compact configuration and inherently low cross-polar (XP) radiations. It is also found that the true potential of asymmetric DGS has not yet been explored completely. This work investigates in detail different configurations of DGS for a rectangular patch with aspect ratio 0.8 and operating near 10 GHz. It also demonstrates two new configurations of asymmetric DGSs investigated for the first time for any type of rectangular patch. These DGSs can provide upto 20 dB suppression in the peak XP radiations in the H-plane without affecting the primary radiation mode.

articleTitle: Compact Low Frequency Tripler With Integrated Filter for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, design and development of an active low frequency tripler with an integrated filter is presented for space applications. The proposed active tripler is designed using bipolar junction transistor (BJT) embedded with both lumped and distributed networks as harmonic terminations, to achieve better than 50dBc harmonic suppression along with good return loss which is the cornerstone of the design. The frequency tripler is fabricated on 25mil Rogers TMM10i substrate and has dimensions of 65mm$\times$50mm. The fabricated tripler provides conversion loss of 7dB with 248MHz typical input frequency and return loss of better than 13dB and has stable performance over −15°C to 55°C temperature range. The reported tripler has extremely good return loss and harmonic suppression when compared to state-of-the-art designs and has been successfully used in Ka band radar altimeter system of Chandrayaan mission.

articleTitle: System Design of HRWS Frequency Scanning SAR for Airborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: High Resolution Wide Swath (HRWS) imaging is a key requirement for future SAR sensors and many topologies for same are being proposed in literature. Frequency scanning SAR (FScan SAR) is one of the promising candidate which along with providing the HRWS imaging capability, keeps the payload hardware simplified. FScan SAR utilizes the frequency dispersion phenomenon of array antennas fed with wide bandwidth chirp signals to provide intra-pulse beam scanning which is employed to provide wide swath imaging. As the beam scanning is done within the pulse there is no compromise in azimuth resolution. This paper presents the system design of airborne version of FScan SAR designed to image 30 km swath with 0.5 m ground resolution along with data processing aspects. The proposed system can be used for on demand high resolution imaging and also as a testbed to further enhance the frequency scanning SAR methodology and its processing algorithms. Simulation of one range line using the FScan SAR processing methodology with three point targets is also presented to verify the system performance.

articleTitle: Compact and Broadband Elliptical Microstrip Antenna with Low Cross-polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact and broadband elliptical microstrip antenna (MSA) is designed using multilayer stacked patches with direct coupling. Two dumbbell shaped patches are printed underneath an air suspended FR-4 substrate layer. These patches are stacked on the top of an elliptical MSA, which is designed on the bottom layer, and fit in the same area as occupied by elliptical patch. The dumbbell shaped patches are excited through electromagnetic and direct coupling, which is enabled by connecting two symmetric shorting posts between ellipse and dumbbell shaped patches. The antenna geometry is enclosed in a metallic cavity enclosure to enhance gain and to reduce back radiation. The designed elliptical MSA is a low-cost antenna with compact size of $0.85 \lambda \times 0.6 \lambda \times 0.15 \lambda$. It provides 43% BW (1.621 to 2.51 GHz) with peak gain of 9 dBi and front to back ratio (FBR) of more than 16 dB over BW. The cross polarization (X-pol) is less than 20 dB from 1.7 to 2.51 GHz. The designed antenna can be used for IoT devices utilizing 2G, 3G,4G-LTE, Wi-Fi and 5G applications.

articleTitle: Adulteration Detection of Glycol in Medical Grade Solvents Using the CSRR Loaded Stepped Coplanar Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study presents a novel CSRR-loaded stepped-CPW sensor to detect adulteration levels of glycol in medical-grade solvents. The proposed RF system comprising the stepped-CPW resonant sensor and specially designed molded glass capillary tube as a sample holder, is well suited for detecting small levels of adulteration in bio-grade glycerol. The main advantage of the proposed sensor is its strong field confinement in the sensing region, defined in terms of the shift in the resonance frequency resulting from changes in the dielectric constant. It is demonstrated that the two-ring CSRR topology, excited by the stepped-CPW and designed on a 0.8 mm thick FR-4 substrate operating at 8 GHz, provides improved sensitivity and high Q-factor compared to its single-ring counterpart. The proposed sensor is tested to detect the adulteration level of EG in medical glycerol. Various adulteration levels of EG in glycerol can be detected using the proposed device due to a substantial shift in the resonant frequency with even a small change in the adulteration level. This study introduces a comprehensive theoretical framework, including vital factors to be considered during the design phase, and explores the usage of the proposed sensor for quality monitoring of various types of medical-grade fluids.

articleTitle: Compact and High Efficiency UHF SSPA for Communication Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design, development and measured performance of compact and high efficiency 100W UHF SSPA for satellite on-board applications. The SSPA is designed using GaN HEMTs for medium power and high power amplifier stages and includes diode based power detector for providing RF power telemetry. The SSPA produces 100W output power with worst case efficiency of 60% under all operating temperatures and has a low power dissipation of 70W. Being a space hardware, the designed SSPA follows all derating guidelines to meet the required performance and has a maximum device channel temperature within $150 ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with worst case device compression of 1.5 dB. The realized SSPA also has a compact footprint of 250 mm x 170 mm.

articleTitle: Dual-Functional Metasurface Reflector for Wideband Polarization Conversion and RCS Reduction Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wideband polarization transforming reflective metasurface with dual functionality is proposed in this work. It converts the incident TE(Transverse Electric)/TM(Transverse Magnetic) waves into circularly polarized waves in a portion of the operating band and also into TM/TE waves respectively waves at the remaining frequency spectrum. The proposed unit cell’s front side comprises of tapered rectangular metal connected with a circular patch and backside by a metal ground. Proposed structure exhibits circular polarization (CP) conversion from 13.5-20.9 GHz and cross polarization (XP) conversion from 11.12-12.64 and 23.32-34.65 GHz. The proposed meta-atom and 90 degree rotated image are used to construct checkerboard metasurface with $10 \times 10$ elements for RCS reduction. It is inferred from the simulation results that a significant reduction in RCS is observed in the LP-XP band. The dimensions of the realized meta-atom are $0.297 \times 0.297 \times 0.062 \lambda_{0}^{3}$ (where $\lambda_{0}$ is dependent on lowest operating frequency), and is best suitable for future wireless communication and RCS reduction application simultaneously.

articleTitle: An AlGaAs Diode-based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for mmWave Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The role of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) has been significant for Millimeter Wave(mmWave) applications. The RIS provides the potential to redirect the incident wave with beamforming using programmable and reconfigurable devices. In this work, an AlGaAs diode-based single-layered RIS unit cell is proposed with beamforming operation at mmWave communication in the reflection mode. The unit cell, with a size of $10 \times \mathrm{l}0 \times \mathrm{l}.6\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}^{3}$, is integrated with two AlGaAs-based pin diodes as reconfigurable elements. It provides a resonance bandwidth of 31.5-32.85 GHz (1.35 GHz) and 31.5-32.34 GHz (0.84 GHz) with a 31.9 GHz resonant peak in On and Off-states respectively. The variation in the reflection beams is observed due to the reflection phases $0^{0}$ (On-state) and $15^{0}$ (Off-state). The proposed single-layered structure is designed and simulated using a CST full wave simulator with AlGaAs diode equivalent lumped elements. Hence, the designed RIS unit cell is suitable for mmWave communication, which provides radiation coverage.

articleTitle: An Automatic RF Measurements with Vector Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The rapid evolution of wireless communication technologies has necessitated efficient and accurate characterization of RF components and systems. Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) have emerged as indispensable tools for such measurements due to their capability to analyze complex RF networks. This paper presents an automated, simplified test setup for RF measurement using VNA with 87% test time reduction compared to manual measurement. The proposed automatic measurement system is designed to streamline testing, reduce human intervention, and enhance measurement precision. It employs state-of-the-art automation techniques, integrating hardware and software components to perform a series of RF measurements seamlessly. Additionally, the paper discusses the development of a user-friendly graphical interface, providing an intuitive platform for customized test parameters, to configure & control the VNA, and visualizing measurement outcomes. The user interface enables straightforward batch processing and dumps auto-report generation.

articleTitle: Low power MOSFET based RF discharge oscillator for Rubidium Atomic Clock
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: As is well known, the Rubidium Atomic Clocks are the workhorse of satellite navigation. The physics package, which is a subsystem of Rubidium Atomic Clock, mainly decides the long-term frequency stability of Rubidium Atomic Clock. Inside this physics package, the RF discharge oscillator lies and is the heart of the physics package. This paper presents design, development, testing and characterization of low power MOSFET based (Common Gate configuration) RF discharge oscillator, which is developed for the first time. The oscillator is intended to discharge electrodeless Rubidium bulb (Rb bulb) that provides spectral components to support optical pumping for Atomic signal generation & detection. The load of the oscillator is the Rb bulb & it has dynamic nature on the verge of discharging. Due to that dynamic nature it is quite challenging & tedious task to discharge the Rb bulb. The oscillator is a Clapp power oscillator having 61.12 MHz frequency (tunable between 55MHz-75 MHz), consumes 3.25 Watt DC power, produces about 0.5 Watt RF power & 14.73% efficiency. The detailed method of discharging the Rb bulb is also presented in this paper. The circuit is realized in 2-layer FR4 PCB using MRF 134 MOSFET (MACOM make) as an active device.

articleTitle: Circular patch impinged 4×4 patch metasurface loaded, Dual polarized, Wide-band antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband, miniaturized meta-surface loaded, dual-polarized antenna for planar array applications. A novel square and circular patch meshed metasurface is devised to enhance the edge length and minimize the surface area to $0.57\lambda_{0}\times 0.57\lambda_{0}$. The metasurface is analyzed to extract the modes and effective constitutive parameters. The antenna provides a massive reflection bandwidth of 38% (4.25 GHz to 6.25 GHz) in both the polarization. Two U-shaped orthogonal traces are utilized to facilitate dual-polarized feeding scheme. It is shown that by introducing two layered feeding scheme, the isolation level has increased from 10 dB to 37 dB. The antenna achieves 6.5 dBi to 10.7 dBi gain within operational band for both the polarization with average radiation efficiency of 98%. The proposed antenna holds significant promise for practical applications in wireless communication and the remote sensing domain.

articleTitle: S-/C-Band Common Aperture Microstrip Antenna with Polarization Versatility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of an S-/C-band common aperture microstrip antenna. It features dual linear polarization (LP) at S-band and dual circularly polarized (CP) at C-band. The S-band element is proximity coupled to two orthogonal microstrip feeds. The C-band array is an aperture coupled to other two composite feeds which produce left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) and right-hand circular polarization (RHCP). The dependencies of isolation on relative slot positions and inter-layer spacing have been investigated. The antenna yields an impedance bandwidth of wider than 3.5% at the S-band with an isolation better than 22 dB. At C-band, it exhibits wider than 21.2% impedance bandwidth, wider than 10.2% axial-ratio bandwidth, and isolation higher than 18.5 dB. Design details and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Enhancing transmitter efficiency for 5G MIMO Beamforming Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Digital predistortion is a well-known technique used in communication systems to improve the efficiency and linearity of power amplifiers. However, the high-dimensional nature of MIMO Beamforming systems makes it challenging to implement digital predistortion algorithms in real time. To overcome this challenge, the paper implements several dimension reduction techniques, including independent component analysis (ICA), principal component analysis (PCA), compact singular vector decomposition (CSVD), and partial least square (PLS). The authors evaluate the performance of these techniques based on the reduction in computational complexity and the preservation of system performance metrics such as adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) and normalized mean square error (NMSE). The results show that all the dimension reduction techniques can reduce the computational complexity of the digital predistortion algorithm. The authors also compare the tradeoffs between the computational complexity reduction, numerical stability, and the preservation of system performance metrics for each technique. Overall, the study concludes that dimension-reduction techniques can effectively reduce the computational complexity of digital predistortion algorithms in MIMO Beamforming systems. However, the selection of the technique should be based on the specific performance requirements of the system.

articleTitle: An Improved SPST Switch Using PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents an improved single-pole-single-throw (SPST) switch using PIN diodes. The primary aim of the design is to mitigate the parasitic effects of a PIN diode across a wide frequency range. However, as theoretical parasitic compensation is performed solely at a specific frequency, the comprehensive switch performance depends on the wideband parasitic values. To accomplish this, adjustments are made to the diode parasitic values to expand the bandwidth of the switch. The diode is employed in the shunt arm and connected to the main line via an impedance transforming network. A transmission line-based analysis is provided to explain the working principle of the switch. Finally, the proposed design is verified through fabrication and measurements in the X-band. The overall responses show significant improvement compared to the conventional design. The simulation shows that a single stage SPST switch provides 20 dB isolation over 1 GHz at the mid-band frequency of 10.0 GHz which is at least 75% more than the conventional design using the same diode. The mid-band insertion loss also decreases.

articleTitle: Study of the Tilted Mounting Angle of Automotive Radar Antenna Installed Behind a Painted Bumper
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper studies the effect of the tilted mounting angle of an automotive radar antenna installed behind a painted bumper. First, a series-fed radar antenna array is designed and installed behind a painted bumper. Afterwards, the radar antenna is rotated about the x-, y-, and z-axis to investigate the impact of the tilted mounting angle. Further, the gain performance of the antenna in the yz and xz planes is studied and compared with the no rotation case. The performed study aid in understanding the rotation limit that can be tolerated for the application of Long Range Radar.

articleTitle: Microstrip Fed All Metal Lens Antenna - As a Power Transfer Medium for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A rectenna for wireless power transfer is proposed for 5G band, using an ultra-wideband 2D lens antenna with all metal structure. Glide symmetry assisted metasurface is used to design the lens. A flare is designed to match the impedance between the free space and the parallel plate tip of the lens layers. Three microstrip Feeds are designed to excite the antenna in the 5G frequency band (24.25-27.5GHz) at 25 GHz. The microstrip feed allows smooth transition between the lens and the rectifier circuit co-integration. The overall proposed system gives a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 62% at an input power of 12.5 dBm.

articleTitle: Wideband Multi-channel RF Selection Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and implementation of a wideband multichannel RF selection unit has been discussed in this article. It consists of two input channels, one Built-in test (BIT) source and four output channels. Any input channel/BIT can be routed to any output channel. It comprises of three sections: 1)RF section; 2)Power Supply, Control & BIT section; 3)AC-DC conversion section. It is realized as stack up of two PCBs on either side of mechanical housing. Top side of housing comprises of VHF to C band RF section. Bottom side comprises of VHF band RF section, VHF to C band BIT section, Power supply, digital controls circuitry and AC-DC converter. PCB s are hybrid multilayer. Vertical coax based RF transitions are used for routing BIT and RF signals to RF output paths, resulting in compact integration. Digital controls and power supply are connected from bottom PCB to top PCB via board to board connector. Realized unit measures 10.7 dB min Gain with < ±2 dB Gain Flatness and ≤5.3 dB Noise figure over frequency and temperature. It provides very high isolation (>90 dB) among output channels and very low output spurious. The unit works on 230 VAC supply. Realized unit has cleared Environmental stress screening (ESS) testing successfully.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna using Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized pattern reconfigurable antenna operating at 3.5GHz is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a dual-feed antenna as a source and $7 \times 7$ coding metasurface as a superstrate. The feeding position of the patch antenna is orthogonal to each other and optimized to generate good circular polarization. The unit cell utilized in coding metasurface exhibits transmissive characteristics for dual-polarized incident waves, with its structure consisting of an even-loop and a diagonal strip. Three PIN diodes are placed on the unit cell to control overall emission. The proposed antenna performance is evaluated in nine distinct modes of operation. The antenna achieves circularly polarized beam steering from -18° to +22° in the $y z$-plane. In each beam steered direction axial ratio is less than 3-dB. The antennas overall bandwidth is from 3.48 to 3.56GHz with peak gain of 3.49dBic.

articleTitle: Design and Development of C and X band LNA MMIC’s using Indigenous 0.25um AlGaN/GaN-on-SiC HEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper expounds the design of C band and X band GaN based LNA MMIC’s with indigenously developed $0.25\mu\mathrm{m}$ AlGaN/GaN-on-SiC HEMT Technology. Designed LNA’s are fabricated and the measurement results of fabricated LNA MMIC’s are discussed in details in this paper. The achieved measured results of C band (5.4-5.9GHz) LNA MMIC are NF ≤ 1.7dB, Gain~21dB, I/P return loss better than 16dB and O/P return loss better than 14 dB. For X band (9-10GHz) LNA MMIC, achieved measured results are NF ≤ 2.1dB, Gain~14dB, I/P return loss better than 17dB and O/P return loss better than 12 dB.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Adaptive Beamforming on Large Inter Element Spaced Aperiodic Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Phased array radar systems are crucial in various applications, but they often face limitations in terms of grating lobes, interference mitigation, and side lobe levels. To address these issues, an advanced architecture and algorithm for adaptive beamforming is proposed and implemented. The objectives of this work include optimizing the signal of interest, suppressing interferences, and reducing side lobe levels. This paper presents the design and implementation of adaptive beamforming techniques on grating lobes suppressed aperiodic phased arrays. Algebraic methods and computational procedures are developed to achieve these objectives. Extensive simulations are conducted using MATLAB software tools to validate the proposed approach. The results demonstrate that adaptive beamforming can be applied in aperiodic phased arrays with large inter element spacing.

articleTitle: An SDR-based Passive Radar for Detection and Tracking of Drones and UAVs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Drones and Unmanned aerial vehicles have gained high popularity and are equally dangerous and threaten infrastructures and public safety. Monitoring of such unmanned aerial vehicles is of great importance not only for defense but as well for civilian sectors. Implementing an active radar is not always feasible to track these aerial targets in urban areas and due to possible interference with other critical RF systems. A non-invasive solution for the detection and tracking of drones and UAVs is proposed in this paper. In this paper, a passive radar has been implemented using software-defined radio, lowcost hardware, and custom codes. The proposed system has been tested in outdoor experimental setups with results that validate drone detection and tracking using passive radar.

articleTitle: Inductance Prediction Model for the Planar Meander Structure using RBF
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, prediction of meander line inductance using deep learning supervised regression Radial Basis Function (RBF) model has been demonstrated. The meander line inductance model has the input parameters: number of meander turns, the length of long arm, conductor width and conductor thickness. The dataset of 10,000 points created using the analytical expression available in literature. The developed RBF model have the mean squared error and $R^{2}$ are 0.931 and 0.997 respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband and Efficient Doherty Power Amplifier in n78 C-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient, linear, and broadband Doherty power amplifier (DPA) design in n78 C-band. In order to achieve improved performance, a modified load combiner network (MLCN) approach is incorporated into an inverse Doherty PA (IDPA) architecture. Proposed PA is realized through a premier and cutting-edge n78 band device, GTRB384608FC. Proposed DPA covers entire n78 band from 3.3 to 3.8 GHz (500 MHz) with enhanced efficiency of 40.5% to 46.5%, for an average power of 47.5 dBm and attained peak power, ranging from 54 dBm to 55.5 dBm. As well as it able to sustain an output PAPR in between 6.5 dB to 8 dB across the spectrum in continuous wave (CW) signal excitation.

articleTitle: SIW Cavity-Backed MIMO Antenna with Planar Excitation for Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a fully planar substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is proposed for Ku-band applications. The complete structure of the proposed MIMO antenna configuration is realized on a single layer of substrate by closely placing two identical SIW cavity-backed slot antenna elements with radiation fields orthogonal to each other. In the proposed antenna, a unique combination of the grounded co-planar waveguide (GCPW) feeding network with SIW cavity-backed slot antennas significantly enhances the MIMO performance while keeping the overall profile simple and small. The proposed antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 6% (14.−15.2 GHz) with isolation and ECC better than 30 dB and 0.00025, respectively, over the entire operating band. Maximum gain of 7.3 dBi is achieved. The other MIMO parameters of the proposed antenna are also well-suited for the design of compact receiver modules for Ku-band very small aperture terminal (VSAT) communication applications.

articleTitle: High Yield Design of an On Chip X-band Power Divider Based on GaAs IPD Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes high yield design of a compact X band power divider using an optimized inductor on an Integrated Passive Device (IPD) technology on GaAs substrate. Simulation shows that an excellent RF performance can be achieved using only single section of “T” or “Pi” network in a small size of $1.1 \mathrm{~mm} \times 1.1 \mathrm{~mm}$ that is $0.04 \lambda_{0} \times 0.04 \lambda_{0}$ where $\lambda_{0}$ is the free-space wavelength at 10 GHz. The design was optimized considering the process and components tolerances. Yield better than 98%, achieved for return loss performance better than 15 dB, insertion loss of 0.52-0.7dB and isolation better than 15dB over 8 to 12GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: An analysis on leg muscles strengthening exercises by using wearable UWB technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents an analysis on leg muscles strengthening exercises utilizing wearable ultra-wideband (UWB) technology. For analysis of various exercises, channel parameters are examined by using proposed compact wearable antennas mounted on the human subject at suitable places. Moreover, SAR analysis of this antenna has also been performed which is within acceptable limit (<0.927 W/kg). The study of channel formed due to distance variation takes into account both LOS and NLOS links. For this analysis, path loss and rms delay spread have been considered as basic parameters. The differences in channel information are attributable to the antenna’s location, human body obstruction, and various activities that are being performed. The proposed wearable antenna design has a very compact size which makes it suitable for analysis that is being performed on lower limb activity monitoring having applications in healthcare industry.

articleTitle: Design of Hexagonal Pyramidal Conformal Array Antenna for S-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study examines the impact of coupling between elements of a hexagonal pyramidal conformal array antenna on the radiation patterns and individual coupling of those elements. The antenna array is in the shape of a truncated hexagonal pyramid, with a patch antenna on each of the six pyramidal faces and a cluster of seven antennae on the top. The effect of these interactions on the radiation patterns and performance of these antennas is studied in detail, with an emphasis on the radiation pattern and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameters. Return loss of -60dB is achieved which enhances the antenna’s overall efficiency and performance, leading to better communication range, higher data throughput, and improved signal reception.

articleTitle: Side lobe blanking in active phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of side lobe blanking antenna in active phased array antenna (APAA) is discussed. The antenna configuration has been presented. The distribution of antenna is obtained by using Genetic Algorithm (GA). The radiation pattern of side lobe blanking antenna is demonstrated at bore sight as well as scanned condition without affecting the main beam radiation properties. The simulated results are in good agreement with measured results. The paper presents the simple method to design a side lobe blanking antenna using Genetic Algorithm to meet requirement of active phased array antenna at scan condition.

articleTitle: K/Ka Band ADE Reflector with broadened beam size in 27-31 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports a K/Ka-Band Axially Displaced Ellipsoid (ADE) reflector Antenna with shaped main and subreflector surfaces operating in 17-22 GHz and 27-31 GHz frequency bands. In addition to the full band operation, the reflector system also broadens the beam size in receive band 27-31 GHz in order to cover a wider geographical foot print when operated from a MEO satellite. The feed is axially corrugated horn and is kept purposefully close to the subreflector inorder to avoid separate struts for holding subreflector. The beam size in 27-31 GHz band is increased from 2 degrees to 2.5 degrees while keeping the beam size in 17-22 GHz band unaffected.

articleTitle: Digital video communication using salt water standing columns
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Audio and video communication is achieved using simple salt water standing columns over a wide frequency range (50-670) MHz. Communication is tested over a distance of 45 meters. In these experiments, salt water columns with different insulator bases and different conductivity are used for testing RF communication. Salt water column is used on either side for transmission and reception of the signals. Salt water containing charged particles acts as antenna. RF power is coupled to salt water using a N-type coaxial connector. Advantage of this antenna is its simple configuration, transparency, low cost, wide bandwidth, conformability, reconfigurability, good electromagnetic coupling and easy transportability. This system offers low RCS (Radar cross section).

articleTitle: Design and Development of RF Synthesizer for Rubidium Atomic Clock
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, we have successfully developed an innovative, low-noise, and straightforward 6.834 GHz microwave frequency synthesizer designed for rubidium atomic clocks. This synthesizer's core components include an ultra-low-phase-noise 10 MHz OCXO, an active frequency multiplier, a step recovery diode multiplier, and a digital signal generator using FPGA technology. Utilizing frequency multiplication and mixing techniques, frequency precision is achieved in generating the output atomic resonance frequency. The phase noise performance of the 6.834 MHz signal was thoroughly evaluated, resulting in -50 dBc/Hz @1 Hz and -97 dBc/Hz @ 1 kHz. These measurements resulted in an instability contribution of 3.2E-12 for a 1-second averaging time, a performance level that closely matches the clock shot noise limit due to the Dick effect. This dedicated microwave frequency synthesizer not only enhances the compactness but also reduces power consumption in engineering rubidium atomic clocks. Moreover, this synthesizer scheme holds potential for application in other high-performance rubidium atomic clocks.

articleTitle: Dual Band Complex to Real Impedance Matching Through Dual Band Quarter Wave Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel technique to match Frequency Dependent Complex Loads (FDCLs) to real source impedance at uncorrelated dual frequencies is presented. The impedance transformation occurs in two steps. In the first step, the load susceptances are cancelled through stubs. The left behind unequal real loads are then transformed to Z0 through dual band quarter wave transformer. In this article, the strength of a combination of open-short stubs and T-section branched stub to cancel any two arbitrary susceptances at two frequencies is thoroughly studied. Also a novel technique to transform two unequal real loads to the port impedance, Z0 is proposed. The scheme allows concurrent operability. The complete mathematical description of all the proposed structures with closed form solutions are provided. Two prototype matching networks for frequency ratios 2.875 and 4.8 are designed and implemented on ROGERS RO4003 substrate having dielectric constant of 3.38 and substrate height of 20 mils. The simulated and the measured results are in a good accordance.

articleTitle: Wideband 3D Printed Dual Polarized Digital Metasurface Reflectarray Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low cost wideband dual polarized 3D printed digital metasurface reflectarray antenna for mm-wave applications is presented in this paper. The metasurface unit cell element is composed of dielectric dipole loaded with stubs. The optimized dimensions of the unit cell element provides eight binary states (000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111) with a phase difference of $\pi / 4$. The metasurface reflector of dimensions $4.5 \lambda_{o} \times 4.5 \lambda_{o}$ is designed and illunmated by a 3D printed horn, kept at the optimized focal point of 45 mm. The measured results shows a stable radiation pattern over the operating frequency range from 26 GHz-36 GHz. A maximum gain of 19.5 dBi is obtained at 34 GHz, corresponding aperture efficiency of 35%. Besides, a measured 3 dB gain bandwidth of 32% is obtained, indicating the wideband characteristics of the proposed metasurface reflectarray antenna.

articleTitle: A Finite Element Analysis of MEMS-based Magnetoelectric Micro Antenna for On-chip RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Magnetoelectric (ME) antennas hold great promise for energy harvesting applications in low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) bands. This paper presents a finite element method (FEM) simulation of a miniaturized MEMS-based magnetoelectric antenna for RF energy harvesting. The proposed rectangular MEE antenna has dimensions of $260 \mu {m} \times 80 \mu {m}$. This micro antenna is much smaller than the conventional antenna and coils for the HF band, i.e., 3-30 MHz frequency range. The ME antenna involves the synergistic coupling of the magnetostrictive layer of Terefnol-D with the piezoelectric layer of the Aluminum Nitride (AIN) sandwich between Terefnol-D layers. The various electrical parameters of the ME micro antenna, such as impedance, phase, reflection coefficient, and induced voltage, are calculated. The proposed antenna resonates at the frequency of 10.514 MHz with a bandwidth of 38 kHz. At resonance, it generates a harvested voltage of 1.9 mV, 0.6 mV, and 0.03 mV at incident in-plane RF magnetic fields of 0.9mT, 0.5mT, and 0.1mT, respectively. The harvested voltage reduces to 6.53 $\mu \mathrm{V}, 2.1 \mu \mathrm{V}$, and $0.2 \mu \mathrm{V}$ at incident out-of-plane RF magnetic fields of 0.9 mT, 0.5 mT and 0.1 mT, respectively. The harvested energy can be used to drive low-power electronic devices like biomedical implants.

articleTitle: Design and Development of THz Pyramidal Horn Antenna from 220 GHz to 330 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, we present the design of a terahertz (THz) pyramidal horn antenna. The antenna is designed to operate in the frequency range of 220 GHz to 330 GHz, and is optimized for low side lobe levels and high gain. The design process involves the use of CST Microwave Studio software to model the antenna’s electromagnetic behavior and optimize its performance. A standard WR $3.4 (0.864 \times 0.432$ mm$^{2}$) waveguide is used to feed the antenna. The final design achieves a gain of 30 dBi in simulation and is fabricated using state-of-the-art manufacturing techniques. The designed THz pyramidal horn antenna exhibits excellent performance in terms of gain, bandwidth, and side-lobe levels, making it a promising candidate for use in THz communication systems.

articleTitle: Isolation and Gain Enhancement of MIMO Diversity Antenna using Metamaterial Absorber and Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work explains the design of a wideband two-port multilayer multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) array antenna with polarization diversity mechanism. The proposed antenna provides wider impedance bandwidth (IBW), circular polarization (CP) radiation, improved isolation, and higher gain performance due to the loading of dual-layer metasurface, which is based on a linear-to-circular polarization converter (LTC-PC). The intended MIMO antenna provides a wider IBW of 34.1% (4.61-6.69 GHz), higher gain of 10.12 dBic at 5.9 GHz, and isolation is better than 32 dB for the complete operating band. Furthermore, the antenna provides polarization diversity mechanism, with port-1 provides right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) radiation and port-2 provides left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) radiation.

articleTitle: Design of C band 120W Space TWT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The article presents design details of C band 120W TWT and its subassemblies like electron gun, electron focusing system, helix slow wave structure (SWS) and multistage depressed collector along with results. This TWT is targeted for space application as part of communication satellites and specific design considerations have been made to ensure its space worthiness. The design is optimized to provide highest efficiency in the frequency range of 3.7GHz to 4.2GHz with minimum saturated output power of 120W and saturation gain more than 50dB.

articleTitle: Complementary Radially Shaped Split Resonator Structure for Quality Assessment of Cooking Oils
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A complementary radially shaped split resonator (CRSR) sensor structure with improved sensitivity is proposed in this work for the quality assessment of cooking oils. The developed sensor resonates at 3 GHz with a quality factor of 110 and quite a high uniform field concentration in the sensing region. The improved fractional sensitivity (8.7%), and the enhanced electric field confinement are some of the salient features of the proposed sensor as compared to those of a typical complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) of the same dimension. The structure is simulated using the CST MWS with its equivalent circuit developed in ADS. The fabricated high-sensitive RF sensor prototype is employed to differentiate the cold-pressed oils and their respective commercial versions, by recording the change in the insertion loss and the resonant frequency corresponding to these two versions of the oil. It is demonstrated that the proposed sensor due to its high sensitivity is able to provide a reasonable shift in the resonant frequency as well as the transmission magnitude notch for the pure and refined versions of both the coconut oil and the mustard oil.

articleTitle: Dual Circular Polarized Compact Antenna in S-Band for Drone Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of a dual CP antenna for S-band applications 2-3 GHz is proposed in this paper. Pair of cross dipoles are used to achieve dual circular polarization. To improve antenna gain, circular fence monopoles are added to the ground and cross-slot is inscribed on the top patch. Surface current shows that RHCP is achieved at two different frequencies for this design. The axial ratio (AR) achieved with this antenna less than 3 dB for a beam coverage of ± 30° for ensuring a reliable link with the ground station. This application is used for data transfer in drone based RCS measurements.

articleTitle: Dual band Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Filter With High Rejection and Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a dual band bandpass filter with improved rejection between the two passbands and selectivity, is presented. The two passbands are centered at 2.4 GHz and 3.5 GHz with Fractional Bandwidths (FBW) of 4% and 5.5% respectively. Trisection topology is used to create both the passbands using rectangular SIW resonators resonating at its fundamental TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> and next higher order TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">210</inf> modes. To reduce the circuit foot print, two layer structure is adopted. This design offers two transmission zeroes (TZs) in between the passbands resulting at least 48 dB rejection over 2.75 GHz-3.25 GHz. The measured reflection and transmission losses are better than 11.2 dB and 3.21 dB for first whereas they are better than 15.5 dB and 3.01 dB for the second passband respectively.

articleTitle: A Multilayer Slot Coupled Multi-element Monopole Radiator with End-fire Radiation Pattern for mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, an antenna for millimeter wave (mmWave) application is presented. The antenna has a 3layered structure that uses three pairs of metallic monopoles embedded in the top substrate layer, which are fed through slot-coupled microstrips using a microstrip feed line printed below the bottom substrate. The antenna demonstrates the ability to radiate in the end-fire direction. The antenna has a -10 dB reflection bandwidth from 22.3-27.1 GHz, and the realized gain within the operating bandwidth is noted from 6.1-7.9 dBi. The proposed antenna finds its application in 26 GHz 5G mmWave frequency band and 24 GHz ISM band. The antenna can also be used as an element of a multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna and antenna array for the massive MIMO (m-MIMO) application.

articleTitle: Novel Reconfigurable Multiband Reflective Units Based on Minkowski Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Two kinds of multiband reflective units with a Minkowski fractal geometry are proposed based on our previous work. To make full use of the miniaturization capability of fractal geometry and achieve a multiband performance at the same time, five first-order Minkowski fractals with optimized patch sizes and scaling factors are combined first. And four corner patches are then modified to broaden each operating band. Extensive simulations and analyses are conducted for the unit based on the well-known full wave simulation software ANSYS HFSS, and the simulation results show that the proposed unit of the first kind realize average phase range of more than 400 degrees in bands centered at 22.2 GHz, 27.2 GHz and 33 GHz. And the proposed reflective unit of the second kind can achieve multiband performance in frequency bands centered at 7.3 GHz, 9.0 GHz and 23.3 GHz, while the total area of the unit is only about 0.6 squared wavelength. The proposed unit cells are very suitable for the design of antennas focused on beam-forming and beam-steering applications used in satellite communications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis of Conventional Frequency Selective Surfaces for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Conventional designs of arrays of metallo-dielectric frequency selective surface (FSS) for terahertz (THz) frequency range such as square conducting pads (Pixels), metallic mesh, mesh-loop (ML), square loop (SL) and complementary square loop (CSL) are analyzed and compared through simulations. Pixel FSS demonstrates 0.58 THz wide stop-band and 0.14 THz wide pass-band centered at 2.96 THz and 3.35 THz respectively. By complementing, the pixel array becomes a mesh array that appears as a band-pass FSS from 1.89 THz to 3.45 THz. ML array is formed by removing a square ring from the mesh array and provides a 0.32 THz wide pass-band and 0.3 THz stop-band centered at 0.82 THz and 1.15 THz. After eliminating the outer mesh of ML array, SL array yields a 0.32 THz wide band-stop FSS centered at 1.22 THz. Later, the CSL array is formed when SL array is complemented, and the array demonstrates a 0.6 THz wide pass-band at 1.14 THz. The pixel array provides a high signal rejection capability and the widest −10dB stop-band in the frequency range of 2.58-3.16 THz. This analysis and comparison is significant for reduction of EM coupling or interference in THz based integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Tunable Bandpass Filter at Microwave Frequency Using Plasmonic Metamaterial Based Ring Resonator Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: As compared to the current 4G mobile technology, a higher bandwidth and a lower latency will be provided by 5G and beyond technologies, which is planned to be deployed in 2020-2030, providing connectivity to billions of devices and enabling bandwidth with more than hundreds of megabits per second and very low latency less than 1 millisecond (ms). The tunable wideband RF system is essential part for realization of above mentioned technology in which tunable Band Pass Filter (BPF) is important microwave component. The tunable filter with variable frequency response is designed by altering of the electrical path of the mode current. Spoof surface Plasmon Polaritons (SSPPs) based BPF structure are the artificial engineered material-based design. This is trend towards of Microwave Photonics or Metamaterial Physics to application of tunable Bandpass Filter at Microwave Frequency. The paper comprises of corrugated ring resonator SSPP structure with tuning capability using novel approach at Microwave Frequency.The corrugated ring resonator-based bandpass filter show octave bandwidth i.e. the 3 dB passband is achieved between 3. 5-7.0 GHz. The varactor tuned corrugated ring resonator is shown to achieve electronically tunable BPF.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Sub-THz Antenna for 6G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low profile circularly polarized antenna is proposed in this communication. The proposed antenna has four layers: radiating window, excitation layer, air cavity, and a coupling layer. Nearly square slots present in the excitation layer are key radiating element of the antenna and asymmetrical position of slots is responsible for the circular polarization. Antenna gives a realized gain of 11.9 dBic while providing efficiency of 95.1%. The fractional impedance bandwidth of 8.9% from 270-295 GHz is attained by the antenna with 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 12 GHz(4.3 %) from 278.2 GHz to 290.2 GHz within the band with 285 GHz as centre frequency.

articleTitle: Application of metamaterials in mmWave 5G antenna designs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: High gain antennas with very small physical footprint are required for portable devices operating in the mmWave 5G bands. The standard antenna topologies might fall short to deliver the required performance metrics. Meta-material concept might be useful to deliver the required metrics with the budgeted dimensions of commercial portable devices. This paper gives an overview of the application of metamaterials for gain enhancement of antennas, specifically designed for portable devices. Two case studies are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity Dual Notch Microwave Sensor Inspired by Metamaterial for Characterization of Dielectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The research study presents a new microwave sensor capable of detecting the permittivity and thickness up to 1.2mm of dielectric materials. The sensor consists of a modified complementary split ring resonator with dual modes, which is stimulated by a microstrip transmission line. The presence of two zero frequencies in the transmission response of the sensor can be attributed to the dual-mode resonance of the magnetic-LC resonator. When dielectric materials with varying thicknesses and permittivity are introduced onto the resonator, the corresponding zero frequencies undergo a change. The monitoring of these variations in frequency allows for the estimation of both the permittivity and thickness of the dielectric samples under examination. The sensor under consideration has two distinct notches, with the second notch demonstrating increased sensitivity as a result of its higher resonance frequency. The sensor exhibits very high relative sensitivity for both notches. The findings derived from simulations, observations, and mathematical formulations demonstrate a high degree of concurrence.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Analysis Using Fast Volume-Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we use the Method of Moment (MoM) based Fast Volume Surface Integral Equation (FSVIE) for the full wave analysis of an array antenna at 13.75GHz. In the FSVIE, the dielectric volume part is modeled with SWG tetrahedral basis function, and the conducting surface part is modeled with the RWG triangle basis function. The acceleration of matrix filling and solution is carried out using Adaptive Cross Approximation (ACA) based matrix compression method. Our results show FSVIE gives significant savings for matrix storage as well as time savings for both matrix fill and solution.

articleTitle: Thermally Switchable Wideband Metamaterial Absorber using Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a switchable Metamaterial Absorber (MMA) design and simulation based on phase change material (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is presented. VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has been used for the switchable behaviour of MMA. The proposed design is having absorption bandwidth of 2.11 to 8.41 GHz covering the S and C bands for normal incidence of electromagnetic waves. When VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is in the metallic state, the design works as a wide band absorber whereas in the insulating state, it behaves as a wide band reflector. The design is symmetrical which leads to polarisation insensitive behaviour of MMA. It is stable for oblique incidence response up to 30 degrees for TE polarization and up to 60 degrees for TM polarization. The profile of MMA is $0.098 \lambda_{L}$ with a periodicity of $0.141 \lambda_{L}$ where $\lambda_{L}$ corresponds to the lowest frequency. The proposed MMA will be an effective way out of the problem of complex DC biasing circuits and the use of multiple lumped elements in active metamaterial absorbers.

articleTitle: Development of Lightweight and Flexible Carbon Nanofiber and Polyurethane Nanocomposite for EMI Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Future-generation EMI shielding requires thin, flexible, stretchable nanocomposite structures for conformal, flexible and bendable electronic appliances that can sustain harsh environmental conditions. The present work shows the design and development of such type structures by encapsulating carbon nanofiber (CNF) inside polyurethane (PU). The 8 wt% CNF (CNF8) shows improved conductivity and EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) in the X-band (8.2 to 12.4 GHz). The maximum total SE (SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) of 34.41 dB for CNF8 is observed at 0.75 mm thickness, unaffected by the complex environmental conditions like two hours of water sonication, 1000 mechanical bending cycles, and horizontal and vertical bending. The microstructure and electrical conductivity profile of these fabricated structures are used to explain the absorption dominating the EMI shielding process. Further, the layers of CNF8 are stacked together with the help of solvent followed by mechanical pressing, and the maximum SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 71.61 dB was achieved for a thickness of 2.21 mm. For a broadband EM shielding application, the SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> is calculated theoretically via simulation in CST microwave studio. The fabricated flexible, lightweight nanocomposite structures exhibit good EMI shielding and can be used in conformal surface coating and electronic packaging in defence, and aerospace applications.

articleTitle: Design of Minituarized Ku-Band Front End for Satellite Command Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents wideband miniaturized Ku-Band RF front end operating in the frequency band of 12.75 GHz to 13.25 GHz. The realized RF front end is highly compact as compared to the existing narrow band front end. The front end incorporates in house designed hermetically sealed MMIC LNA packaging using space qualified process, the packaged LNA is drop in type and provides ease of assembling. The complexity of local oscillator generation at Ku-Band was negated by designing a low conversion loss sub-harmonic filter. The miniaturized front-end distinctive features as compared to exiting front end is usage of fewer active devices, bandwidth improvement, fewer assembly elements, reduction in power consumption from 650mW to 200mW, improved gain from 10 dB to 15 dB, low LO drive, fewer spurious of below -50 dBc, all parameters are maintained over the operating temperature of -30 °C to +60°C. The miniaturized design has reduction in size and weight by 70% compared to existing design.

articleTitle: A 140 GHz SiGe Power Amplifier with >12.5 dBm P1dB and >8% PAE for Phased Array Systems in 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a 140 GHz power amplifier for phased array systems in 6G communication. The power amplifier is designed using 130nm SiGe process (SG13G2) from IHP foundry. To compensate for low gain of devices at Sub-THz/THz frequencies, the proposed single-ended two-stage power amplifier utilizes cascode topology for each stage. Additionally, the proposed work carefully analyses the impact of interconnects/parasitic on device performance and subsequently minimizes the interconnect/parasitic losses to achieve state-of-art power added efficiency of 8-15% and gain of $\gt20 \mathrm{~dB}$ in two stages. The power amplifier shows output P1dB of $\gt12.5 \mathrm{dBm}$ from $133-153 \mathrm{GHz}$ with corresponding PAE of about 10 %. Achieved saturated power (Psat) is $\gt14.2 \mathrm{dBm}$ with corresponding PAE of about 12 % over this band.

articleTitle: High Isolation Ka-band Multi-Port PIN Diode MMIC Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: AlGaAs/GaAs PIN diode based Ka-band SP4T and SP2T switches are designed and tested, with measured insertion loss less than 2 dB and isolation better than 48 dB over 25-33 GHz band. The on-wafer measured results are in close match with simulations. These MMIC switches are EM simulated using ADS Momentum tool. Combination of series and shunt diode topology is used to get optimum insertion loss and isolation at Ka-band. These chips have on-chip bias networks and DC blocking capacitors and are well suited for realization of miniaturized RF switch matrix at Ka-band.

articleTitle: A Multi-Octave High Linearity Broadband MMIC Amplifier with Active Bias Circuit for Gain Requirements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and development of a broadband MMIC amplifier along with measured results discussed in the paper. The amplifier designed in the frequency range of 100MHz to 6.0 GHz. The broadband gain block MMIC amplifier offers the small signal gain of 10dB with gain flatness of ±2dB. The design based on a GaAs pHEMT process. A single stage design approach chosen to meet the gain of proposed specifications. It works on single drain supply voltage of +5V and draws the current of 70mA typically. A current mirror circuit used in the design to provide the stable gate bias. This MMIC realized in the die dimensions of $0.9 \times 1.0 \times$ 0.1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Finally, it is packaged into SOT-89 package.

articleTitle: Design &Developement of Monolithic IQ mixer using UMS PH25 GaAs process at 5400±125 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and development of a C band monolithic passive IQ mixer using $0.25 {\mu} \mathrm{m} -\mathrm{p}-$HEMT process of UMS foundry is presented here. In the Mixer design, power divider and rat-race coupler are based on lumped element approach to reduce the chip area, Quadrature hybrid is designed using power divider approach, where required phase difference obtained using equivalent lumped model of RH/LH transmission line at the output ports of power divider. This topology reduces the size of circuits at low frequency as well as provides wide bandwidth operation of hybrid. The on-wafer measurements of fabricated large production of MMIC mixer shows typical conversion loss of 13dB with 0.8 dB flatness over the RF frequency $5400 \pm 125$ MHz and IF frequency DC-125 MHz, along with LO to RF isolation better than 35 dB. The mixer was simulated, ruggedized for improved yield and tested at three different LO powers to ensure less sensitivity of mixer with temperature dependent LO power variation. The obtained yield is very good and 100% fabricated MMIC’s are fully functional and validates high production yield.

articleTitle: PIN Diodes Integrated Switchable Trans-Receiver Short Range Radar Antenna for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Short Range Radar (SRR) antenna for automotive applications is proposed in this paper. Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) slot array antenna at 24 GHz is designed to operate in SRR mode. The slots are designed in a 2x4 arrangement in the SIW slot antenna array, where lx2 Y junction power divider is implemented in which each arm of the power divider feeds the lx4 slotted array. Here, the same SIW-slot radiator can act as the transmitting and receiving antenna based on the status (ON/OFF) of the two RF PIN diodes, placed in the ground plane of the antenna. To obtain the proposed transceiver functionality of-the-shelf DSG9500-000 RF PIN diodes are used in this work. The designed transceiver yields a maximum gain of 7.72 dBi and 4 dBi in in the receiving and the transmitting mode respectively. The proposed idea finds application in the field of short range radar which focuses on parking assistance, pre-crash sensing, blind spot detection, obstacle detection.

articleTitle: An Ultrawideband 5G Interference Mitigation Filter for C-Band Ground Based SATCOM Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a compact and high Q microwave filter with stringent rejection and group delay requirement for C-Band ground receiver applications to mitigate terrestrial 5G interference. The proposed filter is designed using coaxial interdigital resonators with non-resonating nodes. The filter provides more than 60 dB rejection in the frequency band of 3.3-3.67 GHz and more than 30 dB rejection above 4.23 GHz. The designed filter is ultra-wideband with 13% fractional bandwidth at 3950 MHz. Filter is compact (185 mm length), light-weight (mass about 300 gms), and designed with WR-229 waveguide interface.

articleTitle: Electrical and Thermal Design of ka-band Dual- Anode Electron Gun with PPM Focusing for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Space Traveling Wave Tubes (TWTs) have special constraints pertaining to compact size, less weight, and high-efficiency requirements. In order to achieve these design objectives, each and every component of the space TWT has to be designed taking into account these space requirements. In this work, the authors have designed a dual-anode electron gun for ka-band space TWT, which offers the flexibility to change the beam current through telemetry command remotely during its operation to compensate for unintended performance degradation. The capability for tuning the beam current is offered by changing the control anode voltage, which is studied in detail in this paper. After optimizing the electron gun design for desired beam parameters, the design of a periodic permanent magnet (PPM) structure has also been carried out. The optimization of the PPM structural parameters and magnetic field values to attain a confined flow of electron beam with less scalloping percentage has been carried out. The thermal analysis of the dual-anode electron gun has also been performed to study the temperature distribution and thermal displacements within the electron gun to ensure the safety limits.

articleTitle: Design of Single-Ended and Differential Power Amplifiers using SiGe HBT for SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the load-pull measured performance of two cascode power cells along with simulation performance of two matched power amplifiers (PAs) at Ku-band for Satcom applications. The two cascode power cells are fabricated in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. At 18GHz, Load-pull measurements show 18.6dBm/19.5dBm of output power with 48.3%/51.2% of PAE at P1dB/P3dB. A single-ended PA and a differential matched PAs are designed using the cascode power cells as building blocks. Simulation results show that the single-ended PA achieves an 18.5dB of small signal gain and 20.5dBm of output power with 44% PAE at 3dB compression point. Using EM simulated low-loss baluns at input and output, the differential PA has shown 5dB improvement in small signal gain with similar large signal performance.

articleTitle: Transitional Study of Diverse Geometrical Patch Antennas with Secure Unitary Physical Size, Ground Plane, Excitation Feed, and Impedance Matching Point
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study explores transitions from a simple secure fundamental unitary square patch to a secure unitary circular patch, maintaining a constant physical patch area, ground plane size, and coaxially fed fixed ratio excitation point. Transition shape-geometry includes the square (unitary fundamental), rectangle, pentagon, hexagon, and circle. At each transition shape, critical antenna parameters such as the resonant frequency, VSWR, and radiation pattern have been studied using HFSS software and the transitional differences are analyzed and compared. Key findings include a tendency for weak resonances that exists at the fundamental resonant frequency of the unitary square patch across all the transitional patch shapes, featuring a strong dependency of resonance frequency on patch geometry, a shift in resonant frequency towards the higher side of the frequency spectrum, and a significant influence of transition shapes on patch antenna radiation patterns. The study crusade that a combination of shapes-geometric patterns can be utilized to synthesize higher resonant frequencies, realize multiple operational bandwidths, and enable a distinct radiation pattern while maintaining fixed physical attributes. Validation is demonstrated through a simulated combinatorial half-square and half-circle patch of constant unitary area. This analysis presents essential insights for creating signature unitary-pixel patch antennas, tailored for specific application scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of Radio Frequency Power Amplifier Module at C-Band for Data Communication Link
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a radio frequency power amplifier module for the C-band data communication link. The power stage is designed using a gallium nitride device in the hybrid microwave integrated circuit technology to achieve good efficiency and linearity. The designed matching network achieves the matching loads obtained from load-pull analysis, while keeping harmonics short at the intrinsic current generator reference plane of the device. The driver amplifier and gain stages are also optimally chosen to obtain high gain of the entire module without deteriorating the linearity. This power amplifier module operates from 4.6–5.0 GHz while delivering maximum output power upto 43.8 dBm in measurement. The measured maximum drain efficiency of the designed power stage is 53.2% at saturation with an EVM of 6% and adjacent channel power ratio of more than 30 dBc.

articleTitle: Strategies to achieve high brightness in collinear Sagnac polarization entangled photon source
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Entangled photon source is a basic building block of various quantum technologies such as quantum communication, QKD, quantum metrology, etc. Spontaneous parametric down conversion (SPDC) process is widely reported method for generation of entanglement due to its ease of implementation and stable performance. In this paper, we report design and development of type-II Sagnac loop based entangled photon source with a high brightness of $8.42\times 10^{4}$ pairs/s/mW with 98.18% visibility, a CHSH inequality violation of S=2.777±0.006 and state fidelity of 97.8%. An automated test setup has also been developed for carrying out the measurements. The essential formulated design procedure to achieve optimal performance has been discussed and presented. The measured performance of developed source is also compared to other reported sources having the same configuration. In this work, higher brightness is achieved with comparable fidelity to previously reported works. This methodology can be extended to any collinear Sagnac loop based entangled photon sources.

Author Keywords: Type-II Periodically Poled Potassium Titanyl Phosphate (PPKTP)

articleTitle: Antenna Array Fault Diagnosis Using Particle Swarm Optimized CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents particle swarm optimized convolutional neural network (PSO-CNN) for antenna array fault diagnosis. The CNN hyperparameters are tuned by employing two evolutionary algorithms separately and their performance is discussed. Fault scenarios dataset of 4 X 4 planar antenna array is generated using Ansys HFSS and CNN model is implemented using Tensorflow 2.6.0 Google platform. Three kind of faults; the feed point fault, network fault and fault at patch are is addressed in this paper. The result of fault diagnosis using PSO-CNN is compared with genetic algorithm optimized CNN (GACNN). The 100% fault diagnosis accuracy with 0.3 validation split is achieved for PSO-CNN with improved computational time and less model complexity.

articleTitle: FSS Integrated Hybrid Nanocomposite Microwave Absorber Structure for Stealth Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a hybrid microwave absorber (MA) comprising the frequency selective surfaces (FSS) and a thin lossy nanocomposite sheet, for stealth technology in the X-band (8.2-12.4 GHz) is proposed. The first step here requires the synthesis of exfoliated graphite (EG) and the barium strontium titanate (BST) fillers using the microwave-assisted intercalation and sol-gel techniques, respectively. The EG (4 wt%) and BST (10 wt%) fillers are then embedded into the epoxy resin to obtain the EGBST lossy nanocomposite sheet. The reflection coefficient (S11) of up to 13.7 dB covering a 10-dB absorption bandwidth of 1.94 GHz from 7.92-9.86 GHz is attained for this nanocomposite sheet having 2.1 mm thickness. Afterwards, the EGBST nanocomposite sheet is integrated with an optimized FSS layer to realize a hybrid MA (HMA) structure to enhance the overall absorption bandwidth. The optimized HMA structure enhances the 10-dB absorption bandwidth of the resultant sample to 3.67 GHz (8.12-11.79 GHz) covering 90% of X-band for a thickness of just 2 mm $(\sim \lambda / 15)$, attaining a minimum reflection coefficient of $-28 \mathrm{~dB}$. The proposed nanocomposite-based hybrid microwave absorber can potentially be used for the radar applications conforming to the stealth technology.

articleTitle: Low Profile Broadband Wheel Shaped Resistive-FSS Glass Composite for Aerospace Stealth Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We present the design of a wheel-shaped resistive frequency selective surface (RFSS) based ultra-broadband radar absorber working for 5.2.-18.7 GHz. The proposed absorber has been designed using customized resistive material having a surface resistance value of $270 \Omega / \square$, employing aerograde glass fiber reinforced plastics (GFRP) laminate as a substrate material. The bottom layer has been terminated using a carbon - fibre reinforced plastics (CFRP) layer, which acts as a ground plane. The proposed RFSS absorber has been implemented and simulated with the help of CST microwave studio; the simulation result shows a minimum 10 dB reflection loss (RC) in the designated frequency, which covers C, X, and Ku bands. Typical absorption characteristics show fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 113%, with $0.044 \lambda \mathrm{L}$ (where $\lambda \mathrm{L}$ is the cutoff wavelength at 10 dB) thickness. The simulated design has been implemented for fabrication and validated experimentally, showing a close mutual agreement. The proposed absorber is thin (2.5mm) in nature, polarization insensitive (0° −90°), possesses good angular stability (0° −50°), and is easy to fabricate using a customized substrate, which makes it a potential candidate for aerospace stealth design.

articleTitle: A Study on Contactless Flexible Antenna-Based Motion Sensor for Smart Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Wireless sensing plays a major role in expanding the applications towards smart technologies, especially for motion detection in IoT applications. The RF signal between the presented transmitting and receiving antenna pair is used for smart motion detection. Both the transmitting and the receiving antennas were designed to operate at 2.44 GHz resonant frequency. The simulated gain of the transmitting and the receiving antenna is 3.22 dBi and 1.10 dBi respectively. The receiving antenna is made flexible to accommodate conformal applications. Here the received power level of the RF signal at the receiving antenna is used as a parameter for motion detection sensing. The power attenuated is different for different obstructions, where almost no attenuation is observed for dielectrics and the attenuated power is significant for metals and humans. This theory helps in expanding contactless technologybased motion sensing for smart-home applications.

articleTitle: High-Performance Slotted Patch Crossovers for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Crossovers are specialized devices that facilitate the transmission of signals while eliminating the need for incorporating three-dimensional structures that are not in a planar arrangement. By integrating patch crossovers into Radio Frequency (RF) systems, the overall configuration becomes simplified, resulting in cost savings and ease of manufacturing.
