The current body of literature presents a distinctive, efficient, yet straightforward methodology for the design and development of RF Slotted Patch Crossovers (SPCs) with enhanced performance characteristics. By introducing rectangular slots into the existing reported crossovers, various benefits are stimulated such as enhanced isolation, size reduction, reduced insertion loss, and improved impedance matching. This manuscript elucidates an augmentation approach, which is equally applicable for a variety of patch crossovers, including configurations such as squares, circles, and hexagons. Additionally, a parametric analysis has been conducted to assess the impact of varying various design parameters in different crossover configurations. The optimized design of presented SPC, improves the isolation from $-15 \mathrm{~dB}$ to $30 \mathrm{~dB}$ and the patch area is reduced by 33 percent compared to their non slotted counterparts.

articleTitle: Broadband Millimeter Wave MIMO Antennas at 28 GHz with Low Mutual Coupling Using Frequency Selective Surface Wall
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Multiple input multiple out (MIMO) gains a lot of attention in the current and future generation (5G/6G) wireless communication. This paper presents two new designs of 2-element and 4-element MIMO antennas with low mutual coupling at millimeter wave regime. The two MIMO antennas are optimized to operate over 5G new radio band n261 (27.5-28.35 GHz). The substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) based cavity-backed slot antenna with a gap-coupled parasitic patch is used for the MIMO element. A new dual-layer frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed to suppress the space wave coupling between the antennas. The FSS exhibits wideband second-order bandstop filter response, which reflects the RF signal between 25.99 to 30.06 GHz with $\left|S_{21}\right|\lt -20 \mathrm{~dB}$. The FSS is placed vertically between the antennas to obtain isolation of > 49.9 dB and > 24.4 dB for the 2-element and 4-element MIMOs at the center frequency. When all the elements are excited with equal amplitude and equal phase, the designed MIMOs show a peak realized gain and efficiency of 9.89 dBi and 97.1 % for 2-element and 10.84 and 94 % for 4-element. Both MIMO arrays exhibit a low cross-polarization <−12.44 dB and <−18.5 dB and good diversity performances.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz Transformer Coupled Low Power Quadrature VCO using Ring Inductor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a 60 GHz transformer coupled low power quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (QVCO) using a single turn ring inductor. The single turn inductor is shared by the pair of oscillators. A digital cap bank is used for fine tuning of the oscillator. The circuit is designed in 65 nm CMOS process. The frequency of the oscillator is tuned from 59.5 to 60.5 GHz. The proposed 60 GHz QVCO exhibits a phase noise of −81 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset frequency. The DC power consumption is 3.3 mW with a supply voltage of 1 V. As per the authors’ knowledge, this work has the lowest DC power consumption and a competitive figure-of-merit with good quadrature accuracy compared to all other published millimeter wave CMOS QVCOs.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Reflectarray antenna for Full-Duplex Communication at Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a reflectarray antenna exhibiting dual-polarized characteristics and operating in the frequency of 27. 4-28.1 GHz. The dual-polarization in the reflectarray is obtained by illuminating the polarization-insensitive surface with a dual-polarized microstrip patch antenna. The reflectarray surface consists of 17 x17 unit cells, with a cell size of 0.47$\lambda$x0.47$\lambda$. The f/d of the antenna is 0.4, which signifies the compactness of the design. The aperture efficiency of the design is 20%, and it demonstrates a maximum gain of 22 dBi in beams that are polarized orthogonally. The proposed design provides a method to obtain dual polarization where the two ports of the patch antenna can be excited to get two orthogonally polarized radiation fields. The antenna can find application in full-duplex mm-wave communication. The concept of the design is practically fabricated and verified through measurement. The simulated and practical results show a good agreement.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Perturbated Dielectric Resonator MIMO Antenna Coupled with sectored Ring-shape Feeding for mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A perturbed Dielectric Resonator based MIMO Antenna Coupled with sectored Ring-shaped Feeding is proposed for 5G millimeter wave Applications. The feeding is used to generate circular polarization in DR. The introduction of triangular perturbation in ring shaped DRA with optimized dimensions helps to obtain wide impedance bandwidth, which is 23.56GHz-24.9GHz. Consequently, the highest efficiency of 98.4% in desired frequency bands and the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 5.5% have been observed. The MIMO antenna performance is justified by computing the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (dB).

articleTitle: Potential of 3D-Printed Helical Antenna for Kuband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an additively manufactured helical antenna designed for application in the Ku band, spanning the frequency range of 10.5 GHz to 14.5 GHz. The design of this antenna incorporates a method for optimizing impedance, thereby enhancing bandwidth, and it is bolstered by a robust support structure that ensures antenna stability. Measured results shows the antenna's exceptional performance, characterized by a return loss of under -10dB across the 10.5GHz-14.5GHz ultrawide wideband frequency range, accompanied by an impressively broad-side antenna beamwidth of about 35° to 40°. Within the primary radiation lobe, the axial ratio remains below 3 dB, a testament to the manufacturing precision. The proposed manufacturing and design approach represents a significant leap towards enabling intricate antenna geometries, paving the way for technological advancements. This band antenna emerges as a vital asset for satellite communication and holds substantial potential within the realm of ultra-wideband communication systems.

articleTitle: High Power RF & Microwave Tube based heating systems at IPR and its applications to Plasma
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The high Power RF and Microwave systems are used to carry out plasma heating experiments on tokamaks SST1 and Aditya-U. A 35-65 MHz frequency tunable tetrode based RF system capable to deliver 1.5 MW power has been commissioned successfully on dummy load and the source has been integrated with the ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) system for SST-1 Tokamak. A 3.7GHz Klystron based heating system is employed to carry out current drive experiments on SST-1 and Aditya-U. Several experiments have been carried out with lower hybrid current drive and in SST-1 maximum 0.65s long plasma shot is achieved with LHCD. A 42GHz Gyrotron based ECRH system has been commissioned on tokamaks SST-1 and Aditya-U and several experiments related to plasma breakdown and heating have been carried out in both the tokamaks. One more high power source 170 GHz-1MW CW Gyrotron has been commissioned successfully on the dummy load, this system confirms the ITER relevant performance and also the capability to test the megawatt level microwave sources at IPR.

articleTitle: Design & Development of W-Band Monopulse Slotted Waveguide Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes an inventive design of monopulse slotted waveguide array antenna (SWAA) at Wband. The antenna is configured in four layers consisting of 2400 radiating slots arranged in circular aperture with 44$\lambda$ diameter. A 54 x 54 W-band planar SWAA with monopulse comparator in half-height waveguide configuration is depicted here. This multilayer antenna is designed, modeled and analyzed using MATLAB, Ansys HFSS electromagnetic suite & CST microwave studio EM simulation software. It comprises of integrated feeding network and monopulse comparator that are realized in a single layer in back to back configuration. The simulated results show good results with a sum pattern gain of 40 dB, side-lobe level (SLL) is -16.2 dB in H-plane and -18.4 dB in E-plane. The sum pattern beamwidth is $1.42^{\circ} \pm 0.1^{\circ}$ in both planes with radiation efficiency of 75%. The crossover of difference channels in E-plane is 5.1dB and 4.8dB in H-plane and the null depth is more than 41 dB with respect to sum peak in both planes. A proto unit antenna is developed and measured, achieved very good monopulse pattern in both E and H-planes. The measured return loss is more than 15 dB in the desired bandwidth of 800MHz at W-band.

articleTitle: Automated Quad Detector Based Acquisition and Tracking System for Free Space Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: For satellite based optical communication network, acquisition, tracking and pointing (ATP) is inevitable as the laser beam is innately narrow. Performance of ATP system will ultimately be the yardstick of success of optical communication terminal. The ultimate target of this development is to acquire, point and track two remotely located optical communication terminal moving with a relative velocity or spacecraft moving against a stationary ground station. In this work we have demonstrate stare-scan approach of ATP. The transmitting beacon is stationary and receive station has spiral tracking provision for acquiring. Here we have developed an automated mechanism to acquire a terminal using quad detector and gimbal. The experimental detail and measurement at different modes are explained. The future scope of work is also defined.

Author Keywords: Quad detector error voltages (Left-Right L-R and Bottom-Top (B-T))

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Facet Gaps in X-band Origami based Deployable Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the X-band 1.2 m dia deployable origami-based prime focal reflectarray antenna and its study for various facet gaps. The phase-correcting surface has been populated with criss-cross-type subwavelength-based unit cells. The surface has been segmented as per the spiral z-fold and monolithic gores-based origami pattern. The stowing and deployment of the segmented flat surface are detailed in the manuscript and discussed concerning the mechanical constraints to maintain the facet gaps, which accommodates the thick layer stack up of the unit cell and conveys the deployment motion. The RFA with various facet gaps is modeled and analyzed to perform the impact analysis of the facet gap on the secondary performance. It is shown that a 4 mm facet gap results in a 36.72 dBi gain at 9.6 GHz, whereas a 10 mm facet gap offers a 35.80 dBi gain. The significant gain loss is observed with the variation of facet gap and is explained by the reduction in the percent effective aperture area.

articleTitle: Compact Phased Array Antenna Integrated With CRLH Based Digital Phase Shifter for X-Band Radar and Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new compact planar phased array antenna for X-band radar and satellite communication applications. For designing the antenna array, linear 4-elements circular patch using aperture coupled feeding was utilized. The array is combined with a novel composite right/left-handed (CRLH) metamaterial phase shifter. In this work, the phase shifter is designed to obtain digital phase bits of $5.625^{\circ}, 11.25^{\circ}, 22.5^{\circ}$, and 45° by cascading CRLH unit cells. The phase shifter exhibits low insertion loss of <1.87dB at the center frequency 10 GHz with return losses >10dB. The proposed phased array exhibits a peak gain of 7.81 dBi, whose radiating beam can be steered over different scan angles ranging from -16° to +14°. At the highest scan angle, the side lobe level is $\lt _{-}$11.4dB, and the co-to cross-polarization isolation is >22.4dB.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Markerless Activity Tracking System for Supporting Aging and Wellness
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a mm-Wave radar-based system to create a novel method of tracking seniors and monitoring them using ambient wireless signals. Radar sensors, coupled with deep learning models, facilitate the identification of various physical activities without requiring physical contact or the use of wearable devices. The system employs range-Doppler maps derived from a real-life in-home activities dataset for training deep learning networks. The gated recurrent units (GRU) model is chosen for real-time implementation due to its optimal trade-off between speed and accuracy. The system achieves an overall accuracy of 93% for trained subjects, with 86% accuracy for classifying the in-home physical activities of a new subject. Additionally, the system captures the frequency of washroom use, sedentary, duration of sleep, active and out-of-home periods, the level of activity performed by the subject over a period of time, current activity state, and gait parameters.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Schottky Diode based Sub-Harmonic Mixers at 230GHz and 345GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of Schottky diode based sub-harmonic mixers (SHM), a core component which governs the sensitivity of the mm/sub-mm wave receivers at 230GHz and 345GHz. The SHMs are modeled in microstrip topology with quartz substrate housed in waveguide split-block configuration using anti-parallel Schottky diode pair (APDP) as non-linear element. Global design simulation method (GDM) is opted for the design in which circuit is decomposed into small functional blocks and simulated to optimize the SHM performance. Advanced Design System (ADS) and High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) tools are used for non-linear simulations and integrated 3D electromagnetic (EM) simulations, respectively. The prototype designs were fabricated and characterized. The fabricated prototypes provide noise temperatures of 715K and 830K for 230GHz and 345GHz SHMs, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Substrate Integrated Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) fed by Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line for Millimeter Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel substrate integrated dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) fed by Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line. In contrast to the traditional Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) configuration, which has an extra cylindrical dielectric resonator as its primary radiating element, the presented technology utilizes the identical substrate as a feasible alternative to traditional Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRAs), offering several advantages in terms of improved effectiveness, regulated radiation pattern, and compactness. The proposed methodology involves the implementation of DRA structure, which is achieved by utilizing a circular ring encased structure composed of metallic vias. The field distribution attained in the suggested Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) has similarities to the $\mathrm{H E M}_{12 \delta}$ mode of the standard cylindrical DRA. The proposed DRA achieves a broadside unidirectional beam with a gain of 6.3 dBi at 28 GHz. The design technique proposed in this study facilitates the decrease in size and complexity of assembling a dielectric over the feed network, as compared to standard approaches. In essence, this work introduces a straightforward and inventive methodology for designing DRA (Dielectric Resonator Antennas) that effectively addresses the obstacles associated with fabrication and design of planar and compact designs in millimeter wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Beam Scanning Circular Conformal Vivaldi Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This communication presents a Vivaldi antenna with $S_{11}$ less than −10 dB from 4.3 GHz to 9.8 GHz with a realized gain of 8.3 dBi at 7 GHz. A $1\times 7$ circular conformal antenna array consisting of a Vivaldi antenna as a radiating element is designed and has a beam scanning capability of ±45° along the $\phi=90^{\circ}$ plane. The proposed array has a good gain, low sidelobe level, and beam steering capabilities and finds applications in weather radar and amateur radio. Ansys HFSS full-wave simulator is used for design and optimization.

articleTitle: A Compact Aerodynamic-Shaped High Beam-Squint tilted Folded Slot Antenna for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Data-Link Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports the development of a compact aerodynamic-shaped tilted slot antenna having high beam-squint and backside radiation when mounted at the rear-section of high speed unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) or Drone at L-band for data-link applications. A conformal slot has been folded to realize 3D slot to reduce the overall footprint. The 3D slot is tilted 45 degrees to squint the radiation pattern towards back side of UAV from the boresight when mounted on UAV section. The tilted 3D slot is excited with a 50 Ohm SMA connector in end-launch configuration and is filled with Rexolite material to further reduce the size and to protect the antenna parts from environmental degradations. The final antenna is aerodynamic-shaped backed by a tunnel for other RF hardware integration. The overall size of slot is 0.2λ x 0.15λ x 0.09λ while size of antenna is 0.31λ x 0.21λ x 0.18λ at L-band having 20% impedance bandwidth, 5.75dBi peak gain, 127 degrees x 94 degrees beamwidth, 50 degrees tilt from the boresight and high-power handling capability at least upto 200W limited by the SMA connector. A prototype is fabricated and experimentally evaluated to validate the performance.

articleTitle: Novel Dual-mode Reconfigurable Polarizer for Wideband Linear-Circular Transmission and Reflection Operating in Same Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study explores a novel wideband reconfigurable polarizer for K/Ka-band applications. The design consists of two metallic layers: two frequency selective surfaces printed on either side of the low-loss dielectric substrate. Here, the RF pin diode is mounted on the backside of the substrate for switching the device state electronically. The polarizer converts the linearly polarized signal into a circular one with a 3 dB Axial Ratio from 19-28.52 GHz during transmission (OFF state) and 23.87-30.12 GHz during reflection (ON state). In addition, it can convert into cross-polarization with an effective 90% Polarization Conversion Ratio from 32.04-43.96 GHz in reflection mode. The Transfer Matrix Method is used to analyse the polarization conversion mechanism. Surface current distributions can easily demonstrate plasmonic resonances responsible for this multiple conversion. The design performance is investigated for different oblique angles under Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) modes. The proposed polarizer is compact and occupies an electrical dimension of $0.152\lambda_{L} \times 0.190\lambda_{L}$ and an overall thickness of $0.051\lambda_{L}$. Here, $\lambda_{L}$ is the free-space wavelength corresponding to the lowest operating frequency. The design novelty lies in its compactness and the different polarization conversions in the reflection and transmission operating in the same frequency band with better angular stability.

articleTitle: The Implementation of CPML for the Improved HIE-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article introduces an implementation of the convolutional perfectly matched layer (CPML) boundary condition for the improved hybrid implicit explicit finite-difference time-domain (HIE-FDTD) method. The study includes a numerical investigation to validate the effectiveness of the convolutional PML (CPML) implementation, as well as an assessment of its performance. Additionally, the numerical simulations of the proposed convolutional PML (CPML) implementation compared with the traditional HIE-FDTD and leapfrog HIE-FDTD methods. The results of the simulation study indicate that the proposed convolutional PML (CPML) implementation on the improved HIE-FDTD method exhibits comparatively weakly conditional stability when compared with the regular traditional HIE and the leapfrog HIE-FDTD methods.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Large Reflect Array Antenna With and Without faceted for SAR System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the performance comparison of a 1.2 m large reflectarray (RFA) antenna with and without faceted for modern Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) application. In the absence of faceting in the RFA, it faces the issue of narrow bandwidth due to the small frequency operating of unit-cell and spatial path delay. The RFA geometry is designed by faceting the phase-compensating surface into single and double-axis configurations that provide true-time delay and improve spatial bandwidth. The phase distribution across the RFA surface and variation in the gain with frequency are computed using a PMOM method with the help of TICRA software. The results show that single and double-faceted RFAs improve the volume reduction by about 1/3 and 1/7 part of the overall volume of flat RFA. However, it reduces the gain. The proposed RFA contains a simple membrane-based design, hence containing approximately 1 Kg weight of standard parabolic reflector. The simulated results showed that single-axis faceted RFA achieves 39dB gain with ±0.5 dB variation in an improvement for the desired band. On the other hand, further improvement in double-axis faceted can improve the gain and significantly reduce the overall volume compared to a similar type of performance of parabolic reflector.

Author Keywords: without faceted and single & double axis faceted RFA

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Wide-Band Directional Antenna using A Dual-Layer Tapered Shape Artificial Magnetic Conductor Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper the design of a low-profile wide-band directional antenna using a dual layer tapered shape artificial magnetic conductor conductor is presented. It consists of a wideband bow-tie slot antenna backed by $5 \times 5$ unit cell array of artificial magnetic conductor. The proposed antenna leverages the advantages of dual-layer AMC configuration, combining their effects to achieve enhanced bandwidth and radiation characteristics. The dual-layer AMC provides the ±90 degrees reflection phase bandwidth of 1.92 GHz. The proposed wide-band directional antenna operates from 4.04 GHz to 10.62 GHz thus exhibits −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 89.68%. The overall dimensions of the proposed antenna are $60 \mathrm{~mm} \times 60 \mathrm{~mm} \times 6.7 \mathrm{~mm}$. It also exhibits peak gain improvement of 3.57 dB at 5.0 GHz and 4.32 dB at 7.6 GHz when compared to the antenna without AMC.

articleTitle: Ka-band Dual-Anode Electron Gun, Beam focusing system and SWS for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A electron gun of perveance $0.22 \mu$ p has been designed for Ka-band helix Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) which would ultimately have application in satellite communication system. Convergent electron gun with isolated beam forming electrode (BFE) & M-Type dispenser cathode with 3.1mm button diameter has been designed using codes EGUN. It consists of two isolated anodes namely control anode, ion barrier anode in addition to ground accelerating shaver anode to meet the requirement of long life & high reliability. Periodic Permanent (PPM) focusing structure has been designed using Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Col<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf> high intensity magnet in order to reduce the size & weight of the overall TWT. Confined flow beam focusing has been adopted. A compact small size electron gun assembly has been designed using ceramic insulator & suitable support structure with due considerations for high voltage and thermal requirements. High voltage analysis has been carried out using code ESTAT and ANSYS for thermal analysis. Dual anode electron gun, focusing system and slow wave structure (SWS) has been experimentally validated by developing and testing Ka-band TWT prototypes having rated potentials. The design and experimental results are in close agreement.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Polarization Independent Transparent FSS for Dual-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) tailored for dual-band wireless applications. The design comprises multiple C-shaped geometries, which collectively generate a dual-band response achieved by utilizing top and bottom mirror geometry techniques. The proposed structure’s dimensions measure 9 mm $\times$ 9 mm. This singlelayer FSS establishes two pass-bands at 5.82 GHz and 8.96 GHz, each characterized by bandwidths of 1.26 GHz and 1.62 GHz, respectively. The pass-band frequencies of the FSS design can be controlled independently by modifying a singular parameter of the unit cell. The dual-band pass FSS, designed using miniaturized elements, also showcases remarkable resonance stability for varying polarizations and incident angles. The transparent and compact nature of this FSS design renders it applicable across a diverse spectrum of dual-band pass wireless scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and development of high power broadband proximity coupled microstrip array antenna for monopulse RADAR.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper investigated and presented proximity coupled microstrip radiating antenna array at X-Band for monopulse radar application. Feed network designed on thin bottom layer and linear polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna (MPA) designed on top layer. Comparator realized with four quadrature hybrids on feeding layer to realize monopulse network. Thin feeding layer with $0.66 {\lambda}_{0}$ inter element spacing selected in antenna to achieve low sidelobe level (SLL). Feeding layer substrate selected to handle high peak and average powers. Simulated & optimized the design using commercially available electromagnetic software. Bonding film used to attach feeding network with radiating layer. $8.3 \lambda_{0}$ size $(\Phi 280 \mathrm{~mm})$ circular aperture with uniform distribution incorporated. The antenna shows 600MHz Return Loss (RL) and pattern bandwidths, with gain of greater than 26dBi and SLL of less than −19 dB. It is proposed to use for monopulse RADAR application.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Ku-Band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) with Ultra-Low Noise Figure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, we propose a Ku-band low noise amplifier (LNA) that employs a small signal equivalent circuit model of high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT). The design uses a conventional capacitive feedback matching network technique that maximizes the gains and minimizing noise figure (NF), input, output, and isolation losses. Gallium nitride (GaN) HEMT technology is used, which aids in developing a low-noise figure and guarantees the compatibility of the developed LNA for Ku-band space utilization. The proposed LNA based on GaN HEMT de-sign offers gain values of 38.6 dB and 33.4 dB, respectively, at 12 GHz and 18 GHz, with extremely low noise figures of 0.90 dB and 1.01 dB. The input and output return losses over the complete band of operation are better than 12 dB. Notably, for the desired frequency range of 12-18 GHz, the K and Mu values are more significant than unity. The Keysight advanced design system (ADS) is used for performing simulations.

articleTitle: Design and Development of RF-based Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces the design and implementation of an RF-based system for detecting Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The system is composed of an RF module, an automated Pan and Tilt Unit (PTU), and IoTs. The RF module comprises a receiving antenna, a Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA), and a Software-Defined Radio (SDR). With high sensitivity, it can detect RF re-emissions originating from the UAV controller, even at a signal strength as low as -60dBm. The design of the RF module primarily targets the frequency range of 2–6GHz, aligning with the commonly allocated frequencies for civil and commercial UAV applications, which are 2.45/5.8GHz. In conjunction with the RF module and IoT elements, the PTU facilitates azimuthal rotation scanning from 0 to 360 degrees and elevation scanning ranging from 0 to 75 degrees, effectively covering the desired surveillance area. To validate the integrated system, testing is conducted within an anechoic chamber. This controlled environment emulates the UAV setup scenario, featuring single or multiple signal sources at various spatial points and time instances. The comprehensive testing affirms the system’s successful performance, meeting predefined criteria. The system’s efficacy is underscored by the discernible RF radiation patterns received from distinct emitters and their respective spatial parameters.

articleTitle: Null Steering Using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the utilization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) to generate adjustable nulls. The inspiration for this approach arises from the shifting nulls in the radiation pattern of a dipole placed in front of a rectangular patch, which occurs as the patch is laterally moved. The RIS is harnessed to emulate this displacement, accomplished by strategically biasing specific diodes to achieve reconfigurability.

articleTitle: Design of Flame-Retardant, Hydrophobic, Ultrathin, Lightweight and Flexible EMI shielding Fabric and Sheets for Defense, Space & Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the fabrication of flame retardant, hydrophobic, lightweight, ultrathin fabric and sheet samples with very high EMI shielding properties. In this study, a PVDF polymer solution with pre-optimized concentrations of highly conductive nanofillers containing exfoliated graphite, carbon nanofiber, and silver nanoparticles is prepared. This conductive polymer solution is directly mold cast to make a sheet sample and the same solution is coated over cotton fabric to make a fabric sample. The FESEM images show the random distribution of nanofillers forming a conductive network, while TGA analysis confirms the high flame retardancy of these samples up to 300°C. The sheet sample shows a high EMI shielding efficiency of more than 37 dB in the complete X-band for a thickness of 0.20 mm as compared to the fabric sample, which shows more than 20 dB shielding efficiency in the complete X-band for a thickness of 0.315 mm. The high shielding value is achieved due to the formation of a continuous 3D conductive network of nanofiller across the whole body of sheet samples as compared to the fabric-based sample. The experimental results suggest that these samples could be applied for various military, space, and industrial applications.

articleTitle: AI/ML: A powerful tool for future microwave engineering problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The potential futuristic role of Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) in microwave and antenna engineering is discussed in this paper. In context to electro-magnetic circuit design, a brief overview of the AI/ML tools is presented. The current applications are briefly touched upon, and the future research directions are outlined. The authors hope that this paper will encourage early-stage researchers to consider choosing AI/ML techniques to efficiently resolve compound engineering problems involving electromagnetic field analysis. In doing so, some striking examples are cited from the scientific literature.

articleTitle: Alternate Design of the Waveguide Coaxial Coupling System of Ku Band Helix Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The objective of the waveguide coupling system at the output side of Travelling Wave Tube (TWT) is to extract amplified RF power from helix to the waveguide plumbing line. For this purpose, a waveguide coupling system is design using ANSYS HFSS in the frequency range of 11.5 to 13.5 GHz. Typically, waveguide-coupling system has been designed to extract high RF output power. Failure of the braze joint of coaxial coupling system due to multiple heat cycle is common problem of the broadband helix TWT. Failure of this joint result in to break of vacuum seal of the TWT, hence complete TWT failure. To solve this issue, in this paper authors have proposed alternative design of the waveguide coaxial coupling system to improve the yield of the coaxial coupling system. The proposed alternate design of the waveguide coaxial coupling system has improved return loss characteristics and leak proof joint rate, hence reduces overall all failure of the helix TWT.

articleTitle: Wideband Microstrip Patch Antenna Loaded with Double J-Shaped Slots for Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband microstrip patch antenna (MPA). The antenna consists of double J-shaped slots loaded on the patch and a partial ground plane. The wideband characteristic is obtained by using the J-shaped slots. The effect of structural parameters such as the width and the location of slots on the antenna performance is investigated. This antenna is constructed to operate at 3.5 GHz with a $10-\text{dB}$ fractional bandwidth (FBW) of $70.8 \%(2.53 \text{GHz}$ to $5.3 \text{GHz})$, radiation efficiency better than $90 \%$, and gain of 2.62 dBi. The antenna has a size of $45 \text{mm} \times 41 \text{mm}\left(0.88 \lambda_{\text{g}} \times 0.81 \lambda_{\text{g}}\right)$. The proposed antenna is suitable for WiMAX and sub- $6 \text{GHz} 5 \text{G}$ applications primarily for smartphones, access points, and IoT devices.

articleTitle: Study of a Low-Profile Substrate Integrated Waveguide based Bidirectional Dual-beam Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper showcases a single-layer, compact substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) based dual-beam bidirectional array antenna. The SIW is constructed using Rogers-8580 substrate with copper cladding on both sides. One end of the waveguide is fed through a 504$\omega$ microstrip line, while the other end is terminated with metal vias. To get array performance with a bidirectional pattern, some slots are cut strategically from the upper and lower metal walls of the following waveguide. A comparative analysis is conducted between this antenna and a one-sided slotted SIW array. The proposed antenna array radiates in bi-direction, yielding a realized gain of 7.5dBi, fractional bandwidth of 1.5%, and cross-polarization difference (XPD) of 29dB.

articleTitle: Dual Linearly Polarized Common Aperture Microstrip Antenna for S- and C-Band Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript presents the design and development of an S-/C-band common aperture microstrip antenna. It is dual linearly polarized at both bands. The S-band radiator is proximity coupled to two orthogonal microstrip feedlines. The C-band array is an aperture coupled to other two mutually orthogonal microstrip feed network that generate vertical polarization (VP) and horizontal polarization (HP). The dependencies of isolation on relative slot positions and interlayer spacing have been investigated. The antenna yields an impedance bandwidth of wider than 3.65% at the S-band with isolation better than 26 dB. At C-band ports, it exhibits wider than 21.9% impedance bandwidth and isolation higher than 45 dB over the realized band. Design details, findings of the parametric investigation, and experimental results are presented here. Measured results are improved compared to the earlier reported works.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave single feed dual-polarized air-filled SIW slotted antenna array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a single fed dual-polarized air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (ASIW) slotted array antenna for operation in millimeter-wave frequencies is presented. A waveguide slot configuration that can radiate nearly equal components of horizontal and vertical polarizations is presented which is used to design a dual-polarized antenna with a single feed. An arrangement of slots is designed based on the optimization of aperture fields from a combined configuration of transverse and longitudinal slots to obtain dual-polarized radiation. The antenna comprises 8 elements of the designed slot pattern terminated with a short circuit. The spacing between the consecutive array elements and the placement of short circuit is optimized to achieve the dual-polarized radiation over good bandwidth. The antenna features input reflection better than $-10 \mathrm{~dB}$ for a bandwidth of 1.2GHz from 37.3-38.5 GHz with an efficiency over 75% in the entire bandwidth. The maximum gain realized in horizontal and vertical polarizations at 38.2GHz is 9.7dBi and 10.1dBi, respectively. The proposed antenna is fabricated and the measured results are in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of SI-Cancellation in a Co-linearly Polarised Shared-Radiator Full-Duplex Antenna for 6G
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we show an experimental demonstration of the suppression of self-interference (SI) using the antenna domain SI-Cancellation (SIC) method in a co-linearly polarised shared-radiator-based full-duplex antenna system. Here, we initially show the signal impairment in the received QPSK constellation due to the presence of SI signal using a conventional microstrip full-duplex antenna system without SIC. Further, the improvement in the received QPSK signal quality is exhibited using a shared-radiator full-duplex (SR-FD) antenna with reduced SI using antenna domain cancellation. A low-cost in-house experimental set-up is prepared using Adalm-Pluto software-defined radio (SDR) and MATLAB Simulink for the experiment. The proposed FD antenna system operates at a 5.9 GHz operating frequency, suitable for V2X-ITS application.

articleTitle: Beamforming in Micro-strip Phased Array Antenna through Optimal Phase Angle Rounding-Off Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The performance and efficacy of a Phased Array Antenna System (PAAS) can be largely enhanced by efficient beamforming techniques. The PAAS typically uses Digital Phase Shifter (DPS) to attain directional beamforming. The beam quantization effects, resulted due to the use of DPS, can be minimized by the use of innovative beamforming methods. Phase Angle Rounding-Off (PARO) techniques achieve near-continuous beamforming, even when using lower-bit DPS elements. Micro-strip or patch antenna are being widely used not only in commercial applications like mobile phones or medical equipment, but also in defence application like target sensors or telemetry systems. In this paper, we use Optimal-PARO (O-PARO) method of beamforming for a micro-strip array antenna, designed in C-band, for airborne communication receiver application. The use of O-PARO results in significantly reducing the scan steps of the array antenna, with high fidelity of beam pointing. Conversely, low-bit DPS can be used in the PAAS, when employing the O-PARO method, to achieve performance equivalent to larger-bit DPS, which has been demonstrated in this paper via simulations.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Coexistence of Classical and Quantum Communication in Quantum Key Distribution Link
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a quantum key distribution (QKD) system that combines classical and quantum signals in a single optical channel for quantum key distribution application. We carefully optimize the communication link by placing the bright classical channel wavelength longer than the weak quantum one, number and specification of wavelength division multiplexers, and maximizing on-off extinction in the intensity modulator to minimize crosstalk of bright classical photons onto the quantum channel. Our experiments demonstrate a secret key rate (SKR) of 4.39 kbps for an emulated channel length of 65.5 km with less than 3% quantum bit error rate (QBER). The experimental study discussed here is relevant for utilization of existing optical fiber networks for QKD, making the system more robust for practical usage.

articleTitle: Microfluidic HMSIW based Self-Diplexing Antenna for Simultaneous Sensing of Liquid Samples
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A microfluidic sensor based on a half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) is presented in this paper. For the first time, the simultaneous sensing is proposed utilizing the self-diplexing characteristics of the SIW antenna. Diplexing is achieved by loading a modified T-shaped slot on the top metallic plane of the SIW. The antenna resonates at 4.66 GHz and 4.81 GHz, with a minimum port isolation of $\gt30 {\mathrm {dB}}$. Two microfluidic pockets made up of PDMS are introduced on the diplexer antenna where the electric fields are maximum. For demonstration of simultaneous sensing, one of the fluidic pockets is filled with distilled water, and other is filled with ethanol. The interaction between the liquid materials and the electromagnetic fields provide the shift in the resonant frequency of the diplexer antenna. The self-dipleixng microfluidic sensor achieved a high sensitivity of 57.45 MHz/RIU and 89.76 MHz/RIU for distilled water and ethanol, respectively.

articleTitle: Cross-correlated Tensor Surface Impedance Characterization of Orthogonally Discrete IMU & CMU for Impedance Modulated Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a detailed characterization of Tensor Surface Impedance Matrix (TSIM) for orthogonally discrete inductive and capacitive meta unit-cell has been performed. Four orthogonally distributed digitally coded (i.e ${\bf 0 0},{\bf 0 1},{\bf 1 0},11)$ states have been assigned for both orthogonally discretized inductive and capacitive meta unit-cell. Tensor Surface Impedance Matrix (TSIM) is implemented for each unit cell to characterize the isotropic, non-homogeneous nature of $\overline{\overline{Z_{\text{surf}}}}$. From dispersion relation, the variation of phase velocity has been characterized for both Inductive Meta unit-cell (IMU) as well as Capacitive Meta unit-cell (CMU). Further, Cross Correlation between similar coded IMU and CMU has been performed to extract the linear dependency of those complementary structures. Also, the Cross correlation between the proposed orthogonally discrete unit-cells have been performed to extract the equivalent impedance coupling factor $(\ddot{}{Z}_{c})$. Effective $\overline{\overline{Z_{\text{surf}}}}$ vs direction of surface wave propagation $(\theta_{k})$ is characterized for each orthogonally discrete unit cell for both proposed IMU and CMU.

articleTitle: Compact Water-based Microstrip Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Implementation of Microstrip circuits at low radio frequencies presents challenges due to the longer wavelengths, resulting in increased form factor. This can be solved by using a higher dielectric constant substrate. In this paper, we propose a novel approach of implementing microstrip circuits on a composite multilayer substrate based on water having a higher effective dielectric constant $(\epsilon_{\mathrm{e}ff}=26)$. We demonstrate the practical implementation of microstrip circuits on a composite multilayer substrate, by designing a 5th order Stepped Impedance Low Pass Filter with cut-off frequency at 350 MHz. The overall reduction in size of the filter designed on composite substrate is demonstrated by comparing it with a filter designed on a single layer dielectric medium (FR-4). Filters simulated on both the substrates have been optimized for identical electrical specifications, and prototypes have been built and measured to validate the design concept. Measurement and simulation results indicate that filter designed on the composite substrate is 2.5 times smaller in length than the filter designed on a single layer substrate. We propose to use this concept for designing compact microstrip circuits at low frequencies.

articleTitle: A W-Band Power Efficient Frequency Doubler
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A frequency doubler is reported in a hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuit (MIC) configuration using a Schottky diode based design at the W-band. Unwanted harmonic reuse scheme has been adopted for optimal use of the nonlinearity of the multiplying semiconductor device. Commercially available low cost device has been used in this simple balanced design and required results have been achieved. A comparison with prior art works indicates competitive performance. Output power is enhanced by reflecting the unwanted harmonics from the output side back towards the diode again, which mixes with the input fundamental frequency to effectively enhance the output power at the desired harmonic frequency. Thus, improvement in conversion loss is accomplished. A special technique using microstrip stubs has been adopted to provide proper RF grounding to the Schottky varactor diodes at the desired frequency. Measured result shows a minimum conversion loss of 19.8 dB over 89 to 99 GHz with 15 dBm of input power. Spurious rejection is in excess of 50 dBc. Measured output spectrum is highly stable with elevated spectral purity. Therefore, the proposed frequency multiplier is useful for Wband transceivers for wireless communication, imaging and other potential applications.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Circular Polarized Transmitter and Receiver Antennas for Mitigation of Mutual Coupling in Monostatic Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Through-wall radar systems require compact, wideband and high gain antennas for detecting targets. Building walls introduce considerable attenuation on the radar signals. When the transmitted power is raised to compensate the through-wall attenuation, the direct coupling between the transmitter and receiver can saturate the receiver because of which weaker reflections off the target may remain undetected. In this paper, we propose using transmitter and receiver antennas of orthogonal circular polarization to reduce the direct coupling between the transmitter and receiver while retaining the first bounce off the target. In our paper, we demonstrate that the quadrafilar helical antenna (QHA) is a good candidate for this operation since it is characterized by a small size, wide frequency band of operation, high gain and low axial ratio over a wide field of view. We compare the reduced mutual coupling between the transmitter and receiver elements for the oppositely polarized QHA antennas with other commonly used through-wall radar antennas such as the Vivaldi and horn antennas. The system is tested in through-wall conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Metasurface-based Hexagonal shaped CPW feed Antenna for X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a novel Co-Planar Waveguide (CPW) fed hexagonal antenna loaded with metasurface located at a distance of 2.5 mm above the radiator is designed to cover the entire X-band spectrum. The metasurface is made up of two complementary frequency selective surfaces (FSS), in which the top one is constructed using a hexagonal patch with slots and the bottom side is constructed using an asterisk-shaped patch. These FSS possess a positive reflection gradient within the operating frequency of 8 GHz -12.4 GHz and less reflection magnitude which helps to enhance the relative impedance bandwidth of the antenna. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of about 4.4 GHz from 8 GHz to 12.4 GHz with an average gain of 11.11 dBi. The overall electrical dimension of the presented radiating system is 1.92$\lambda_{g}\times 1.75 \lambda_{g}\times 0.05 \lambda_{g}.$ The proposed configuration is suitable for X-band applications such as radar target scanning and weather monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Nested Circular Ring Based FSS-Composite for Low Observable Aerospace Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the electromagnetic design, simulation, and experimental studies of Circular ring-based customized absorber working for broadband frequency 8-21 GHz. The proposed design consists of continuous and split arms-based circular rings associated with four circular arm cut geometry. The proposed absorber has been designed using customized glass fabric reinforced plastics (GFRP) having thickness of 0.2 mm, which is separated to a metallic ground plane (CFRP) by a Roha Cell foam spacer of 2mm. Proposed composite has been designed using customized developed 200 ohms resistive materials, design has been simulated using a full-wave electromagnetic simulator under periodic boundary conditions. The simulation result shows minimum 10 dB reflection loss value (90% absorption) in 8-21 GHz, which covers X, Ku, and some portion of K bands having a full-width absorption bandwidth of 13 GHz with 93% fractional bandwidth (FBW). Further, the proposed absorber design has been fabricated and validated experimentally with the simulated results. The proposed absorber is thinner in nature, polarization insensitive, possesses good angular stability, and features of fabricability using customized substrate. These attributes encompass it for potential usages in aerospace platforms.

articleTitle: A Comparitive Analysis of Statistically Distributed Single and Dual Beam Series Fed MPA Array with Highly Reduced HPBW & SLL For mm-Wave RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a statistically distributed $1 \times 8$ series fed patch antenna array (SFPAA) is proposed to achieve both single and dual-beam characteristics with highly reduced side lobe level (SLL) and half power beam width (HPBW) for energy harvesting applications. The proposed series fed patch antenna array is operating at mm-wave frequency (i.e 22 GHz-24 GHz) with a high directive gain $(\approx 15.5 \mathrm{~dB})$ with highly reduced SLL (upto 21.5dB) and narrow HPBW $\left(\approx 12.1^{\circ}\right)$. Patch widths of the SFPAA are distributed through uniform, normal, and expo-gaussian distribution to realize the antenna performance based on skewness controlling parameter $\alpha$. $S_{11}$, 2D and 3D patterns are mentioned for each distribution to make a complete study on SLL and HPBW on the basis of statistically distributed patch widths. For energy harvesting application, a schottky diode (MACOM Ma4E1317) enabled 24 GHz RF rectifier is designed to perform the RF and DC power conversion. An output voltage of 3V with 42% efficiency has been achieved.

articleTitle: A Novel Tumour Characterization in Microwave Imaging Using Pattern-Based Weighted DMAS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The usage of microwave imaging for biomedical (BMWI) applications is still challenging due to the imprecise reconstruction of the relative permittivity ($\varepsilon_{\text{r}}$) of tissues and the ill-posed inverse scattering problem. Here, a novel two-step approach is proposed for tumour characterization in the BMWI framework. The focus is distinguishing normal and tumourous tissues using a non-iterative approach. An intensity map of the target region is generated to detect the tumour. Then the area around the tumour is further processed to obtain the refined image in terms of the effective $\varepsilon_{\text{r}}$. As the tumour is embedded in tissues of higher dielectric constant, the image thus formed will usually be larger in size than the actual tumour. Thus, to estimate the accurate size, we propose a novel antenna pattern-based weighted delay, multiply, and sum algorithm along with principal component analysis as a synthetic focusing technique. Subsequently, the effective dielectric profile of the embedding medium is approximately estimated, which is close to their actual values.

articleTitle: Proposing a Simple Microwave Power Transfer System Using a Metallic Waveguide Lens and a Novel Magnetron Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wireless power transmission system is developed, which is capable of transmitting power as high as 700W, using microwave radiation at a frequency of 2.45 GHz. The system includes a conventional horn antenna transmitter and receiver and a metallic plate lens. The lens enables the antennas to be operated in their far field region without incurring a loss in power, thus increasing the operating distance of the system. The lens works by shaping the incident wave front to converge at a single point after passing through it. It is designed and simulated on CST Studio Suite and then fabricated, using sheet aluminium, making it lightweight and reducing its cost. A novel method to control the output power of the common cavity magnetron is also developed and tested. Using off the shelf cavity magnetron for microwave generation reduces the complexity and the cost of the system. The salient features of this system include extreme cost reduction, high power rating and portability. The transmission distance is kept 3m for testing purposes, but can be readily scaled up.

articleTitle: Single Feed Based Wide Band Circularly Polarized Radiating Element For S-band SATCOM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper discusses design, simulation, development and evaluation of right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) microstrip antenna with wide axial ratio bandwidth using single coaxial feed for SATCOM applications. The antenna consists of a lower and upper rectangular patch separated by 10 mm air gap in stacked configuration, fabricated on 62 mil RT Duroid 5880 dielectric material. Length and width of the patch as well as a cross structure, orthogonally placed two slots, in lower patch have been optimized to obtain wideband circular polarization. Stacked configuration of microstrip antenna with optimized air gap has been utilized for wide impedance bandwidth. Measured antenna has gain of 8.58 dBic and beamwidth more than 60 degrees at 2.69 GHz. The antenna shows wide impedance bandwidth of about 20 percent and wide axial ratio bandwidth greater than 8 percent. The experimental results of the antenna are quite close to the simulated one in terms of axial ratio bandwidth and impedance bandwidth. The novelty of this microstrip antenna is wide 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth, between 2.54 GHz to 2.77 GHz, using single coaxial feed for SATCOM applications.

articleTitle: Non-planar Frequency Selective Surface based Bandstop Filter for Electromagnetic Shielding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective surface (FSS) based bandstop filter design that has been implemented on different non-planar surfaces for electromagnetic (EM) shielding applications. The unit cell of the FSS features a metallic annular ring geometry printed on a polylactic acid (PLA) dielectric material periodically. The structure has initially been studied on a planar surface and a bandstop response is observed ranging from 8.56 to 11.4 GHz, with the resonance occurring at 10 GHz. The FSS unit cell has then been wrapped on two distinct non-planar surfaces (frustum and hemisphere) and their shielding characteristics are individually studied using the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM). The responses observed for both non-planar surfaces show similar behaviors as that of the planar surface, thereby validating the proposed conformal FSS structure.

articleTitle: Design of Koch Fractal Antenna with Defected Ground Structure for S-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The proposed article presents a wideband characterized antenna with fractal geometry. To improve the impedance bandwidth a second-order iterated Koch fractal curve is incorporated on the lower and upper edges of the main radiator. The operating frequency of the antenna spans from 1.9GHz to 4.3GHz. The impedance bandwidth of $ 77\%$ is achieved due to the implementation of the defected ground structure. The overall geometry configuration is built on a FR4 substrate. The monopole is powered on a line feed attached to the fractal patch with a matched impedance of $ 50\Omega$. The dimensional compactness of the proposed fractal antenna measures $0.641\lambda_{0}\times 0.434\lambda_{0}\times 0.016\lambda_{0}(f_{r}=$ 3.1 GHz). A maximum realized gain measures to 4dBi at 4.22 GHz with better X-Pol level and stable radiation characteristics covering the entire operational band adds to the merits of this investigation. Thus, the proposed monopole can be considered suitable for application in the S-band.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Ultra-Compact Cross Slot Loaded CPW-Fed Antenna for Satellite Communication in Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of communication technology, the demand for efficient and compact antenna designs continues to rise. This research paper presents a novel circularly polarized ultra-compact CPW-fed circular slot antenna tailored for satellite communication applications in the Ka band. The proposed antenna exhibits an impressive impedance bandwidth spanning from 28 - 38 GHz (30.30%) and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 29.90-37.75 GHz (23.19%), making it a promising candidate for high-frequency communication needs. This work showcases a comprehensive design approach, incorporating a step-stepped fed line, a modified circular patch, cross-shaped slots, and a circular slot ground plane to achieve exceptional performance metrics. The designed antenna has radiation efficiency of 89% and peak gain of 5dBi with single element and can find its usage in close range military radar targeting applications.

articleTitle: An Inexpensive Drone and RF Emitter Tracking System Using Monopulse Comparator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radio direction finding (RDF) system finds many applications from commercial to strategic. In this paper, monopulse comparator (MPC) based inexpensive RDF system is presented which can be used for drone and RF emitter tracking. Though MPCs themselves have been realized in various technologies like microstrip, rect-ax and waveguide, however much less research is reported on developing a complete system. This paper presents the complete tracking system from RF front end to baseband processing. For the proof of the proposed concept, a MPC based RDF is designed and developed at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Precise Altitude Estimation in FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Navigation sensors are indispensable for spacecraft as they provide vital data used by the NGC (Navigation Guidance Control) system to guide the spacecraft towards the intended landing site. Among these sensors, the radar altimeter is widely used for altitude information during the landing phase. Nevertheless, accurately determining altitude over different terrains poses a challenge. To overcome this, paper proposes a methodology that utilizes moving average filtering in the frequency domain to reduce noise and enhance the precision of altitude estimation. The proposed algorithm has been implemented over a linear FMCW coherent radar system [1] and has been validated through experiments conducted on helicopter platform, covering a wide altitude range.

articleTitle: Design of a Rugged Radiating Panel Assembly with High Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Reliability is one of the key aspects in any kind of radar design and any failure of the system or sub-system can be critical. This problem particularly becomes severe for huge aperture radars where even a failure at Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) level may cause a system failure. An important radar system considered in this paper is a radiating panel assembly. It is an active aperture array of thousands of radiating elements interfaced with Dual Transmit Receive (TR) modules. The TR modules are governed by a hierarchical Beam steering network which generates the control signals and also provides the steering direction. There are power supply modules which are meant for sourcing the power to each individual LRUs. Therefore, the radiating panel assembly may be conceptualized to be an interconnection of system of systems. A rugged design should cater for prevention of failure of this multi-disciplinary system involving RF, digital controls and Power. In this paper we highlight the design philosophy for prevention of system failure and highlight all the mechanisms incorporated for the same. The approach is modular and scalable and can be adapted for any hybrid system with huge physical apertures.

articleTitle: A Novel Interference-Based Approach for Harmonic Suppression in Microwave Frequency Doublers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel doubler module designed for frequency doubler applications. The module is designed in Keysight ADS software and fabricated on FR4 substrate (with dielectric constant, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=4.6$) to achieve the harmonic suppression of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> & $3 \mathrm{f}_{0}$ at 2.29 GHz and 6.87 GHz, respectively, while effectively extracting $2 \mathrm{f}_{0}$ at 4.58 GHz by a special means of constructive and destructive interference of the signal. The mathematical analysis demonstrates an impressive (more than 60 dB) suppression of the fundamental and third harmonics. The proposed structure is subjected to simulation, fabrication, and measurement along with a typical harmonic generator to validate its concept. BFP840ESD transistor is used to design the non-linear module(harmonic generator), and the doubler module is integrated along with the non-linear harmonic generator to assess its performance.

articleTitle: A 124-202 GHz Compact Wideband Sub-THz On-Chip Monopole Antenna Using Split Ring Resonators in 65 nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed wideband sub-THz on-chip monopole antenna is designed using a commercial 65 nm CMOS process. Initially, a standalone monopole antenna is designed at a center frequency of 150 GHz. The impedance bandwidth of the standalone monopole antenna is 48 GHz. Two square split-ring resonators (SRRs) are introduced to improve the impedance bandwidth. The SRRs are magnetically coupled to the monopole and are used as the radiating elements. A 30 GHz impedance bandwidth improvement is made using the proposed method compared to a standalone monopole antenna. The simulated impedance bandwidth of the proposed on-chip antenna is 78 GHz, which covers frequencies between 124-202 GHz. To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first time SRRs have been used in the on-chip antenna environment for bandwidth enhancement.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency, Broadband Doherty Power Amplifier for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) for 5G applications. The proposed DPA uses high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) Gallium nitride (GaN) based packaged device as an active nonlinear device. DPA uses active load modulation to get high efficiency at back-off power operation. With the simulation results it is observed that the proposed DPA can achieve the highest efficiency of 75.3% at saturation and around 64.3% at 6 dB output back off (OBO) at the center frequency of 3.5 GHz. The achieved bandwidth (BW) is 3.1-3.8 GHz with a gain of more than 8 dB and output power (Pout) of 41.4-44.6 dBm. The proposed DPA can accomplish a wide band characteristic with high efficiency and output power.

articleTitle: Exploring Class B/J Continuum for Doherty Power Amplifier Design at n78 5G Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a simplified high peak power Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) for n78 5G applications. This study implements Foster Loads at the Extrinsic Reference Plane (ERP) at both main and auxiliary PAs for better output power and efficiency. Here, the main PA is operated in a continuous class B/J mode at output power back-off (OPBO) and in saturation at the current reference plane (CRP) for better efficiency over the band. At the output side, using Foster load with less dispersive reactive part removes additional matching network’s requirement since the load-combiner performs the matching condition required for the efficient DPA operation. The proposed DPA results in high peak power of 53.5-55.1dBm with 57-66% Drain efficiency (DE) over 3.3-3.8 GHz (and 45-49.4% DE at 48. 5dBm of output power). For a 5 MHz spacing two-tone signal, better than -22.5dBcC/IMD3 at 6dB OPBO is observed for the proposed DPA design, demonstrating better device linearity.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Mitigation in SATCOM Ku-Band Channel Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The work demonstrates practical implementations to improve radiation susceptibility of highly miniaturized, high gain Ku Band Channel Amplifiers (CAMPs). In a Ku Band satellite communication payload, CAMPs operate at −54dBm input power and provide a high 60dB gain to drive Travelling Wave Tube Amplifiers. EMI mitigation implementations have resulted in radiated emission levels at the output of CAMP <−60dBc with respect to the main signal. The performance corresponds to 89dB shielding effectiveness of the unit, which is very close to what is practically possible with RF and DC interfaces used. These implementations have contributed in achieving excellent transponder gain flatness.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave stripline fed dielectric resonator antenna with assembly features
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An approach to engineering of a high-gain spherical dielectric resonator antenna operating at around 35 GHz is discussed in this work. A stripline-based aperture-coupled feeding technique using stacked multi-layered printed circuit boards architecture has been demonstrated. Precise alignment of the spherical radiating element with respect to the feedline is ensured by an air-filled via in a supportive layer. For system assembly and packaging, a metal shielding layer is applied around the radiating structure. The final circuit design, including its packaging module, is tested to quantify its input impedance matching, radiation pattern, and efficiency. Necessary conclusions are drawn, and the shortcomings are addressed.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an Ultra-Wideband Equal Magnitude and Out-Of-Phase Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design and analysis of an ultra-wideband out-of-phase power divider. The input to the power divider is in a microstrip line which divides the power equally to two sections of a slotline designed on the ground plane of the microstrip feedline. Next, the slotline sections make a transition to microstrip lines which generate an out-of-phase response. The use of shorting vias in the microstrip line and circular shorting stub in the slotline boasts the wideband lowloss response of the circuit design. The equivalent lumped circuit model of the proposed design is presented along with a parametric study of the input matching and fractional bandwidth. The optimized circuit design has an amplitude and phase imbalance of $0.25 \mathrm{~dB}$ and 2.5 degree, respectively over a fractional bandwidth of $164 \%$.

articleTitle: Surface Reflectivity Measurements of Sub-Millimeter Wave Reflector Antenna Using a Quasi-Optical Test Bench
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: It is essential to characterize the surface of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter wave reflector antennas for their electrical properties. The characterization of these electrical properties is critical at these frequencies, as it is necessary for predicting the overall performance of the antenna system. This paper presents a measurement of the electrical reflectivity at 220 GHz. To carry out the reflectivity measurement, a high precision Quasi-Optical free space test bench was employed. This test bench effectively measured the reflectivity of the sample, which represents the surface of the reflector antenna. The setup of the test bench comprised of transmit and receive Gaussian horns, beam-waist guiding mirrors, planar sample holder, and a Vector Network Analyzer. This test bench is operating over the 50 - 220 GHz frequency range. This free-space measurement system facilitated the determination of the reflection (S11) and transmission (S21) coefficients of the planar samples. The reflectivity values were then derived from the measured S11 and S21 coefficients. The study successfully characterized the sample, and the measured results were found to be satisfactory.

articleTitle: Reduction of RCS of a Series Fed Linear Array Antenna using Artificial Magnetic Conductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A series-fed linear array antenna incorporated with artificial magnetic conductors (AMC) for wideband radar cross-section (RCS) reduction is presented in this paper. A five-element microstrip patch antenna array with a series-fed network at X-band has been designed. AMC blocks have been added on two sides of the array in order to reduce RCS over a wideband. The structure provides a wide impedance bandwidth of more than 15% and a gain bandwidth of 10%. A significant RCS reduction band of 90% is observed under normal incidence in both X and Y-polarizations when compared with an antenna array without AMC blocks and a same-sized metal plate. The structure has been fabricated and measured, in which the measurement results show a good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of CP Horn with Integrated Mono-groove Polarizer for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a circularly polarized dual-mode horn antenna that incorporates a mono-groove polarizer. The primary objective of the proposed antenna design is to achieve excellent circular polarization characteristics while simplifying the overall design compared to traditional solutions. By utilizing a single groove on the inner wall of the circular waveguide, the polarizer generates circularly polarized electromagnetic waves and reduces the complexity of the antenna system. To validate the performance of the proposed horn antenna, it was fabricated and evaluated. The measurement results align well with the simulation results, with a measured axial ratio (AR) of $\lt1.2$ dB and a $\vert \mathrm{S}11 \vert \lt -20$ dB achieved within the frequency range of 5.3-5.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Planar RFID Tag Antenna Based on Combined Matching Techniques at 902 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a planar UHF RFID tag antenna is presented which is designed by amalgamation of three impedance matching approaches: Nested slot, T-match and Meandered Inductive Loop (MIL) network. The tag antenna has volume of $76 \mathrm{~mm} \times 30 \mathrm{~mm} \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}(0.228 \lambda \times 0.0902 \lambda \times 0.0048 \lambda)$. The planar structure of tendered antenna can reduce mass production cost of tags. Moreover, the slot based T-matching and MIL network rotation can be tuned in large scale for impedance matching. The presented tag antenna extends its read range upto 14.1m.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide fed Stacked DRA for 5G NR FR2 Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) and Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRA) are designed to work at millimeter wave frequencies. In this study, integrating both these technologies, an antenna with high radiation efficiency and wide bandwidth is proposed. A hemispherical DRA is placed on top of a notched rectangular DRA to achieve a wide bandwidth. A central air gap is introduced in the rectangular DRA to generate a wider impedance bandwidth. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna can operate for dual-band frequency. The bandwidth of these bands are found to be 2.4 GHz (23.17-25.57 GHz) and 5.63 GHz (27.85-33.48GHz). This antenna is circularly polarized and shows peak total gain of 8.51dBiC. The co-polarization and cross-polarization differences are above 15dB for the E-plane and H-plane. The radiation efficiency is above 97% for an entire band of the operating frequency range. The proposed antenna shows promising results for 5G bands. It is suitable for 5G New Radio (NR) Frequency Range 2 (FR2) n258 and n261 bands.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of High Temperature Black Body source in Microwave-Millimeter wave Spectrum for radiometric calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Electron Cyclotron Emission (ECE) radiometer diagnostics are broadband receivers that are widely used as standard microwave diagnostics for measurement of localized thermal plasma temperature profiles. Calibration of these diagnostics is usually done using high temperature sources that possess blackbody like properties. A silicon carbide based high temperature blackbody source is used to calibrate the E-band (60-90 GHz) radiometers at Institute for Plasma Research (IPR). To understand the characteristics of the designed silicon carbide calibration source in the microwave range, Sparameters are determined using ABmm wave VNA. This manuscript discusses the results obtained from the characterization over a wide frequency range starting from Kaband (26-40GHz) to D-band (140-160GHz) satisfying the varied frequency requirements from the tokamak experimentation end. Linearity test of the designed source is obtained using existing multi-channel radiometer that lies within acceptable limits while the temperature distribution characteristics are observed using an Infrared (IR) Camera. Experimental characterizations of black body source exhibit high absorption capabilities of $\gt60$ dB in $\gt50$ GHz frequency range with a reflection coefficient of $\leq$20dB.

articleTitle: Fractal Shaped Multi-Layer Unit Cell Design With Tunable Polarization Conversion Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A fractal shaped multi-layer unit cell design is proposed in this article to conceive tunable polarization conversion performance over the X-band frequencies for practical use. The multi-layer Minkowski-shaped unit cell structure is designed with a varactor diode element incorporated in it, whose capacitance values can be changed to obtain tunable polarization conversion performance in real-time operation. The structure offers 95% to 99% polarization conversion efficiency over the band of interest and can be tuned over a range of frequency values with a stable and finite granularity feature, justifying its utility for real-time applications. It also retains its polarization conversion performance along with the tunability characteristics over an angular region of 20 degree, when the structure is tilted to 10 degrees on both sides of normal incidence, highlighting its stability of performance for oblique incidence conditions. Detailed simulation results are presented to describe the process of choosing the optimal position of the via components and their diameter values, which quantitatively determine and maintain the conversion characteristics.

articleTitle: Rapid scanning polarizing Martin Puplett type THz Fourier transform spectrometer (FTS) for ITER ECE measurements
