publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: this paper gives a brief overview of the ITER Electron Cyclotron Emission Diagnostic system, outlining the design requirements for Fast scanning Fourier transform Spectrometer. The prototype Martin Puplett Interferometer and its associated data acquisition system are presented. The importance of interferometer characterization and calibration procedures is briefly discussed. Moreover, conventional data analysis techniques are discussed and implemented on the experimentally obtained interferogram from the prototype Martin Puplett interferometer.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Full-Duplex Compact Antenna for Vehicular Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The continuous increase in demand for high-speed wireless communication in vehicles has led to the need for efficient, compact, and reliable antenna systems that simultaneously operate in multiple frequency bands. This paper presents the design and analysis of a compact dual-band full duplex (DBFD) antenna with a hexagon patch and cross-coupling topology for vehicular applications. It is evident from the analysis that the proposed design works at its fundamental mode (TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>) for the desired frequency band. The presented antenna is designed to achieve full duplex operation, i.e., enabling simultaneous transmission and reception of information in two different frequency bands (3.7-3.96 GHz and 5.5-5.94 GHz), respectively. The gain of the simulated design in the lower and upper bands is around 5.2 and 8 dB, respectively. This antenna exhibits desirable characteristics, such as stable radiation patterns, third-order filtering response, and better isolation across the desired frequency bands. The proposed antenna presents a compact size, wideband performance, and feasibility to work in vehicular environments.

articleTitle: K-Band GaN Based Solid State Power Amplifier for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper details the design and realization of State-of-the-art, K-Band Solid State Power Amplifier (SSPA) for Space Applications. This Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) based SSPA is developed indigenously utilizing in-house designed GaAs and GaN amplifier MMICs in driver and high power stages. The SSPA delivers >5W Continuous Wave (CW) output power at 4dB gain compression with large signal gain better than 64dB at the center frequency of 26.07GHz over a bandwidth of 100MHz. The design verification model (DVM) is developed and tested successfully over a temperature range of −5°C to +60°C meeting all the required specifications. The overall high gain of SSPA is split in two separate mechanical housings namely Driver Amplifier (DA) package and High Power Amplifier (HPA) package, which are interconnected using a small co-axial cable. Separate Electronic Power Conditioner (EPC) package provides regulated DC power required by the SSPA. Design challenges pertaining to high frequency-high power design and thermal management aspects for space environments are also discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Dual-band Patch Antenna Design with Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of a dual-band dual-mode slotted circular patch antenna design has been proposed. The differential and common mode feeding of the slotted patch are utilized to excite the two modes having broad-side and omni-directional radiation characteristics. A Wilkinson Power Divider is used to feed the slotted patch antenna for 180 and 0 degrees phase shift at the lower and upper-band respectively. The proposed antenna operates in two frequency bands centered at 3.31 GHz (Impedance Bandwidth=4.80%, Broadside pattern) and 5.86 GHz (Impedance Bandwidth=6.87%, Omni-directional pattern). The electrical size of slotted patch along with the feed network is $0.73 \lambda \times 0.55 \lambda \times 0.44 \lambda$ ($\lambda$ corresponds to 3.3 GHz). The array of four slotted patches are further arranged in a $2 \times 2$ configuration to arrive at the design of pattern and spatial diversity multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system. The ports of the MIMO system have isolation level better than −20 dB, while the far-fields show an envelope correlation coefficients (ECCs) lower than −22 dB in both the operating bands of antenna. The performance characteristics of the single and $2 \times 2$ antenna elements have been validated by measurement carried out on their fabricated prototypes.

articleTitle: Textile Based Absorber For C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel concept for a Frequency Selective Surface(FSS) embedded within textile fabric. The structure of the metamaterial involves three distinct layers: a copper pattern on the upper surface, a textile layer in the middle, and a grounding plane at the bottom. The primary objective behind designing this absorber is to effectively conceal an object from electromagnetic motion detectors and radar systems. An important anticipated characteristic of this design is its inherent flexibility. The desired central frequency of operation is set at 7.4 GHz. Utilizing a series of simulations carried out using CST software, the absorber demonstrates an impressive absorption capability, achieving more than 95% absorptivity. Moreover, the absorber maintains its absorption efficiency over a wide operating angle, extending to at least 90° degrees. Notably, the suggested design demonstrates significant absorption regardless of the electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Design & Development of LTCC Multi-layer Low-pass filter at 2.25GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of miniaturized low-pass filter embedded in low-temperature co-fired ceramic substrate is presented in this paper. A low-pass filter with 2.25 GHz cut-off frequency and 0.25 dB insertion loss designed using LC resonator components. On-wafer measured results confirm that the insertion loss in the pass band is 0.25dB and suppression at 4.5GHz is more than 30dBc. Six layers of LTCC substrate is utilized to miniaturize the filter. VSWR of input and output port is less than 1.18. The volume of achieved filter is $6.45 \mathrm{~mm} \times 5.2 \mathrm{~mm} \times 1.09 \mathrm{~mm}$.

articleTitle: A Tri-Band Quad Feed MIMOTB Antenna with Two-Narrow in Ku-K Bands and n259/n260 5G-mmWave FR2-Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research reports the design of a tri-band (TB) four-port MIMO antenna configuration radiating EM energy. The proposed antenna consists radiating patch printed on the top plane of the top plane which consists of a circular ring embedded within the slotted-hexagonal geometry. The opposite plane is printed with the rectangular partial ground which is etched by a rectangular slot for better impedance matching. The antenna configuration generates three operating narrow-band bandwidths corresponding to 12.81GHz-13.965GHz (Ku band), 14.90GHz-19.355GHz (Ku-K band), and 37.78GHz-43.61GHz (5G-mmWave FR2 band: n259 & n260). The orthogonal arrangement ensures isolation of more than 15.0dB with diversity parameters ECCTB $\lt0.02$ & DGTB $\gt9.998$ dB. The peak gain corresponds to 3.88dBi at 13.63GHz, 4.74dBi at 16.13GHz, and 5.00dBi at 40.62GHz. The proposed MIMO antenna is easily deployable in the 5G infrastructure environment for smart city and IoT applications.

articleTitle: A kW-range Solid-State Power Amplifier Design for OTH Radar’s Transmitter Application.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a High Frequency (HF) band, kilowatt level, Continuous Wave (CW) power amplifier implemented in laterally-diffused metal oxide semiconductor (LDMOS) technology in a single board. It will be used in the transmitter section of Over The Horizon (OTH) Radar and is capable of operating in one of the possible OTH bands i.e. 22 MHz to 24 MHz. The configuration used here for design is Class-AB configuration that helped us achieve a Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of almost 66.5% at 975 W output power for a single stage. Two stages of this circuit, connected in a parallel configuration, will help us to achieve 1.95 kW of RF output, which will be one of the many unit-cells required for OTH transmitter. This novel design solves the problem of using bulky, tube-based RF signal amplifiers and also makes the system much more noise resilient, efficient and compact.

articleTitle: A Compact Unidirectional Triple Circularly Polarized Antenna for sub-6 GHz 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper represents the design of single feed, dual broadband microstrip antenna showing triple circularly polarized (CP) behavior of radiations for the multiband wireless environment. The CP is achieved based on two mechanisms: excitation of orthogonal mode using metasurface loaded diagonal feed patch antenna, and gap-coupling with slotted parasitic patches. Thus three pair of orthogonal mode operating at 3.65 GHz, 5.3 GHz and 5.8 GHz are excited. In addition, the pro-posed antenna has a maximum gain of 7.22 dB at 5.5 GHz. The dual broadband frequencies of operations and the attained CP feature makes the proposed device suitable for sub-6 GHz 5G application.

articleTitle: Analysis of power combiner architecture for push-pull transistors with on-chip and on-board coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Push-pull transistor consists of two dies on common package. It offers advantage in space, cost and process invariance between dies. However, on-chip and PCB layout RF coupling between branches of push-pull transistors becomes unavoidable. In such scenario with significant coupling, an amplitude imbalance is created. When coupling in push-pull amplifier is analyzed, it is analytically deduced that amplitude imbalance is maximized with quadrature splitter and is minimized with in-phase or out-of-phase splitter. The theoretical formulation is validated by simulation and is confirmed by measurements on practical prototype. Two amplifiers are designed using a push-pull transistor with significant on-chip and PCB layout coupling. In one of the amplifiers with quadrature hybrids, power imbalance resulted in imbalance in power dissipated in each die and created asymmetry in junction temperature of the dies resulting in reduced power delivery of amplifier. However, the amplifier with 180° splitter could maintain amplitude balance and deliver designed power of 53dBm. A power amplifier has been designed according to this design methodology and integrated into a SSPA module. The module can operate in CW mode at 200W across 2.5-2.7GHz.

articleTitle: Enhancing Micro-Strip Patch Antenna Design for HFSS using a Python package -‘AntGen’
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Modern wireless communication systems heavily rely on microstrip patch 5G antennas because of their small size, simplicity of integration, and adaptability. We introduce “AntennaGenerator (AntGen),” a feature-rich Python Package that smoothly integrates with the High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software, to simplify the process of developing and enhancing microstrip patch antennas (MSPA). With the help of AntGen, antenna engineers and researchers can quickly construct, alter, and improve MSPAs with a variety of optimizations, such as cut-outs, slots, and L slots, to name a few.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Efficiency Enhancement of a Parasitic Patch Based Wireless Power Transfer System for IMDs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, experimental verification of PTE (power transfer efficiency) enhancement is provided for a WPT (wireless power transfer) system consisting of circularly polarized (CP) transmitter and receiver antennas. The WPT system is first studied in three different realistic simulation environments. The PTE of the WPT system is enhanced by judicious use of a parasitic patch near the aperture of the implanted antenna (receiver). A low-cost experimental setup using software-defined radio (SDR), spectrum analyzer, fabricated antenna prototypes and skin-mimicking gel is implemented for the demonstration of PTE enhancement.

articleTitle: Polarization Independent Multi-band Metasurface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the present report we have proposed a multiband polarization insensitive meta-surface consisting of circular and rectangular patch on top of a dielectric medium. The simulations were carried out for finding S-parameter and polarization effects on the designed material at different polarization angles. The influence of substrate thickness on absorbing electromagnetic radiation is studied and the DUT is fabricated based on that particular dimension where the maximum absorption is achieved. The experimental studies were carried out for the fabricated structure and slight shift in the resonance frequency of the reflectance data as compare to the simulated data was observed due to the fabrication errors. All the reported absorbing peaks have the ability to absorb above $80 \%$ of its incident signal without any polarization, so it can be a useful material for radiation reduction application in stealth purpose. The electric field, magnetic field and surface current distribution pattern were also recorded for all four resonance peak which provide more information about the fabricated material.

articleTitle: Design of 2X2 EMCP Fed Microstrip Patch Array For Altimeter Payload on Space Re-Entry Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of X-band 2 $\times$ 2 EMCP fed microstrip array antenna designed to be placed on the outer body of the space re-entry vehicle (SRV) for radar altimeter application. This paper describes the modelling and analysis of array antenna with SRV body covered with Thermal protection system (TPS) layers; The reasons for poor isolations between transmit and receive antenna and methods to improve it. The antenna is designed & optimized using the 3D electromagnetic solver, taking effects of SRV body and TPS layers to achieve the desired performance with peak gain 10.4 dBi and return loss better than 20dB (8% bandwidth for 20dB). The antenna is also fabricated & measured. The fabricated antenna in stand-alone condition has a gain of 12.4 dBi, return loss better than 25dB and RF isolation between the transmit and receive antenna pair better than 70dB.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction of Slot Antenna using FSS Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the radar cross section (RCS) of the rectangular slot antenna is reduced in out-of-band frequency range using frequency selective surface (FSS) structures. FSS can act as the band stop filter at the operating frequency of the antenna. It results in RCS reduction of the antenna. The proposed antenna has a resonance frequency of 3.4 GHz. The radiation pattern is maintained for the reduced RCS antenna structure.

articleTitle: A Temperature Compensated Light Weight Coaxial Band Pass Filter for Aero-Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: One of the challenges in designing coaxial band pass filters for aero-space applications is to simultaneously minimize the temperature drift and weight. In this paper, the authors have addressed this issue in a simple yet effective manner. In a high Q coaxial cavity resonator (where tuning screw loading is not significant), the solution proposed is to employ invar for resonator post and aluminum for rest of the housing. To validate the proposed concept, a 4th order filter at C band is designed, fabricated and measured. The active temperature measurements of the filter from -55° C to 125° C reveal that the equivalent temperature coefficient of frequency variation of the filter, evaluated based on the center frequency shift, is less than 4.8 ppm/°C. The weight of the filter is less than 90 grams.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Compact, High Gain and High P1dB MMIC Based Low Noise Amplifier at V-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a I-Band MMIC based broadband low noise amplifier using a GaAs based pHEMT of 0.10 μm gate length. A 4-stage cascaded amplifier configuration has been chosen. Source inductive degeneration and feedback have been used simultaneously in order to achieve improved stability and gain flatness over the required bandwidth from 50 to 60 GHz. A flat gain of 23±1dB and a maximum noise figure of 3.2 dB have been achieved over the band within a chip size of 1.4 mm x 2.4 mm. The output 1dB compression point is also significantly high and is simulated to be 11.2 dBm. The 60-GHz band offers wide license-free bandwidth. The amplifier finds its application in point-to-point links for telecommunications back hauls, Wireless Personal Area Networks (WPAN) and Wireless HDMI.

articleTitle: Design and development of C-Ku wideband MMIC power amplifier using 250nm GaN HEMT process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband MMIC power amplifier design for C-Ku band AESA radar to be used for the purpose of jamming. The MMIC PA has been designed for the frequency range of 5 GHz to 18 GHz and has been fabricated with using 250 nm Gallium Nitride on SiC process of UMS, France. The fabricated power amplifier chip has an output power of $39.2 \pm 0.7$ dBm with small signal gain of $19 \pm 1.5$ dB and power added efficiency of 15%-25%.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Based Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Recent advances in development of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based antenna arrays prompted this research to study the effect of mounted antenna array’s radiation pattern in pitch, yaw, and roll movement for UAVs like drones (quadcopter herein) for phased array applications. This paper brings out the various array design constraints and the effect of the 3D position of array elements plus swarm of quadcopter system forming an airborne antenna array. The sensitivity of array’s interelement spacing for making the desired formation of quadcopter cluster to produce desired radiation pattern performance over the hemisphere is analyzed. A qualitative assessment of airborne antenna array is presented using a commercial method of moment-based electromagnetics solver, Altair Feko.

articleTitle: An Elliptical Shaped Wideband MIMO Terminal Antenna with Improved Isolation and Radiation Efficiency for 5G mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A quad-port wideband, multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system is discussed here for millimeter wave applications. The proposed antenna consists of a microstrip line, an elliptical shaped patch, a thin rectangular line, and a radial stub. The intended unit antenna is electrically large size of $1.93 \lambda_{0}$ $\times 2.07 \lambda_{0} \times 0.07 \lambda_{0}$ at 28GHz. The modified radiating structure fed by a microstrip line with a partially ground plane is used here as a single radiating element. The proposed wideband antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of (24 - 32 GHz) 28.57%, radiation efficiency > 95% and good radiation characteristics. Due to the orthogonal arrangement of the radiating elements, the MIMO antenna has been transformed, which offers high isolation (>25 dB) and better polarization diversity performance. Both the diversity gain (DG) and the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) are examined and determined to be within acceptable parameters.

articleTitle: Inductorless Analog Time-Delays for Nonlinear RF Signal Processing Circuits in 180nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Extremely low latency and low power consumption is crucial for emerging spectrum sensing, electronic warfare, and wireless communications applications such as phased-array beamforming for wideband signals, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) at high RF bandwidths for AI/ML inference on RF waveforms, and tunable multi-band microwave filters. Analog computers implemented in high performance integrated circuit (IC) platforms based on CMOS radio-frequency (RF) IC technologies have significant potential for such edge computing applications. The fast and low-latency response of analog RFICs ensures that tight performance specifications in terms of both latency and power consumption can be met without compromising on computational throughput. The analog computing approach also allows sensors to directly communicate with edge processors and produce intelligent action outputs at low latency without the power overhead of digitization incurred by conventional edge computing systems. Many of the necessary analog computations require a true time delay (TDD) analog memory as a fundamental building block. This paper discusses recent work on realizing analog memory using TTD elements for radar, communications, and AI/ML applications. The circuits were designed in TSMC 180nm CMOS technology and simulated at the transistor level using Cadence Spectre.

articleTitle: High Gain Holographic Antenna Using Microstrip Aperture Feed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a high-gain holographic antenna using microstrip aperture feed for beam scanning applications. Two holographic surfaces are designed and excited to get the radiation pattern at two different angles, 0 degrees and 20 degrees, with a high-gain of 20. 5dBi and side lobe level (SLL) of 15. 5dB. Both holographic surfaces with aperture antennas effectively work from 15GHz to 20GHz, which is wideband. The proposed antenna could be helpful for satellite and modern wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Omni Directional Antenna System For Onboard Telemetry Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed study on a linearly polarized microstrip antenna that is miniaturized and conformal in design. The antenna is intended for use in the S band frequency range and is specifically designed for onboard telemetry systems in small aerospace vehicles. The study includes the design of the antenna as well as placement analyses on a cylindrical body, in single as well as two element configurations. The effects of mounting the antenna on a cylindrical body and the corresponding effects of mutual coupling that show up in the resultant radiation characteristics are thoroughly examined and reported. Further, the study highlights that an antenna configuration where the elements are placed diametrically opposite to each other provides an omni-directional coverage in the roll plane of the cylinder.

articleTitle: A Low Power CMOS Wide Band Active Inductor Based PLL at L and S Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique for the Wideband PLL design. High Frequency Wideband PLL is mainly used for the reconfigurable High Frequency carrier and clock signal Synthesis. Here the novel wideband PLL is designed for the wideband high frequency clock Synthesis for Serializer-Deserializer or Frequency synthesizers-based applications using the high-performance wideband active inductor based VCO, designed using 180 nm CMOS process and tested for the frequency band from 200 MHz to 2.5 GHz. Active inductor based PLL gives wide tuning range due to the cancellation of the parasitic capacitances in the circuit. VCO is designed with the active inductor based cross coupled negative resistance topology with two control voltages to control the coarse and fine frequency tuning. A switchable bank of resistors with a current mirror is incorporated for the fixing of the active inductor control voltage for coarse frequency tuning in PLL. Due to wide band operation, PLL can also be used for the L and S band signal generation in Microwave subsystems.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurability using Plasma for Beamsteering Application at S-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: For the UHF range, a circular plasma antenna array with beam shaping is designed using CST. The simulation results are detailed in paper [1]. This paper presents the experimental results of the fabricated plasma antenna array. In this setup, an omnidirectional metal antenna is positioned at the center of a metal ground that includes plasma reflectors. These plasma reflectors create a plasma blanket around the omnidirectional antenna. When the plasma frequency exceeds the antenna’s operational frequency, the plasma functions perfectly as a reflector; however, when the plasma frequency is lower, it becomes transparent. Turning off the fluorescent lights generates a plasma window, allowing the electromagnetic signal to be scanned 360° by sequentially activating and deactivating these plasma tubes. Consequently, the antenna beam can be electronically steered in any direction within the 360° range, eliminating the need for mechanical steering. The experimental S11 of the plasma antenna array measures -23.58 dB at 2.8 GHz and remains below -10 dB within a frequency band spanning from 2.4 GHz to 3.2 GHz. The experimental front-to-back ratio of the array is 6 dB for plasma windowing.

articleTitle: All-metallic Q-Band 8×8 Gap Waveguide Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An all-Metallic Q-Band linearly polarized $8\times 8$ gap waveguide array antenna is presented in this paper. Pin dimensions are chosen so as to create a stop band in our operating frequencies (36-40 GHz). A $2\times 2$ subarray is designed which is composed of a T-shaped feed structure based on RGW (Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology) along with a coupling layer which couples the E-field from the feed to the corresponding upper radiating slots. Finally a $8\times 8$ antenna array is built up by the above elements. The proposed antenna array achieves over 12% impedance bandwidth from 36-406 GHz frequency range with − 10 dB reflection coefficient. Measured Gain for the antenna array is 25.5-26.3 dBi from 36-40 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact Planar Microstrip Patch Antenna in Commercial Ultra-Wideband Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact microstrip patch antenna of size 35mmx30mmx0.8mm is projected here. The radiator looks like Pillow which attained broad aperture and cover wide spectrum from 3 to 14. 26GHz (130.5%). The antenna offers omnidirectional radiation patterns with stable gain variation and high radiation efficiency in the covered spectrum. The antenna is suitable for many ultra-wideband wireless technologies, especially for indoor communication.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin LIG Film for X band EMI Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The development of lightweight and ultrathin materials is quite important for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding of myriads of electrical devices, especially in the telecommunication and the aerospace industry. In this work, a novel ultrathin Laser Induced Graphene (LIG) film with total thickness of only 0.05 mm is synthesized, fabricated and tested for the EMI shielding application. The proposed LIG film, based on the customized conductive material, is fabricated using a pulsed CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser system. It is demonstrated that the fabricated LIG sample exhibits more than 10 dB total shielding effectiveness (SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) in the entire X band. The ratio of SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>/ thickness(mm) for the fabricated LIG film is found to be greater than 200, which is phenomenally high as compared to the state of the art EMI shielding materials. Further, the electrical conductivity of the LIG film is measured and this data is utilized to perform simulation using the numerical EM simulator; the CST Microwave Studio for the SE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> performances. A close matching is observed between the measured and the simulated SE data. The proposed synthesis scheme appears to be quite promising for design and development of lightweight EMI shielding materials, which can have wide range of applications in industry.

articleTitle: Severity of Fall Detection using Digital Twin for Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In long-term care facilities and retirement resi-dences, falls constitute a paramount health challenge for the geriatric demographic. A plurality of technologies have been investigated for use in fall detection. Recently, radar sensors have been proven reliable in detecting falls. However, the problem of detecting the severity of falls has not yet been investigated. Among the major concerns hindering this development is the lack of a representative dataset containing various fall scenarios that can be provided to different machine learning algorithms. Generating this dataset would require having different participants experience various fall scenarios, which would pose a significant risk to their well-being. In this paper, a severity of fall detection algorithm was developed using radar digital-twin generated data. The radar dataset was generated using human kinematic models fed into a full-wave electromagnetic solver. The results indicate an overall 85% accuracy in the detection of fall types. We believe that this is the first of its kind study that demonstrates the ability to use a radar digital twin for the detection and assessment of the severity of falls.

articleTitle: A compact EBG integrated slot antenna for wearable applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact EBG integrated antenna using a semi-flexible substrate RT 5800 is proposed for 2.45 GHz ISM band. The key techniques used for miniaturization is slots, slits and DGS. The overall size of the proposed antenna integrated with 3x3 array of EBG unit cell is 40x40x2.5 mm3. The impedance bandwidth of 100 MHz (2.41-2.51GHz) is obtained when simulated on tissue layer model in CST microwave studio. The realized gain in free space is 3.09 dBi with a radiation efficiency of 78% for the EBG integrated antenna. As compared to literature this work shows a compact EBG structure which is placed at shortest distance of 2 mm from the main antenna making it user comfortable. The proposed compact antenna is suitable for wearable applications as SAR levels comply with the safety limits.

articleTitle: High Gain Series-Fed Gap-Coupled Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact series-fed gap-coupled microstrip line antenna array operating in the millimeter wave range. The main focus is to achieve high gain, making it highly desirable for beamforming 5G applications. The proposed antenna configuration consists a microstrip line with regularly positioned semi-circle stubs at guided wavelength intervals. These stubs stop the cancellation of surface current in an ideal microstrip line making it an efficient radiator. By controlling the gap between the semi-circular stub and microstrip line a peak gain of 13.3dBi is achieved at 28GHz with an impedance bandwidth $(\mathrm{S} 11\lt -10 \mathrm{~dB})$ of 900MHz [27.63-28.53GHz]. The resonance frequency can be tuned by changing the length of microstrip line from the feeding point. The antenna is suitable for 5G integration for Internet of Things (IoT) based applications.

articleTitle: Compact Lightweight Wideband Multi-channel Millimetre-Wave Self-sufficient Down Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of a compact, lightweight, wideband multi-channel, self-sufficient, phased matched millimetre-wave down converter has been discussed in this article. Here single stage down conversion has been use to down convert millimetre wave signals to S band IF signal with the help of Ku band LO signals. Frequency planning is done carefully to avoid in-band unwanted spurs. Low loss sharp rejection narrow band pass filter is used to get excellent image rejection characteristics. Each down converted IF signal is further converted to differential status signals. These status signals are used to control the operation of the down converter itself. Excellent in-band and out of band harmonics/ spur rejection has been targeted over ultra wideband frequencies. 2dB±1.5dB gain variation, >60dB harmonic/spurious rejection (over DC-40GHz) with >56dBc (min) image rejections have been achieved in the developed prototypes over −25°C to +55°C and 3 axis (X-Y-Z) random vibrations to establish the design concept.

Author Keywords: in /out of Band Harmonics/ Spurs and Phase Matching

articleTitle: Reliability Estimation of an Active Array Antenna Element for Space-Borne Synthetic Aperture Radar Using Ground Test Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The active array antenna of a space-borne synthetic aperture radar instrument comprises a large number of trans-receive modules. These are characterized and tested at various stages of realization viz. module level, antenna panel, integrated payload and spacecraft level. During the realization of the system, some failures were observed in the trans-receive modules. After detailed failure investigations, root cause of the failure was identified and corrective actions were implemented after validation. Failures observed in a system always trigger concerns for the long term system reliability. Reliability estimation of space-borne systems is carried out using MILHDBK-217 which is the widely followed standard. However, this approach does not consider the tests carried out and failures observed. Availability of a large volume of characterization test data opens up the opportunity to carry out the reliability estimation using this data. This paper brings out the reliability estimation of trans-receive modules using the data of ground tests conducted at different stages and the failures thereof.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Stub loaded HMSIW Leaky-Wave Antenna for Continuous Scanning through Broadside
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) leaky-wave antenna loaded with asymmetric stubs is proposed to suppress the open stopband (OSB) effect to achieve continuous scanning through broadside. To achieve this, two rectangular portions are etched out from the diagonally opposite corners of the conventional rectangular stub, thereby introducing the desired asymmetry. The HMSIW’s width, periodicity, and stub length are systematically optimized to attain the desired broadside frequency. To verify the simulation results, prototype of the proposed design is fabricated and the antenna parameters are measured. The antenna exhibits efficient broadside radiation with a maximum gain of 14.8 dBi at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: UWB Antipodal Antenna With Half-Elliptical Parasitic Patch Loaded with Cylindrical Dielectric For Microwave Breast Imaging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Antipodal Antenna (AA) featuring leaf-shaped stubs, a half-elliptical parasitic patch, and a cylindrical lens strategically integrated into its design, aimed at enhancing its suitability for microwave breast imaging applications. The initial focus of this development is on crafting and optimizing the performance of the leaf-shaped stubs. Subsequently, in pursuit of heightened high-frequency gain performance, a half-elliptical parasitic structure is introduced both above and below the substrate. To further elevate the antenna’s gain capabilities, a circular cylindrical dielectric lens is seamlessly integrated. The proposed configuration demonstrates a simulated return loss exceeding 10 dB across the frequency range of 1.4 to 16 GHz, with a projected peak gain of 12.4 dBi at 13 GHz. Notably, this innovative device has proven effective in the successful detection of tumors within a planar breast phantom.

articleTitle: Design of Koch Curve-Based Fractal Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a new fractal antenna design for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) applications. The final design topology is attained by a Koch curve fractal-based pentagonal radiator, the partial ground, and a microstrip feedline, to realize a novel fractal antenna with a small footprint, better structural conformability, and wide Impedance Bandwidth (IBW) to operate in the UWB. The band of the antenna design functions at the 3 GHz to 12 GHz band. A 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order Koch curve fractal is employed along the inner edges of the radiator. The proposed antenna is designed using HFSS 2020 software and also printed on a substrate Roger RT/Duroid 5880 having a dielectric constant ($\varepsilon _{\mathbf{r}} =$ 2.2). It shows a peak realized gain of 4.7 dBi at 4.1 GHz covering the operating band. The miniaturized dimension of the proposed design ($30 \times 30 \times 1$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), acceptable values of gain, efficiency, Cross-Polar discrimination (XPD) of 40 dB, and low profile, make the linearly polarized fractal antenna suitable for UWB applications.

articleTitle: Design of Simple Broadband Millimeter-Wave Monopole Antenna using Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line (SICL) Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel monopole antenna fed through a substrate-integrated coaxial line (SICL) is proposed in this paper. It offers advantages such as broad bandwidth (BW), non-dispersive, easy design, and compact size. The antenna is demonstrated for a frequency range of 24.25 to 29.5 GHz, encompassing several millimeter-wave bands (n257, n258, and n261) specified for 5G. The broadband characteristics of the proposed SICL-fed monopole antenna are obtained using a SICL feed and a monopole element implemented over a finite ground plane. The bottom and top metal layers of SICL are employed to implement a ground plane for the monopole element and reflector to direct the radiated fields, respectively. The proposed antenna achieves an impedance BW of 21.5% for the reflection coefficient below -10 dB. Within the operating band, it exhibits stable end-fire radiation patterns with peak realized gains between 4.7 and 5.1 dBi and cross-polarization values below -12 dB.

articleTitle: Solar Cell Integrated Optically Transparent Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of a solar cell integrated, optically transparent 2X2 antenna for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-to-satellite communication. The antenna is designed to operate in the 9-18 GHz frequency band covering 15 GHz UAV satellite communication data link. The antenna has been fabricated using a low-cost in-house method in which the antenna is created from the Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) embodied polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film. The surface resistance of the antenna is 10 $\Omega$ per Square. The antenna was fabricated and measured without the solar cell and when mounted on it. The antenna operates in a 9-18 GHz band covering various communication bands, including UAV-Satellite communication link at 15 GHz. The simulated realized gain of the antenna is 7.52dBi. It is also demonstrated that the antenna does not interfere to the Solar cell charging and discharging process, and it may be mounted on the UAV wings for the smart communication link. The measured electrical characteristics of the antenna will be shown during the conference.

articleTitle: X Band DGS integrated Rectangular Microstrip Antenna over Flexible Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a dumbbell shaped DGS integrated probe fed rectangular microstrip antenna has been designed and developed over a flexible/textile substrate. Around 25 dB co-pol to cross-pol radiation isolation in H plane with no change in co-pol radiation pattern has found. Further, the same structure has been studied in case the substrate is of wavy/bumpy nature. A prototype has also been fabricated to support the proposed conjecture. It reveals effect of substrate on the radiation charateristics of the antenna.

articleTitle: Linearly Polarized Wideband Koch Fractal Antenna for C and X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research article presents a Koch fractal antenna with wideband characteristics. A threefold scaled down 1st order Koch fractal geometry is etched on the central radiator. The proposed antenna operates in the frequency range from 3.6 GHz to 9.5 GHz. The defected ground plane with a rectangular cut is incorporated to further enhance the impedance bandwidth (IBW). The whole geometry is built on a Rogers RT/ Duroid 5880 substrate. The monopole is excited on a line feeding with the best impedance match of $50 \Omega$. The areal compactness of the proposed radiator measures $0.677 \lambda_{0} \times 0.611 \lambda_{0} \times 0.034 \lambda_{0}\left(f_{r}=6.55 \text{GHz}\right)$ and has a −10 dB bandwidth of 90%. The radiator achieves a peak gain measure of 6.8 dBi at 3.7 GHz. Stable radiation characteristics with better X-Pol, covering IBW are observed in this investigation. Hence, the proposed radiator is a fit for C and X-band applications.

articleTitle: A Compact High-Gain Metasurface Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper provides valuable insights into the design, development, and implementation of a 5G metasurface antenna (MSA). The MSA is assembled with a simple microstrip patch antenna that achieves the realized gain of 4.8dBi using substrate of Rogers RT Duroid 5880 (Lossy) at a frequency of 25.9 GHz. The two-layer $4 \times 4$ order metasurface (MS) has enhanced the gain of the antenna to 9.31dBi. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are $0.52 \lambda_{0} \times 0.52 \lambda_{0} \times 0.51 \lambda_{0}$ where $\lambda_{0}$ is the free space wavelength at 25.9GHz. The overall $4 \times 4$ MSA also provides the maximum efficiency of 86 % at 25.9GHz. The proposed antenna's outstanding performance offer a promising avenue for future 5G deployments, catering to the demands of diverse applications in the era of next-generation wireless networks.

articleTitle: Microwave Active Resonator for High Resolution Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A passive interdigitated capacitor (IDC) resonator with active feedback topology is proposed for sensing applications. The BJT BFP760 transistor from Infineon technology is used to design the active circuitry to improve the performance of the passive IDC sensor in terms of its resolution and quality factor. The proposed active sensor resonates at around 3.5 GHz with an improved quality factor of 12000 as compared to that of the passive structure with a quality factor of around 300. The sensing mechanism for the designed active resonator is demonstrated by first simulating the corresponding passive structure in the CST MWS, and then importing its scattering parameters into ADS to facilitate integration with the active circuitry. The designed structure is then fabricated and measured on a 0.8 mm thick Rogers $\left(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=2.2\right)$ substrate. The measured response under the OFF (Passive), and ON (Active) state shows the effectiveness of the employed active design topology. The improvement in the sensor resolution in terms of its sensitivity is about 46.7%, while the Q factor improvement is about 40 times as compared to that of the corresponding passive IDC structure.

articleTitle: Dual-Circularly Polarized Antenna Array for Automotive Radar at 77 GHz based on SISL Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) architecture based compact dual-circularly polarized antenna is presented. The antenna has a wide impedance and polarization bandwidth, covering 76-81 GHz. The antenna array is created using sequentially rotated elements. The proposed 4-layer antenna has low profile among the available literature with a thickness of 0.15λ while the overall size is 20 mm × 10 mm × 0.611 mm. The port isolation is greater than 35 dB while the cross-polar discrimination is less than -22 dB. The axial ratio is less than 2 dB over the entire band. The above antenna has the potential application as polarimetric radar in automotive industry.

articleTitle: Design of Complementary Meander Shaped Resonator for Adulteration Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new compact planar RF sensor design is realized to assess the purity of edible oils. The shape of the sensor structure is designed to realize an improved sensitivity and quality factor. The sensor structure is quite compact as it utilizes the meander shape tropology. The fabricated sensor prototype provides quite a high-quality factor (298) than that of the conventional design of electrically small resonant sensors (128). Also, the obtained absolute sensitivity around resonant frequency (801MHz) is substantially higher than the literature available data (111 MHz). The sensor provides a 275 KHz shift in the resonant frequency for 20% adulteration of commercially available cheap oil. Moreover, it is found that the sensor can produce nearly 65 KHz shift in resonant frequency for a 5% contamination level, which is well above its repeatability limit of 12.5 KHz.

Author Keywords: Meander shaped complementary split ring resonator (CSRR)

articleTitle: Novel Concept of Projected Polyhedron to Generate Quasi-Periodic Array Lattice for SLL Improvement in Beam Steerable Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the new concept of the projected polyhedron to produce quasi-periodic array lattice, which provides an improvement in peak sidelobe level (SLL) during beam scan. Quasi-periodic array lattices generated by projection of vertices of the single dodecahedron and co-centric dodecahedron and icosahedron on aperture plane, have been discussed in detail. 3-axis rotation and scaling of polyhedrons are used to design quasi-periodic array lattices. Recently developed Jaya algorithm has been employed to optimize the farfield performance of array antenna. The rotation angles and scale factors of polyhedrons are used as optimization variables and the objective function is defined to improve peak SLL while maintaining the minimum inter-element spacing. Both types of quasi-periodic array lattice have been modeled, designed and optimized. Array analysis of the same has also been carried out for ± 30° beam scan and analysis results are discussed in detail. 5.0 dB and 4.2 dB improvement in the peak SLL has been achieved for array lattice with single and co-centric polyhedrons respectively. Performance of polyhedron based array lattice has also been compared with Pinwheel type quasi-periodic array lattice, for comparative assessment.

articleTitle: Exploring Pattern and Polarization Diversity: A quintuple port MIMO Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with five ports, designed for WLAN applications with a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) configuration. The antenna setup involves two cylindrical dielectric resonator antennas (cDRAs) placed on opposite sides of an L-shaped substrate. Each cDRA is driven by a pair of microstrip line-fed conformal striplines, oriented orthogonally to ensure excitation of the $HE_{11\delta}$ mode in the respective cDRA. Careful arrangement of the feeding mechanisms induces specific polarizations in the antenna elements, significantly enhancing isolation between the ports. These two cDRAs operate in disparate directions, thereby originating two distinct and spatially uncorrelated radiation patterns. Additionally, the proposed technique introduces another level of complexity by exciting a $TM_{01\delta}$ mode within a ring DRA positioned at the substrate’s corner. This ingenious approach results in the creation of a third radiation beam. The synergistic implementation of these techniques contributes to an impressive isolation of over 16 dB among the ports. Furthermore, the antenna configuration provides a bandwidth of 12.17%, spanning from 5.4 to 6.10 GHz. The presented findings suggest that this novel MIMO antenna design could be favorably deployed in WLAN applications operating around 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Phased Array Radar Antenna Using Low Profile Cavity-Backed Slots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel four-element array of cavity-backed slot antennas, designed to achieve wider bandwidth and low cross-polarization. The subarray is fed by an end launch line, which is expertly coupled to the low-profile cavity, enabling efficient wideband performance in the S-band frequency range. Unit cell of array is with size of $0.4\lambda X0.45\lambda\times 0.5\lambda$ ($\lambda$ is the free space wavelength at the center frequency of operation). This proposed design facilitates reduced spacing between the individual elements in the phased array antenna. By incorporating a dumbbell-shaped slot, we enhance the bandwidth while maintaining a reduced overall size. Compared to the traditional single resonant CBSA, the proposed design significantly improves the impedance bandwidth from 3% to 12%. Additionally, the shifted feeding location allows for the freedom to insert a thermal heat sink at the center position. Furthermore, the all-metal structure of the antenna retains the advantageous feature of zero dielectric loss performance and can be used for high power operation.

articleTitle: Design of Superconducting Coplanar Waveguide Rat-Race and Branch Line coupler for Circuit Quantum Electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a thin-film on-chip superconducting rat-race and quadrature branch-line coupler for circuit quantum electrodynamics. These couplers are designed at a center frequency of 6GHz using coplanar waveguide technology using a thin film of niobium or aluminum on sapphire substrates. The electrical connections are made between the ground using aluminum air bridges. The insertion losses to the through and coupled ports of rat-race and quadrature coupler are 3.1dB. The quadrature and rat-race couplers offer a wide bandwidth of 2GHz and 3GHz, respectively. A spectral shift of around 400MHz is observed in these couplers when operation is shifted from room temperature to the cryogenic regime. The simulated results have been discussed and analyzed.

articleTitle: Investigations on the Performance of Isophoric Linear Sparse Array Antenna with Low Sidelobe Level due to Non-Isotropic Radiators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design of isophoric (equally fed) linear sparse array antennas (LSA) using particle swarm optimizer (PSO). The synthesized LSA is electromagnetically modelled using method of moments (MOM) based commercial em solver using a practical radiator to study effect of practical constraints such as mutual coupling, finite array edges and realistic element pattern on the LSA performance. The investigations into the performance of the LSAs brings out the various design guidelines and their applicability to the various domains.

articleTitle: Design of 30W GaN V/UHF Broadband Power Amplifier using Simulated Load-Pull Contours
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses the design and experimental results for a broadband efficient power amplifier for software defined radios (SDRs). Load-pull contours for the non-linear device model were generated in the band of interest, 30 – 512MHz (17:1 bandwidth). These were used for matching network design which was implemented through ferrite-based coaxial Ruthroff transformers. Experimental results show that the implemented power amplifier (PA) achieved a power output of 44.7 – 46.3dBm with high DC to RF efficiency of 51 – 69%. Modulation performance of the PA was tested using 2Msps MSK waveform yielding low error vector magnitudes (EVM) of <1%.

articleTitle: Design of Low Scattering Strut for Ground Station Antennas to meet ITU Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the strut designs for ground station antenna, to comply the ITU recommendation for off axis radiation pattern. The conventional rectangular and circular cross-sectional struts have been analyzed in 9.2m Cassegrain optics based shaped dual reflector antenna system. The analysis has also been extended for the rectangular strut with reflecting wedge, the most economical alternative for low-scattering struts. The analyzed secondary performances are evaluated and post-processed to compute the percentage violation of recommendation ITU-R S.580-6 over the angular range for each strut type. The optimization of the wedge angle of the reflecting wedge is carried out to minimize the percentage violation. The presented results reveal that strut incorporating a 45-degree reflecting wedge not only meets the ITU-R Recommendation but also significantly reduces the violation from 32% to as low as 3% as compared to conventional rectangular struts

articleTitle: Development of Gallium Nitride Based S-band 220W Solid State Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The work presents development activities of Gallium Nitride based S-band (2.5GHz) 220W Solid State Power Amplifier (SSPA) for geostationary communication payloads. The developed Continuous Wave (CW) SSPA provides a viable alternative to Travelling Wave Tube Amplifiers at S-band in terms of competitive size, weight and power consumption for SATCOM payload. The developed SSPA is powered using an Electronic Power Conditioner (EPC) and it delivers 220W output power in CW operation with 45% efficiency and meets the linearity goals of -18dBc IMD and 15dB NPR at 1.6dB OBO. The paper also provides an assessment of over temperature performance of the SSPA over -10 to $65^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in vacuum environment.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Reconfigurable Hybrid Fractal Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The article proposes a novel frequency-reconfigurable hybrid fractal antenna that comprises hybrid fractal geometry (combining Koch and self-affine fractals) integrating with two PIN diodes. The overall size of the antenna is $68 \times 31 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ placed on a FR4 substrate material. It can work in wideband, i.e., L - and S-band, by altering the states of two switches. A partial ground plane is used to achieve a wideband and good radiation performance in the antenna. It has two operational bands. These bands are case I, 1.69-3.62 GHz with 72.7% impedance bandwidth when all diodes are OFF; and case II, 1.48-3.18 GHz with 73% impedance bandwidth when all diodes are ON. As a result, the designed antenna’s impedance bandwidth offers continuous wideband frequency covering from 1.48 GHz to 3.62 GHz(84 %). The peak realized gain of 2.5 dBi has been attained at 3 GHz in the S-band. The radiating element has stable radiation properties and a Cross-polar Discrimination (XPD) greater than 30 dB, making it appropriate for wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Angle-dependent switching of bands in metamaterial absorber at near infrared frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We present numerical studies on an angle-dependent bands switchable metamaterial absorber working at near-infrared frequencies. The absorber is made up of one-dimensional silicon strips array on a silicon substrate followed by a $30 \mathrm{~nm}$ gold layer. Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio has been used for simulations and to understand the underlying mechanics of absorption in the system. The absorption is induced by the simultaneous excitation of double Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity resonance in the system. One is in the strips and the other in between the consecutive strips. At normal incidence, the absorber shows only one absorption band with 0.99 absorptance at wavelength $1.491 \mu \mathrm{m}$. But for oblique incidence, there is an appearance of an extra absorption band beyond the 3° angle of incidence, and it reaches 0.99 absorptance for 10° angle of incidence. Therefore, the absorption band can be switched from single to dual and vice versa with the chance in the angle of incidence. So, this absorber can be exploited as a single-band absorber or dual-band absorber as per requirement.

Author Keywords: Dual-band absorber and Fabry Perot resonance

articleTitle: A Novel Serpentine Online Calibration Network for Printed Dipole Phased Array Antenna at Ku-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel serpentine-shaped online calibration network for printed dipole Active Electrically Scanned Array (AESA) antenna at Ku-band. When AESA antennas are deployed in the field, online calibration network is essential to correct imbalances in amplitude and phase excitations of antenna elements without bringing the array back to test range. A passive serpentine-shaped microstrip network is designed to couple power from calibration network to all antenna elements uniformly. One serpentine line couples power from the cal line to nearby two linear arrays of printed dipoles. All cal lines are combined onto a single port to excite the network with a common source. Simulation results show coupling amplitudes from calibration network to antenna elements are about $- 40 \pm 5$ dB. Calibration network has been realized and coupling amplitudes are measured from calibration network to all antenna elements. Measured results show a good correlation with the simulation results. Design of a serpentine-shaped passive online calibration network to couple power strongly and uniformly onto all printed dipole elements is a novel contribution of this work.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Wide Beamwidth Microstrip Antenna Backed by Choke Ring for S-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design methodology, fabrication and measurement results of a dual circularly polarized, wide beamwidth antenna operating in S-band are presented in this paper. The antenna comprises of a microstrip patch assembly placed on top of a metallic choke ring. The microstrip assembly consists of two substrates stacked to each other. A dual probe fed circular patch and parasitic crossed dipoles are printed on one substrate, while a 90° hybrid coupler connecting the two feeds is printed on other substrate. The antenna exhibits a 17 dB return loss bandwidth of more than 8%. This design has a stable phase centre and exhibits realized gain greater than 0 dBi with axial ratio less than 3 dB for low elevation angles (± 25°) for both polarizations. Results of RF characterization and farfield measurements of the antenna have been included, which are observed to be in close agreement to the simulated results.

articleTitle: Compact Cylindrical X-band Luneburg Lens Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Luneburg lens antenna is one of the promising candidates for beam scanning applications. However, the bulky size of the conventional Luneburg lens makes it less practical for wireless communication systems, especially at lower frequencies. This manuscript proposes a compact cylindrical Luneburg lens antenna with a diameter of 95.9 mm (3.2 wavelengths at a central frequency of 10 GHz) which can be used instead of a spherical Luneburg lens. The proposed lens is designed by placing concentric hollow cylinders with optimized thickness and permittivity values without any air gaps with a rectangular waveguide as a feed. Simulated results show that the designed cylindrical Luneburg lens antenna can operate over the X-band with a peak gain between 15-18.5 dBi.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Dual Band Integratable Antenna for Sub-6GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost antenna with dual band characteristics has been presented. For the first band, the proposed antenna fully covers 2.45 GHz, Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) and Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band covering 2.4 – 2.5 GHz band with impedance bandwidth better than -14dB. For the second band, it offers impedance bandwidth w.r.t. better than -14dB for public safety applications. Moreover, the second band also covers 4.8-5.2 GHz band w.r.t. - 10dB impedance bandwidth. It is designed using FR-4 low-cost substrate with thickness of 0.8mm. Moreover, it exhibits good radiation characteristics in terms of radiation patterns and gain. The shape and compactness of antenna allow its easy integration to sub-6GHz devices and IoT applications.

articleTitle: Inkjet Printed Wideband Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, a reconfigurable wideband antenna with inkjet printing is created using a low-cost resin coated commercial photo paper substrate. A PIN diode is primarily utilized to disperse the surface current, which gives the proposed antenna reconfigurable features in the lower frequency region. The antenna’s dimensions are 28. 94mmx36.36mmx0.44mm, and it has a partial ground that covers the mobile and wireless bands from 3. 32GHz to 7. 73GHz. For the antenna’s design parameter to be optimized, parametric analysis is done. The primary radiator is intended to operate at a frequency range of 4-7. 7GHz, while the L-shaped radiators are intended to work between 3. 3-3.9GHz. Peak gain and radiation efficiency for the suggested antenna were 3. 45dBi and 65%, respectively. Reflection coefficient, gain, and efficiency simulation and measurement findings indicate that the antenna design is in good agreement. This method eliminates the requirement for several electronic parts to provide multiband frequency.

articleTitle: Printed Angled Dipole Linear Array Antenna with 1:32 Un-Equal Power Combiner for X-Band Phased Array Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 32-element printed Angled dipole array antenna with unequal power division feed network for X-band phased array application presented. A printed angled dipole antenna (PADA) as a radiating element designed with a modified parasitic cap in front of the dipole aperture to control the beam width over the operating frequency range. The 32-element array is designed along with a 1:32-way power divider. The power divider employed corporate feed with an un-equal power division based on Taylor distribution to achieve 30dB side lobe level. The proposed linear array antenna achieved a peak gain of 19dB. The Antenna Array simulated using Ansys High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS), a Finite Element Method (FEM) solver. Stripline to microstrip transition incorporated at the Power divider input port for easy fabrication. The proposed model is validated through measurements.

articleTitle: A Miniature Selective Bandpass Filter With Frequency-Variant Couplings Realized Using Uniform-Impedance Quarter-Wave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, electromagnetic coupling characteristics of uniform-impedance folded quarter-wave resonators are explored for their application in high-performance inline bandpass filters. The folded quarter-wave resonators enable realization of two-types of frequency-variant couplings. Transmission zeros generated due to these couplings enhance the filter’s selectivity, improve out-of-band rejection level and also suppress a few of the harmonic passbands. These multiple merits, achieved by a simple fold, are demonstrated through the design of a fourth-order filter centered at 0.313 GHz with 11.86% fractional bandwidth. The fabricated prototype shows selectivity factor, defined as the ratio of 3-dB to 20-dB bandwidths, of 0.62 and roll-off rates of 1256 dB/GHz and 1156 dB/GHz at the upper and lower sides of the passband, respectively. Auxiliary open stubs are added to aid filter’s inherent harmonic suppression capabilities such that a stopband up to 10.2 times the center frequency is achieved with minimum rejection level of 20 dB. Moreover, the folds allow a miniature filter footprint of 0.048 by 0.129 times the wavelength at the center frequency.

articleTitle: U-Net With Dilated Convolution for Improved Clutter Removal in GPR Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The clutters are inherent in ground penetrating radar (GPR) investigations which severely affects the performance of subsurface target detection. Therefore, removal of clutter is an essential preprocessing step in GPR survey. Several approaches are existing in literature for this purpose. However, it is quite challenging to remove the clutters for a rough ground surface using conventional methods. In this paper, a dilated convolution based U-Net architecture is proposed to improve the clutter removal performance of GPR B-scan images. The effectiveness of proposed approach over standard U-Net is validated on synthetic as well as laboratory measured data through qualitative and quantitative evaluation.

articleTitle: Signal integrity aspect of High Speed Interface Routing in multilayered PCB environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The strategy of selecting the routing layer to attain better signal quality of high-speed channel interfaces is presented. The effective capacitance and inductance associated with the overall trace will get modified especially depending on uses of transition. Moreover, most of the HSIO interfaces routing possess upper limit on the number of transitions vias without stressing on the selection of trace routing layer and its connection with transition via. However, the analysis carried out shows that the optimized trace routing layer assignment helps to mitigate the effective via parasitic that helps to attain better channel loss margin. Therefore, a systematic numerical analysis is presented to develop the more useful consideration regarding the routing of HSIO interface (USB4 @10Gbps) corresponding to multilayer PCB. A commercially available 3D field solver is used to analyze the frequency domain channel response corresponding to USB4 interface. The time domain analysis is also carried out to compare the parameter of eye diagram. It is shown that routing of HSIO in appropriate signal layers helps to provide better margin. For the USB4 interface, an improvement of $3.6 \mathrm{~dB}$ in insertion loss and 49mV improvement in eye height is recorded that helps to meet the Retimer specification.

articleTitle: Transparent Metamaterial Absorber Fabrication by Pulsed-DC Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Metamaterials are artificially engineered structures with unprecedented control over electromagnetic waves and their properties. They have wide range of electrical and optical applications like absorbers, camouflage, sensors and antennas. In this communication an alternative technique of transparent metamaterial fabrication is proposed. Indium tin oxide (ITO) is sputtered on acrylic substrate for the desired duration through a shadow mask to get the desired pattern. Measurement of the absorber indicates strong correlation between simulated and measured results. The challenges associated with fabrication technique has been discussed in detail. The proposed technique is a good alternative to traditional laser micromachining of ITO-PET. Using this technique custom made sheet resistance can be achieved while designing unit cell which provides another degree of freedom.

articleTitle: Design of CPW Fed 4 × 4 MIMO Antenna for UWB Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a $4 \times 4$ MIMO antenna fed by CPW for UWB applications is demonstrated. A substrate composed of FR-4 is utilized in the design of this antenna. The UVB functionality of the antenna is made feasible by truncating the upper and bottom edges of the radiating patch. The modified step-like pattern has been carved into the lower part of the rectangular patch. The size of the antenna is $80 \times 80 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ having large bandwidth (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> <−10dB), extending from 2.29GHz to 10.9GHz. The antenna elements have been arranged in an orthogonal manner to increase the isolation without any additional decoupling structure. All four patches have mutual coupling which is below −15dB. The suggested antenna is capable of achieving the highest gain of 5.9dBi. MIMO antennas have a variety of performance parameters to consider. It has an Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) and a Diversity gain (DG) that is lower than 0.01 and greater than 9.95dB, respectively. The design that has been planned is a suitable aspirant for UWB wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Wideband Conformal AVA on a Dielectric Cylinder for Airborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a wideband conformal antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) mounted on a dielectric cylinder for airborne applications in the S, C, and X bands (2-12 GHz). The planar design incorporates an exponential flare, rectangular slits (RS) for impedance matching at lower frequencies, and a parasitic elliptical patch (EP) for gain enhancement. The antenna is simulated on a Rogers substrate (RO4350B) with a dielectric constant of 3.5 and dimensions of $116 \times 124 \times 0.508$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Simulation results show excellent performance in terms of reflection coefficient, gain, and radiation pattern for both the planar and conformal antenna. Comparative analysis with existing literature demonstrates superior impedance matching, gain, and radiation pattern performance. The proposed antenna’s conformal nature and wideband capabilities make it suitable for airborne and defence applications.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Antipodal Vivaldi SIW Filtenna at K band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The research paper presents an innovative antipodal substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filtenna. The approach involves arranging U-shaped slot resonators in a linear cascade to establish two pass bands and one stop band. The antenna is seamlessly incorporated on the same plane as a cascaded band-pass filter, resulting in a dual-band filtenna that resonates at 25.72 GHz and 28.38 GHz. These frequency bands lie in the K band (18-27) GHz and Ka band (27-40) GHz frequency range. The miniaturized antipodal filtenna dimensions are 6.3 mm $\times$ 26.1 mm $\times$ 1.58 mm. Better impedance matching of −26.8 dB and −20.72 dB is achieved at each band. A high fractional bandwidth of 2.76% (700MHz) and 1.97% (580MHz) is obtained at lower and higher resonant frequency band. The introduced antenna design attains a reconfigurable radiation pattern. In the first band, the filtenna exhibits ideal end-fire radiation, achieving a peak gain of 5.9 dBi. In the second band, it shifts from broadside to end-fire direction, showcasing a peak gain of 6.2 dBi. The frequency bands of 26 GHz and 28 GHz fall within the 5G spectrum range, making the proposed antenna design well-suited for applications in mobile communication, satellite communication, and radar systems.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Cavity-backed Conformal Antenna with Wide Sectoral Coverage and Low Cross Polarization for High Power X-band Airborne Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript reports the development of a circularly polarized (CP) cavity-backed conformal antenna with wide sectoral coverage. The proposed antenna has a single rectangular cavity which is fed by a slot at an angle of 45 degree to excite two orthogonal resonant modes. The cross slot is used to generate the orthogonal modes. By conceiving two narrow slots symmetrically on either side of the cross slot, circular polarization is excited. The antenna generates Left-Hand Circular Polarization (LHCP) with half-power beamwidths of $120^{\circ} \mathrm{x} 62^{\circ}$ and a gain of about 5.8 dBiC. It features cross polar discrimination (XPD) higher than 21 dB at the boresight and a power handling capability of 200 W. The power handling capability is primarily decided by the SMA connector used at the antenna input. To protect the antenna from the environment 4.3mm Rexolite is used as a Radome, which is flash mounted to the conformal surface.

articleTitle: Scanning Radar for Hazard Detection during Landing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Accurate and soft touchdown at a predetermined location necessitates the utilization of precise ground-based navigation sensors tailored for such destinations. Instruments like altimeters, velocimeters, and inertial navigation systems continually provide the status of the lander’s position. These sensors play a pivotal role in guiding the lander to the intended landing site. Furthermore, an essential element in achieving a soft landing is a terrain related hazard detection sensor during the final phase of descent. This sensor is crucial for ascertaining the safe grid location where the lander’s legs can be positioned securely, preventing toppling and enabling the successful deployment of rover. A comprehensive design for such a hazard-detecting radar system has been conceived, and its performance has been simulated and summarized in the research paper. The findings demonstrate that a G-band radar imager delivers exceptional resolution of less than 0.5 degrees across a field of view spanning 28 degrees. These outcomes identified the necessary technology for developing such radar systems.

articleTitle: Novel Innovative Schemes for Remote Update of Software and Firmware for Digital and RF LRUs in Large Aperature Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Any long range radar requires the use of a very large active aperture array antenna with thousands of Transmit Receive Modules(TRMs). The command and control distribution to these RF LRUs are distributed through digital LRUs arranged in multiple levels of hierarchy in a series-parallel fashion. There is a need to periodically update the software and firmware in the processor and FPGA respectively in Digital and RF LRUs till the time system functionality is successfully proven. For a large aperture array whenever any software or firmware update is required, automatic update through remote programming is the only viable option. In this paper, we highlight such an important and complex scenario where the software of digital LRUs are updated through remote programming and then subsequently the firmware for the FPGAs are updated with the help of the processor. Moreover, for programming the RF LRUs, a comparative analysis between In-Application Programing (IAP) and In-System Programming (ISP) is also presented. The programming scheme is designed to accomplish remote update in a matter of few minutes even if thousands of LRUs need remote update of firmware. These innovative programming techniques have been successfully implemented, tested and proven.

articleTitle: Time domain enhancement of tab-routed microstrip line with EMC validation for DDR4 memory design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
