abstract: One of the key challenge routings for command/address and chips select lines of DDR4 interface as microstrip line on Form factor board like SBC (Single board computer) is likely possible due to its lossy behavior over crosstalk and emission behavior. In this paper, tab routing topology is applied to conventional microstrip design. Time domain behavior like eye height (EH) and eye width (EW) and radiated emission likely near-field is investigated. There is 1.22% and 23.89% improvement on EW and EH respectively, achieved over conventional design at 3200 Mbps speed. At the same time, electric field confinement is observed which reduces emission in terms of electric field intensity over a conventional design..

articleTitle: Dual Channel Diplexer based on Stepped Impedance Filter and Microstrip Open-Loop Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-channel, wide-band diplexer design using coupled stepped impedance resonators (SIRs) for lower frequency (0-3.3 GHz) and open-loop resonators for upper-frequency channels (3.3-4.5 GHz). The impedance length ratio of SIRs is tuned to the desired resonant frequency. A cross-shaped open loop square ring resonator is used for the upper-frequency channel. The insertion losses in the pass bands are less than 3 dB. The two operating channels have measured better than 26 dB of isolation.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual Polarized Antenna for Mobile Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wideband dual polarized base station antenna is suggested in this paper. The complete antenna is modeled in metal to withstand all environmental hazards. It consists of an air coupled balun feeding and a T-matched dipole. A dual orthogonal polarized antenna arrangement is easily supported by this antenna structure, which qualifies it for base-station applications. The antenna input impedance is 100 Ohm, making it easily converted into a two-element array by adding a power divider. The antenna is created using the custom 3D shapes available in the Antenna Toolbox™ from MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>. The antenna operates from 1.6 GHz to 3 GHz, with a VSWR $\lt2$ and isolation between the two ports that is below -16 dB. The antenna gain is 7 dBi over the band. The half power beam width (HPBW) of the antenna is 74°. The antenna can also be fabricated using 3D printing technology.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Three Way Equal Power Divider With Multiple Harmonics Suppression
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a modified two-stage three-way Wilkinson-type equal power divider design with cascaded Lshaped defected microstrip structures loaded in the quarter wave length transmission line sections achieving both miniaturization and harmonic rejection. A design has been fabricated at 1GHz for validation which shows 25 percent miniaturization and more than 18dB rejection of 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th harmonics along with good operational bandwidth and isolation.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Circularly Polarized Square Ring-Shaped Slot Radiator for Active Integrated Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a right-handed circularly polarized square ring-shaped slot radiator and a multi-layer transition designed for Ka-band (19.7GHz-20.2GHz). The 12-layer stack of printed circuit board (PCB) is configured as per the manufacturing requirements. The design of square ring-shaped slot radiator and a low loss transition from co-planner waveguide (CPW) to stripline is carried out using the 12-layer PCB stack and the details are presented in the paper. To generate the circular polarization, the proposed square slot antenna is fed by a 1:2 stripline-based power divider whose outputs are in the quadrature phase. The radiating element is also embedded with vias fencing to achieve minimal cross-coupling in the array environment. The slot radiator, feed network, and transition are analyzed using a 3D electromagnetic solver. The $2.5 \%$ return loss bandwidth for $\geq 15 \text{dB}$ level and $\leq 3.5 \text{dB}$ axial ratio is achieved over the operating band. The slot radiator is also fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Design of Doherty Amplifier for Efficiency Enhancement of 5G gNB Using GaN Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The recent trends in communication systems make use of modulation schemes like 256-QAM which offer excellent spectral efficiency but also exhibit from high Peak-to Average-Power-Ratio (PAPR). This makes it difficult to sustain the power amplifier’s efficiency at output back-off (BO). This paper proposes a Doherty power amplifier implemented using Qorvo GaN on SiC HEMT, which works in the n257 band, and its design methodology has been presented. An asymmetrical architecture has been opted as it offers better efficiency. A two-stage cascaded structure has been implemented along with harmonic suppression to improve the gain as well as efficiency performance. The design has also been simulated on an Arlon DiClad 880 substrate using grounded CPW lines. The asymmetrical DPA achieves a peak gain of 14 dB at 28 GHz, with PAE of 28 % at saturation and 21.6% at 6-dB BO. The maximum power delivered by the power amplifier is about 39.86 dBm.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Polarization-Insensitive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have assumed an important role in the development of the backbone of new communication standards. Their ability to dynamically cause a change in the propagation characteristics of the incoming signal, coupled with their small size and inexpensive nature, has led to their accelerated adoption across the new-age network infrastructure for purposes such as establishing a secure link between the source and the receiver, dynamic switching to the least path-loss transmission path, and so on. The key concerns in designing an RIS that caters to the different applications are polarization-insensitivity and angular stability with respect to the transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarized signals. In this work, a miniaturized RIS design is presented for phase switching which is not only polarization-insensitive, but also achieves angular stability for both TE and TM polarized signals. A wide phase switching is obtained (−160° to +160°) by using varactor diodes, as well as high angular stability is achieved up to 50° with an operating frequency centered at 3.5 GHz. The full wave simulation results are presented and corroborated with the equivalent circuit model (ECM) response. It is hoped that this design would lead to the development of more robust and practical RIS structures for beam-steering applications.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Antenna for Satellite Communication with Underwater Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of dual band circularly polarized antenna for S-band communication. The antenna is fed by center-fed technique and has two patches corresponding to two frequencies namely the radiation patch and auxiliary patch making it a compact design. The radiation patch operates at lower frequency band 2.2 GHz to 2.3 GHz and the auxiliary patch operates at the high frequency band 2.7 GHz to 2.8 GHz. The antenna is designed to reduce the sidelobes by using horizontal and vertical choke rings. The simulated result shows that the return loss is better than 10 dB. Surface current plots present dual circular operation at two different bands. The developed low cost compact antenna finds application in satellite communications especially for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles.

articleTitle: Patch Array Antenna Fed Using Ridge Gap Waveguide Power Divider for SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation, development and measurement of single linear polarized patch array antenna fed using ridge based gap waveguide feeding network. The designed antenna covers the frequency range of 28GHz-30GHz. The simulated efficiency of the antenna is better than 90% with a simulated gain of 22.72dBi. Measured performance of the antenna has been presented and discussed. The presented antenna can be used for SATCOM applications at Ka band.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion Metasurface for X-band and Ku-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact reflective dual-band linear-to-circular polarization (LP-CP) converter is presented in this paper. The unit cell comprises a modified structure of L-shaped patch and three parallel dipoles for dual-band operation. It achieves a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) from 8.09 to 10.59 GHz (26.7%) at lower band and 17.53 to 18.63 GHz (6.08%) at upper bands respectively for y-polarized incidence. Linear polarization to right-hand circular polarization conversion can be achieved with the proposed design. Moreover, axial ratio remains below 1.28 dB between frequencies 8.28 to 10.18 GHz and 17.69 to 18.52 GHz indicating high efficiency of CP conversion. This structure can be employed to generate a circularly polarized system for X-band and Ku-band satellite communication.

articleTitle: Substrate Engineering for Tuning the Absorption Response of Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this manuscript, the idea of substrate engineering is proposed and studied. The study is performed over a resistive patch printed on top of various 3D printable substrates. Two 3D printable fibers are used for the purpose: one is polylactic acid (PLA) and the other is conductive acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (CABS). The substrate design and composition are optimized for lowering overall thickness improving bandwidth, and quality factor. At last, a unit cel design is proposed for X-band absorption. More than 90% absorption is achieved up to 45° for both TE and TN polarization. The unit cell has 4-fold symmetry and is mounted on top of a honeycomb substrate made up of a composition of PLA and CABS fiber having 50% mixing by volume.

articleTitle: Real-Time Structural Surface Cracks Monitoring Using SRSR-Based Microwave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A slotted rectangular spiral resonator (SRSR) based array sensor is presented for real time metallic structure surface cracks monitoring on carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) or metallic structures. The SRSR-based unit sensor utilizes a fringing field sensing capacitor (FFSC) and transforms into an array by arranging cascaded sensor elements, enabling the detection cracks. The sensor array comprises 10 uniform rectangular spiral resonators connected to a 50 mm-long transmission line with a $50 \Omega$ characteristic impedance. The sensor operates either as a band-stop or band-pass filter, depending on the presence or absence of cracks in structure. The sensor functions within the frequency range of 5 to 6.5 GHz and has the capability to detect cracks with dimensions as small as 2.5 mm in terms of width, length, or height having any orientation. The sensor arrangement detailed in this study presents a compact and affordable remedy that could function as a technique for real-time detection of cracks in structures like bridges, oil or gas pipelines, and more.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Wideband Planar Antenna Design for FOPEN Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a compact antenna operating in the L-band for foliage penetration (FOPEN) radar applications. The antenna structure is built using a planar technology having two dielectric layers and three metallic layers. Further, it consists of a modified near-field resonant parasitic (MNFRP) mesh structure on the top layer, an MNFRP composite Egyptian axe dipole (CEAD) placed in the middle layer, and an L-shaped dipole as a feeding element in the bottom layer. In addition, the two substrates: Roger 4003C and Roger 4350B, are sandwiched between the three metallic layers. Thereafter, the L-shaped dipole is excited separately with the MNFRP CEAD and MNFRP Mesh structure to provide resonance at two different frequencies (1.3 GHz and 1.8 GHz) in the upper portion of the L-band. Besides that, the overlapping nature of the proposed antenna structure yields enhanced bandwidth. The overall dimension of the antenna is approximately $0.41 \lambda$ $\mathrm{X} 0.41 \lambda \times 0.0038 \lambda$. The simulation results reveal that the proposed antenna structure produces a 550 MHz impedance bandwidth(−10dB) with 2.13 dBi gain and achieved the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of 1.12. The simulations are carried out using the computer simulation tool (CST) microwave studio suite.
